Source: docs/guide/user/hierarchies.md

# Type, Method and Call Hierarchy

PHPStorm's three hierarchies, with the same shortcuts, toolbar and wording. Put the caret on a
class, a method or a function and press the shortcut; the result opens in the **Hierarchy**
tool window on the right (one tab per run; a new run of the same symbol replaces its tab).

| Action | Windows / Linux | macOS | Menu |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Type Hierarchy | `Ctrl+H` | `Ctrl+H` | Navigate \| Type Hierarchy |
| Method Hierarchy | `Ctrl+Shift+H` | `Cmd+Shift+H` | Navigate \| Method Hierarchy |
| Call Hierarchy | `Ctrl+Alt+H` | `Ctrl+Alt+H` | Navigate \| Call Hierarchy |
| Hierarchy tool window | — | — | View \| Tool Windows \| Hierarchy |

All of them can be rebound in Settings | Keymap (action ids `TypeHierarchy`,
`MethodHierarchy`, `CallHierarchy`, `ActivateHierarchyToolWindow`).

## Type Hierarchy

![Subtypes of an interface](docs/screenshots/hierarchy-type.png)

Opens for the class, interface, trait or enum at the caret (a name in the code, or the class
the caret is in). The toolbar switches between PHPStorm's three views:

- **Class Hierarchy**: the chain of parent classes down to the class, then everything that
  extends it. For an interface or trait this is the list of its subtypes.
- **Supertypes Hierarchy**: the class at the top, its parent class, interfaces and traits
  below it, recursively.
- **Subtypes Hierarchy**: every class extending or implementing it, and every class using a
  trait.

The class the hierarchy was opened for is shown in bold. Icons tell classes, abstract
classes, interfaces, traits and enums apart.

## Method Hierarchy

![Method Hierarchy with its legend](docs/screenshots/hierarchy-method.png)

Opens for the method at the caret (its declaration, a call that Forge can resolve, or the
method the caret is in). The tree shows the classes below the topmost declaration of the
method, each with PHPStorm's mark:

| Mark | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| ✓ (green) | Method is defined in the class |
| ✓ (blue) | Method is declared abstract in the class, or in an interface |
| ! (red) | Method should be defined since the class is not abstract |
| − | Method is not defined in the class but defined in a superclass (or a used trait) |

**Hide Classes Where Method Is Not Implemented** (the filter button) leaves only the classes
that define the method, and the classes on the way to them. Method Hierarchy is available for
PHP files.

## Call Hierarchy

![Callers of a method with the call sites](docs/screenshots/hierarchy-call.png)

Opens for the method or function at the caret and shows its callers. **Caller Methods
Hierarchy** and **Callee Methods Hierarchy** switch between the functions that call it and
the functions it calls. Each level is loaded when you expand a node, so large call graphs stay
fast; a function that calls itself further up is marked and not expanded again. Calls from
outside any function (a route file, a script) show the file.

The list below the tree shows the call sites of the selected node, with the line number and
the source line; click one to open it. Several calls from the same method are one node with
"(2 usages)".

![Callees in the light theme](docs/screenshots/hierarchy-call-light.png)

## Toolbar

| Button | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Sort Alphabetically | Sorts every level by name; otherwise the order is the sources' (superclass before interfaces, files in project order) |
| Scope: All / Production / Test / This Class | **Production** hides test code and library code, **Test** shows only test code (`tests/`, `__tests__/`, `*Test.php`, `*.spec.ts`), **This Class** only the class itself (Type and Method Hierarchy) or the calls inside its class (Call Hierarchy). Parents of a match stay visible so the tree keeps its shape |
| Expand All / Collapse All | Expands or collapses the tree (Call Hierarchy: only the levels already loaded) |
| Autoscroll to Source | Opens the selected node in the editor while you move through the tree |
| Refresh | Computes the hierarchy again for the same place, keeping the view options |

![Scope menu](docs/screenshots/hierarchy-type-scope.png)

In the tree, `Up` / `Down` select, `Right` / `Left` expand and collapse, `Enter` or `F4` and a
double click open the declaration.

## Where the data comes from

- **Language servers** first: their `typeHierarchy` and `callHierarchy` requests (for example
  the TypeScript server for JavaScript and TypeScript, Intelephense Premium for PHP).
- **Forge's PHP index** for PHP files: classes, interfaces, traits and enums of the project
  with their parents (vendor classes are resolved through Composer's PSR-4 autoloading when
  vendor packages are indexed as libraries), method declarations and calls. It works without
  any language server and fills in what a server leaves out (traits, abstract classes). When
  both answer, the results are merged.

Remote projects work the same way: the PHP index runs on the remote host next to the files.


---

Source: docs/guide/user/go-to-test.md

# Go to Test and Create Test

**Navigate | Test** (`Ctrl+Shift+T`, macOS `Cmd+Shift+T`, action id `GotoTest`) jumps between
a class, component or module and its tests, like PHPStorm:

- From a class or module it goes to its tests; from a test it goes to the tested class or
  module (**Test Subject**).
- One result opens directly.
- Several results open the chooser **Choose Test for Order (2 found)**, best match first: the
  test whose folders mirror the class's (`app/Models/Order.php` →
  `tests/Unit/Models/OrderTest.php`) comes before `tests/Feature/OrderTest.php`.
- Without a test the chooser **Choose Test for Order** only offers **Create New Test...**,
  which is also the first row whenever tests exist.

![Choose Test for a class without tests](docs/screenshots/go-to-test-chooser.png)

| From | To |
| --- | --- |
| PHP class `Order.php` | `OrderTest.php` (PHPUnit or Pest), anywhere in the project |
| PHP test `OrderTest.php` | `Order.php` outside the test folders |
| `Button.vue`, `format.ts`, `api.js`, … | `Button.spec.ts`, `format.test.ts`, `__tests__/api.test.js`, `tests/…/format.test.ts` |
| JS/TS test | the module or component with the same name |

Tests are found in Rust next to the project's files, so remote projects are searched on their
host.

## Create New Test

**Create New Test...** opens **Create New PHP Test** for PHP classes and **Create New Test**
for JavaScript, TypeScript, Vue and Svelte files. All fields start with the values PHPStorm
would suggest and can be changed:

![Create New PHP Test dialog](docs/screenshots/create-php-test-dialog.png)

| Field | PHP | JavaScript / TypeScript |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Test framework | PHPUnit; Pest first when composer.json requires `pestphp/pest` or `tests/Pest.php` exists | Vitest or Jest from package.json (`vitest`, `jest`) or `vitest.config.*` / `jest.config.*` |
| Class / Module to test | the class's fully qualified name | the file |
| Test class name | `<Class>Test` (PHPUnit) | — |
| Namespace | from composer.json's `autoload-dev` PSR-4 rules; typing a namespace moves the directory along | — |
| Superclass | the project's `Tests\TestCase` when it exists, Symfony's `WebTestCase` for controllers, otherwise `PHPUnit\Framework\TestCase`; the list offers the others | — |
| File name | `<Class>Test.php` (follows the class name until edited) | `<name>.test.ts` or `<name>.spec.ts` like the project's existing tests |
| Directory | see below | next to the subject, in `__tests__` or in `tests/`, like the project's existing tests |
| Generate | `setUp()` / `tearDown()` (Pest: `beforeEach()` / `afterEach()`) | `beforeEach()` / `afterEach()` |
| Generate test methods for | the class's public methods (no magic methods) → `testShip()`, Pest `test('ship')` | the module's exports → `it("format")` |

Where PHP tests go:

| Project | Class | Test |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Laravel (`tests/Unit`, `tests/Feature`) | `app/Models/Order.php` | `tests/Unit/Models/OrderTest.php`, namespace `Tests\Unit\Models` |
| Laravel | `app/Http/Controllers/OrderController.php` (also `Livewire`, `Console`) | `tests/Feature/Http/Controllers/OrderControllerTest.php`, superclass `Tests\TestCase` |
| Symfony (`App\Tests\` → `tests/`) | `src/Service/Mailer.php` | `tests/Service/MailerTest.php`, namespace `App\Tests\Service` |
| Without `autoload-dev` | `src/Billing/Invoice.php` | `tests/Billing/InvoiceTest.php`, namespace `Tests\Billing` |

Laravel's Unit tests extend `PHPUnit\Framework\TestCase` like the skeleton's, unless the
project's Unit tests already use `Tests\TestCase`.

**OK** creates the file (never replacing an existing one), opens it with the caret in the
first test, and shows it in the Project tool window. The new test gets its green run icons in
the gutter like every other test.

![The created test with run icons](docs/screenshots/create-php-test-created.png)

The JavaScript / TypeScript dialog:

![Create New Test dialog for a TypeScript module](docs/screenshots/create-js-test-dialog.png)

A generated PHPUnit test:

```php
<?php

namespace Tests\Unit\Models;

use PHPUnit\Framework\TestCase;

class OrderTest extends TestCase
{
    protected function setUp(): void
    {
        parent::setUp();
    }

    public function testShip(): void
    {

    }
}
```

A Vitest test imports the selected exports from the subject:

```ts
import { describe, expect, it } from "vitest";
import { format } from "./format";

describe("format", () => {
  it("format", () => {
    expect(format).toBeDefined();
  });
});
```

Jest tests use Jest's globals and need no import.

  Related Symbol (`Ctrl+Alt+Home`) also lists a file's tests among its views, routes and

- [File and code templates](docs/guide/user/file-templates.md): the PSR-4 rules behind the namespace and
  directory fields.

# File Structure, Navigation Bar and Related Symbol

Three of PHPStorm's navigation helpers, with the same shortcuts and wording. All three work
for PHP, Laravel, Symfony, Lua, HTML, CSS, JavaScript, TypeScript and Vue files, and in
remote projects.

## File Structure popup

**Navigate | File Structure** (`Ctrl+F12`, macOS `Cmd+F12`) shows the structure of the
current file as a tree: namespaces, classes, interfaces, traits and enums with their
constants, properties and methods (signatures, visibility and static/abstract badges as in
the [Structure tool window](docs/guide/user/php.md#structure)), functions, Lua tables and modules, CSS rules, HTML
elements and custom folding regions. The member at the caret is selected when it opens.

![File Structure popup](docs/screenshots/file-structure-popup.png)

- **Type to search**: the tree keeps the matching members and their classes; matched
  characters are highlighted and the best match is selected. Matching is fuzzy with camel
  humps, as in [Search Everywhere](docs/guide/user/search-everywhere.md#fuzzy-matching).
- `Up` / `Down`, `PageUp` / `PageDown` move the selection, `Enter` or a click jumps to the
  member, `Escape` closes the popup.
- **Show Inherited** (PHP): also lists the members a class inherits from its parent classes
  and interfaces, read from the PHP index; they are grayed out with `↑Parent` on the right.
  Press `Ctrl+F12` again while the popup is open to switch it.
- **Show Fields**: properties, constants and variables (shown when the file has some).
- **Show Lambdas**: anonymous functions and callbacks in JavaScript and TypeScript.
- **Sort Alphabetically**: sorts each level by name, keeping constants, properties and
  methods grouped.

![File Structure with inherited members and speed search](docs/screenshots/file-structure-inherited.png)

## Navigation Bar

The navigation bar shows where you are: the project, the folders, the file and, with
**Members in Navigation Bar**, the class and method at the caret:
`acme-shop › app › Http › Controllers › ProductController.php › ProductController › show()`.

![Navigation Bar with a folder's dropdown](docs/screenshots/navigation-bar.png)

- Click a segment to open its dropdown: a folder lists its folders and files, a file its
  classes and functions, a class its members. Type to filter the list; `Enter` opens a file,
  jumps to a member, or moves into a folder and shows its content.
- **Jump to Navigation Bar** (`Alt+Home`, macOS `Cmd+Up`) focuses the bar with the file's
  folder open and the file selected. `Left` / `Right` move between segments (and their
  dropdowns), `Down` opens the dropdown, `Enter` opens the selected file, `Escape` returns to
  the editor.

![Alt+Home with speed search](docs/screenshots/navigation-bar-alt-home.png)

![A class's members in the Navigation Bar](docs/screenshots/navigation-bar-members.png)

**View | Appearance | Navigation Bar** chooses where it is shown:

| Option | Where |
| --- | --- |
| **Top** (default) | above the editor of every editor group; the status bar keeps the file's path (project, folders, file) and works the same way |
| **In Status Bar** | only in the status bar, members included; dropdowns open upwards |
| **Don't Show** | hidden; `Alt+Home` shows the bar as a popup over the editor |

![Navigation Bar in the status bar](docs/screenshots/navigation-bar-status-bar.png)

![Alt+Home while the bar is hidden](docs/screenshots/navigation-bar-floating.png)

The same options are in **Settings | Appearance & Behavior | Appearance | Navigation Bar**:
*Navigation bar* (`appearance.navigationBar.location`: `top`, `statusBar`, `hidden`) and
*Show members in the navigation bar* (`appearance.navigationBar.showMembers`, on by default).
Library files (PHP stubs), scratches and data editors show their own path, without
dropdowns.

![View | Appearance | Navigation Bar](docs/screenshots/navigation-bar-menu.png)

The structure breadcrumbs at the bottom of the editor are a separate feature, see
[Sticky lines, breadcrumbs and Reader mode](docs/guide/user/code-structure.md#breadcrumbs).

## Related Symbol

**Navigate | Related Symbol...** (`Ctrl+Alt+Home`, macOS `Ctrl+Cmd+Up`) jumps to the files
that belong to the current one. With one result Forge opens it directly; with several the
**Choose Target** popup lists them grouped by kind.

![Related Symbol of a Laravel controller](docs/screenshots/related-symbol.png)

| From | To |
| --- | --- |
| PHP class | its PHPUnit or Pest test (`OrderTest.php`), and back from the test |
| Laravel controller | the views it renders (`view('products.show')`, `View::make`, Inertia pages) and its routes in `routes/*.php` |
| Blade view | the controller methods that render it and `Route::view` routes |
| Laravel model | its migrations (`create_orders_table`, `add_…_to_orders_table`, or the model's `$table`), factory, policy and seeder, and back |
| Symfony controller | the Twig templates it renders (`render()`, `renderView()`, `#[Template]`) |
| Twig template | the controller actions that render it |
| Vue, React, Svelte component or JS/TS module | its tests (`*.test.ts`, `*.spec.ts`, `__tests__/`, a `tests/` folder), stories (`*.stories.ts`) and style sheets (`*.module.css`, `*.scss`), and back |

![Related Symbol of a model](docs/screenshots/related-symbol-model.png)

If nothing is related, a hint says "No related symbols". The files are found in Rust next
to the project's files, so remote projects are searched on their host.

Source: docs/guide/user/file-types.md

# File types and syntax highlighting

## How a file's type is chosen

Like PHPStorm's Settings | Editor | File Types, Forge decides a file's type from, in this order:

1. **file names and path patterns**, e.g. `Dockerfile`, `.env.local`, `composer.lock`,
   `config/services.yaml` (in Symfony projects);
2. the **longest matching extension**, so `user.blade.php` is Blade, not PHP, and
   `page.html.twig` is Twig;
3. the **interpreter of a `#!` line** for files without an extension (`#!/usr/bin/env bash`,
   `#!/usr/bin/env python3`, `#!/usr/bin/env lua`).

Files that match nothing are "Plain text". The type is shown in the status bar and decides the
highlighting, the indentation (2 or 4 spaces), the language server and the file icon.

Plugins add types or replace bundled ones while they are active: in a Symfony project
`config/services*.yaml` becomes "Symfony Services", elsewhere it is plain YAML.

The complete list of types, extensions and file names is in the
[file types reference](docs/guide/reference/file-types.md).

## Changing file types

Settings | Editor | **File Types** lists the recognized file types with their **File name
patterns**, like PHPStorm:

![File Types settings](docs/screenshots/file-types-settings.png)

- Select a type and add a pattern with **+** (`*.module`, `Procfile*`, `config/*.conf`), edit it
  with the pencil or remove it with **−**. A pattern belongs to one type: adding one that
  another type has moves it (the form tells you which type had it). Added patterns are bold,
  removed bundled ones are struck through; adding a removed one again restores it.
- **+** above the type list creates a **custom file type** (below); **−** and the pencil remove
  and edit custom types.
- **Ignored Files and Folders** lists names the Project view hides (`.git`, `__pycache__`,
  `*.pyc`, `.DS_Store`, …; `*` and `?` are wildcards).
- **Restore Defaults** in the header brings back the bundled patterns, removes custom types and
  resets the ignored names.

The changes apply to files opened afterwards, in the desktop app and in browser mode alike
(the detection runs in Rust, `forge-filetypes`). They are stored in `fileTypes.associations`,
`fileTypes.custom` and `fileTypes.ignoredFiles`.

### Custom file types

PHPStorm's "New File Type" dialog: a name, a description and the syntax highlighting of the
type.

![New File Type](docs/screenshots/file-types-custom.png)

| Option | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Line comment, Only at line start | starts a comment to the end of the line, e.g. `#` or `//` |
| Block comment start / end | e.g. `/*` and `*/`; may span lines |
| Hex prefix | e.g. `0x` for `0xFF` |
| Number postfixes | characters allowed after a number, e.g. `lLfF` |
| Support paired braces, brackets, parens | typing `{`, `[` or `(` inserts the closing one |
| Support string escapes | `\"` does not end a string |
| Ignore case | keywords match in any case |
| Keywords 1–4 | one keyword per line; each list has its own color (keyword, built-in, type, constant). Keywords may contain other characters, e.g. `#define` |

Strings in `"` and `'` and decimal numbers are always highlighted. Add the type's file name
patterns on the right after creating it; `Ctrl+/` comments lines with its line comment.

![A custom file type in the editor](docs/screenshots/custom-file-type-editor.png)

## Highlighted languages

About 70 languages are highlighted, among them PHP, Blade, Twig, Smarty, Latte, Jinja2,
Handlebars, Go templates, Velocity, Pug, HTML, CSS, SCSS, Sass, Less, Stylus, JavaScript,
TypeScript (and JSX/TSX), Vue, JSON, YAML, TOML, XML, Markdown, SQL, Lua, Python, Go, Rust,
Java, Kotlin, C, C++, C#, Ruby, Shell, PowerShell, Dockerfile, Nginx, Apache config, INI,
dotenv, Makefile, CMake, LaTeX, HTTP requests and many more.

| | | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ![TypeScript](docs/screenshots/syntax-typescript.png) | ![YAML](docs/screenshots/syntax-yaml.png) | ![Twig](docs/screenshots/syntax-twig.png) |
| ![Dockerfile](docs/screenshots/syntax-dockerfile.png) | ![.env](docs/screenshots/syntax-env.png) | ![Markdown](docs/screenshots/syntax-markdown.png) |

## Config and script formats with extra support

Some formats get more than colors, without needing a language server:

| Format | Files | Extras |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Shell Script | `.sh`, `.bash`, `.zsh`, `.bats`, `.bashrc`, `.profile`, `PKGBUILD`, `#!` scripts | completion of keywords, builtins, functions and variables; folding |
| Python | `.py`, `.pyi`, `SConstruct`, `#!` scripts | scope-aware completion, syntax checks |
| YAML | `.yml`, `.yaml`, `.neon`, `.clang-format`, … | folding, syntax checks |
| JSON | `.json`, `.jsonc`, `.json5`, `.lock`, `.babelrc`, `composer.lock`, … | folding, syntax checks |
| Dotenv | `.env`, `.env.local`, `.env.*.local`, `.env.example`, … | `${VAR}` interpolation, completion of variables in the file, Symfony Flex section folding, checks for unquoted spaces, unterminated quotes and duplicate keys |
| Ignore files | `.gitignore`, `.dockerignore`, `.npmignore`, `.*ignore` | pattern syntax, duplicate pattern hints |
| Dockerfile | `Dockerfile`, `Dockerfile.*`, `Containerfile`, `.dockerfile` | instruction, flag, stage and build-arg completion, hover docs, checks (unknown instruction, missing `FROM`) |
| Docker Compose | `compose.yaml`, `docker-compose.yml`, `compose.*.yaml`, … | Compose Specification completion and hover docs, works in incomplete files |
| INI | `.ini`, `php.ini`, `.editorconfig`, `.gitconfig`, systemd units, `my.cnf`, … | section folding, checks for broken sections and duplicate keys |
| Config | `.conf`, `.config` | key/value pairs, interpolation, nginx-style blocks |
| Postfix | `main.cf`, `master.cf` | parameter and restriction completion with documentation, lookup table types, checks |
| E-Mail | `.eml` | header/MIME highlighting, header completion, decoding of encoded words on hover, folding, checks |
| Symfony Services | `config/services*.yaml` (Symfony projects) | service, parameter and tag completion, `@service` and `%parameter%` highlighting |

These syntax checks feed the Problems view, but step aside when a language server for the
file is running (for example yaml-language-server), so you do not get every problem twice.

## Template data languages

Template languages (Twig, Smarty, Latte, Jinja2, Handlebars, Go templates) mix template tags
with content in another language, the **data language**. Forge highlights the content in its
real language and draws the template tags on top, so a LaTeX or SQL template is just as
readable as an HTML one.

![Twig in LaTeX](docs/screenshots/syntax-twig-latex.png)

The data language of a file is chosen from the first of these that applies:

1. the patterns in Settings | Languages & Frameworks | **Template Data Languages**
   (`templates.dataLanguages`), one entry per pattern: `legacy/latex/*.tpl=latex`,
   `*.mail.twig=text`;
2. a **compound file name**: `invoice.tex.twig` is LaTeX, `report.sql.twig` is SQL,
   `style.css.tpl` is CSS, `config.yaml.twig` is YAML;
3. HTML.

Data languages: `html`, `xml`, `latex`, `css`, `scss`, `less`, `javascript`, `typescript`,
`json`, `sql`, `yaml`, `ini`, `shell`, `go`, `text`. The setting can be stored per project and
applies to files opened afterwards.

![Twig in SQL](docs/screenshots/syntax-twig-sql.png)

### Template delimiters

In some data languages the default delimiters are part of the content, for example `{` in
LaTeX. The **Delimiters** table on the same page (`templates.delimiters`) sets the delimiters
of a template language *in a data language*, one row per pair, as the engines themselves allow
(Smarty's `left_delimiter`, Twig's `tag_variable` / `tag_block` / `tag_comment`, Jinja's
`*_start_string`, Go's `Delims`):

| Template | Data language | Delimiters (default) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Smarty | LaTeX | `[[ ]]` |
| Twig, Jinja2 | LaTeX | `\VAR{ }`, `\BLOCK{ }`, `\#{ }` |

Add a row with **+**, edit it with the pencil (or a double-click) and remove it with **−**.
The form shows the delimiters of the chosen template language; a pair can only appear once.
Files without a row use the language's usual delimiters (`{ }` for Smarty, `{{ }}`, `{% %}`
and `{# #}` for Twig). The table can be stored per project, and open editors follow a change
right away.

![Template delimiters](docs/screenshots/settings-template-delimiters.png)

Everything that knows about tags uses the configured delimiters: highlighting, comment
toggling (`Ctrl+/` inserts `[[* *]]` or `\#{ }`), folding of blocks, matching delimiters,
auto-closing and completion of the end tag after `[[/` or `{/`. In a data language without
its own parser (LaTeX, INI, Shell) a `%` or `#` inside a tag no longer starts a comment.
Smarty's `{literal}` blocks and its auto-literal rule (`{ ` followed by a space is text) are
respected.

![Smarty in LaTeX](docs/screenshots/syntax-smarty-latex.png)

![Twig in LaTeX](docs/screenshots/syntax-twig-latex-letter.png)

![Smarty](docs/screenshots/syntax-smarty.png)

## Language intelligence

Highlighting is built in. Completion, hover and diagnostics for most languages come from a
[language server](docs/guide/user/language-servers.md); Forge suggests installing one when a file uses a
feature only a server provides. JSON and YAML files are validated, completed and documented
from their [JSON schema](docs/guide/user/json-schema.md) without a server.


---

Source: docs/guide/user/language-servers.md

# Language servers

Completion, hover documentation, diagnostics, Go to Declaration and formatting for most
languages come from **language servers**: separate programs that speak the Language Server
Protocol. Forge does not bundle them. It knows about 30 of them, finds the ones you have
installed, offers to install missing ones, and starts them when a project needs them.

Servers start **lazily**: when you open the first file of a language. Several servers can serve
the same file and their results are merged, for example TypeScript + ESLint + Tailwind CSS on
a `.tsx` file.

## Settings | Languages & Frameworks | Language Servers

![Language Servers settings](docs/screenshots/language-servers-settings.png)

| Option | Setting | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Start language servers for languages found in the project | `langservers.autoStart` | on |
| Files scanned to detect languages (ignored files, `node_modules` and `vendor` are skipped) | `langservers.scanLimit` | 20000 |
| Suggest installing missing language servers | `langservers.hints.enabled` | on |

Below is the server table, grouped by language. Groups for languages that occur in the open
project are marked **used in this project**; **Project languages only** hides the others. The
header shows how many servers are running and installed, and **Detect Again** (the refresh
icon) searches for executables again.

Each row has:

- an **Enabled** checkbox (`langservers.servers.<id>.enabled`);
- the **Status**: Running (with indexing progress), Installed, Not found, Disabled, or why a
  server is skipped (for example "Chosen in Languages & Frameworks | PHP" for the PHP
  servers, or a server of the same alternative group already running);
- the **Path** where it was found, or an **Install…** button.

Select a row to see its details:

![Server details](docs/screenshots/language-servers-details.png)

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Description, licence, homepage | from the catalog |
| Command | the command line Forge starts |
| Executable | a custom path to the executable (`langservers.servers.<id>.path`); empty = detect automatically |
| Extra settings (JSON) | merged into the server's settings (`langservers.servers.<id>.settings`); put startup options under an `"initializationOptions"` key. **Show Defaults** shows what Forge sends by default. |
| Install | the ways to install it |

### Where Forge looks for servers

In this order: the project's `node_modules/.bin`, Forge's own server folder
(`<data dir>/forge/langservers/node_modules/.bin`, e.g.
`~/.local/share/forge/langservers` on Linux), the `PATH`, npm/nvm/volta/fnm global folders,
`~/.local/bin`, Composer's global `vendor/bin`, cargo, go, dotnet and gem folders, Neovim's
Mason (`~/.local/share/nvim/mason/bin`) and Windows `.cmd` shims. TypeScript SDKs and
`@vue/typescript-plugin` are also looked up in the project's and Forge's `node_modules`.

### Installing a server

**npm servers install with one click.** Their rows have an **Install** button; Forge downloads
everything itself, nothing else needs to be installed first:

1. **Node.js**: a `node` 18 or newer on the machine is used; otherwise Forge downloads the
   official Node.js LTS build from `langservers.download.nodeMirror`
   (default `https://nodejs.org/dist`), checks it against the release's `SHASUMS256.txt` and
   keeps it in `<data dir>/forge/runtimes/`.
2. **The package**: packages without dependencies (Intelephense) come straight from the npm
   registry (`langservers.download.npmRegistry`, default `https://registry.npmjs.org`) and are
   checked against the registry's sha512 integrity hash; others are installed with the npm that
   belongs to that Node.js, into Forge's server folder — never globally.
3. Servers in Forge's folder are started with Forge's Node.js, so no `node` on your `PATH` is
   needed.

Progress shows in the status bar ("Installing Intelephense: Downloading Node.js … 45%") and in
the row. Afterwards the server starts with the next matching file, without reopening the
project.

![Install buttons](docs/screenshots/language-servers-install-buttons.png)

Other servers keep **Install…**, which opens a dialog with the command and its output:

![Install dialog](docs/screenshots/language-servers-install-output.png)

- Other tools (`brew`, `pipx`, `go install`, `cargo install`, `dotnet tool`, `gem`,
  `composer global require`) run exactly as listed in the catalog, without a shell.
- Commands that need root (`apt`, `pacman`) are only shown with **Copy Command**; run them in a
  terminal.
- Download-only servers link to their release page; download them and set **Executable**.

The full list of servers, their commands and install options is in the
[language servers reference](docs/guide/reference/language-servers.md).

### Updates

Once a day Forge asks the npm registry whether the servers it installed have newer versions
(**Check for updates of servers installed by Forge once a day**, `langservers.updates.check`).
A balloon "Language server update available" offers **Update** / **Not now**; updating
restarts the server.

![Update offer](docs/screenshots/language-server-update-offer.png)

| Option | Setting | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Check for updates once a day | `langservers.updates.check` | on |
| npm registry | `langservers.download.npmRegistry` | `https://registry.npmjs.org` |
| Node.js download mirror | `langservers.download.nodeMirror` | `https://nodejs.org/dist` |

For development there is also a command-line installer (`pnpm langservers` in `app/ui`, binary
`forge-langservers`): `install [--accept-intelephense-licence] [package…]`, `updates`, `where`.

### Alternatives

Some servers are alternatives: only the first enabled and installed one starts.
`typescript-language-server` is preferred over `vtsls`; `basedpyright` over `pyright`.
Disable the preferred one to use the other.

### Servers that depend on the project

ESLint starts only with an ESLint config (`eslint.config.*`, `.eslintrc*`) or an `eslint`
dependency; Tailwind CSS only with `tailwind.config.*` or a Tailwind dependency; the Angular
Language Service only with `@angular/core`. Servers that belong to a plugin (TypeScript to
WebForge, Vue to `forge.vue`, Lua to `forge.lua`) start only while that plugin is active.

## Install suggestions in the editor

When a file uses something only a language server provides, and that server is not installed,
a banner above the editor offers it. A JSON `"$schema"` or a YAML
`# yaml-language-server: $schema=…` modeline needs no server: Forge validates, completes and
documents such files itself (see [JSON Schema](docs/guide/user/json-schema.md)). While the JSON or YAML server
runs for a file, Forge leaves schema problems, completion and hover to it.

- **Install…** opens the install dialog.
- **Not now** hides the banner until Forge restarts.
- **Don't show again** stores the server in `langservers.hints.dismissed`.

## Status bar

The language server widget shows "Indexing… TypeScript 45%" while a server reports progress,
otherwise the running servers and their state. Click it to open the Language Servers page.

## PHP: Intelephense and Phpactor

PHP servers are configured by the PHP pack, on Settings | Languages & Frameworks | **PHP**
(`php.lsp.server`):

| Choice | Behaviour |
| --- | --- |
| Auto (default) | Intelephense if installed, else Phpactor |
| Intelephense | always Intelephense (shows where it was found, or "not found on PATH (npm i -g intelephense)") |
| phpactor | always Phpactor |
| None (built-in index only) | no language server; completion and diagnostics from a server are missing, Forge's index still gives structure, search, hover and Generate |

The server starts when a PHP project opens and restarts when these settings change. Its cache
goes to `<cache dir>/forge/intelephense`, never into your project.

### Installing Intelephense

Intelephense is never bundled with Forge (its licence forbids redistribution), but Forge
downloads it for you from the npm registry. When a local PHP project opens without it, a
balloon says "PHP language server Intelephense is not installed" with **Install**, **Not now**
and **Don't ask again**. The PHP settings page and the Language Servers page have an
**Install Intelephense** button as well.

![Install offer](docs/screenshots/intelephense-install-offer.png)

The first install asks you to accept the Intelephense licence (stored as
`php.intelephense.licenceAccepted`). Forge then installs it as described in
[Installing a server](#installing-a-server) (with Node.js if needed) and starts it right away.

![Installing](docs/screenshots/intelephense-install-progress.png)

| Option (Settings \| Languages & Frameworks \| PHP) | Setting | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| When Intelephense is not installed: Ask when a PHP project opens, Install automatically, Do not install | `php.intelephense.autoInstall` | `ask` |
| I accept the Intelephense licence | `php.intelephense.licenceAccepted` | off |

You can still install it yourself (`npm install -g intelephense`); Forge finds it on the `PATH`.

### Intelephense licence key (premium)

Intelephense is free; a licence key from intelephense.com unlocks its premium features (rename,
code actions, type hierarchy and more). Forge never ships a key.

1. Open Settings | Languages & Frameworks | Language Servers (or the PHP page) and find
   **Intelephense: Free**.
2. Click **Enter Licence Key…**, paste your key and confirm with `Enter`.
3. The status changes to **Premium (key …1234)** and Intelephense restarts.

![Licence dialog](docs/screenshots/intelephense-licence-dialog.png)

The key is stored in the operating system's keychain (service `forge-lsp`, account
`intelephense`), never in a settings file, and is passed to the server as `licenceKey`. In free
mode no key is sent. **Change Licence Key…** replaces it; **Remove Licence** in the dialog
deletes it.

> **Note:** a key saved by an older Forge version in the setting `php.lsp.licenceKey` is moved
> to the keychain once.

## Lua

lua-language-server gets the APIs of LÖVE or Neovim depending on Settings | Languages &
Frameworks | Lua | **Lua environment**. See [LuaForge](docs/guide/user/luaforge.md#lua-language-server).

## Remote projects

In a [remote project](docs/guide/user/remote-development.md) language servers run on the remote host, next to
the files: the PHP server (the Forge agent finds Intelephense or Phpactor on the host) and the
catalog servers, whose project scan, detection (`node_modules/.bin`, `PATH`, npm/nvm/volta, …)
and configuration happen on the host too.

**Install** on the Language Servers page installs on the host: the Forge agent downloads
Node.js (when the host has none) and the npm package into Forge's directory on the host
(`~/.local/share/forge`), checking their hashes, and streams its steps and download progress to
the page. The page names the host, and so do the install dialog and the Intelephense offer, which
always asks before downloading onto a host (also with `auto install` set to always). The
Intelephense licence is accepted on your machine. Updates of the servers Forge installed are
checked on the host too.

![Language Servers page of a remote project](docs/screenshots/remote-finish-langserver.png)

![Installing on the host](docs/screenshots/remote-finish-langserver-dialog.png)

## Troubleshooting

- **"Not found" although it is installed**: Forge may have been started from a desktop launcher
  with a shorter `PATH` than your shell. Set **Executable** to the full path, or start Forge
  from a terminal.
- **A Node-based server fails to start**: servers you installed yourself need `node` on Forge's
  `PATH`; servers installed by Forge use Forge's Node.js.
- More in [Troubleshooting](docs/guide/troubleshooting.md#language-server-not-found).

Source: docs/guide/user/keymap.md

# Keymap

Forge ships **PHPStorm's default keymaps** 1:1, for Windows/Linux and for macOS, keyed by
PHPStorm's action ids, plus PHPStorm's keymaps for people coming from **VS Code**, **Eclipse**,
**Sublime Text** and **Emacs**. Shortcuts you know from PHPStorm work the same, and actions that Forge has
not implemented yet stay bound and show "*Action* is not available yet" instead of doing
something unexpected.

The complete list with both platforms is in the [keymap reference](docs/guide/reference/keymap.md); the
[shortcut pages](docs/guide/user/shortcuts/index.md) explain them by topic and the
[reference card](docs/guide/user/shortcuts/reference-card.md) fits on one page.

## The most important shortcuts

| Action | Windows/Linux | macOS |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Search Everywhere | `Double Shift` | `Double Shift` |
| Find Action | `Ctrl+Shift+A` | `Cmd+Shift+A` |
| Go to Class / File / Symbol | `Ctrl+N` / `Ctrl+Shift+N` / `Ctrl+Alt+Shift+N` | `Cmd+O` / `Cmd+Shift+O` / `Cmd+Alt+O` |
| Recent Files | `Ctrl+E` | `Cmd+E` |
| Go to Declaration | `Ctrl+B`, `Ctrl+Click` | `Cmd+B`, `Cmd+Click` |
| Quick Documentation | `Ctrl+Q` | `F1`, `Ctrl+J` |
| Generate | `Alt+Insert` | `Cmd+N` |
| Reformat Code | `Ctrl+Alt+L` | `Cmd+Alt+L` |
| Settings | `Ctrl+Alt+S` | `Cmd+,` |
| Commit | `Ctrl+K` | `Cmd+K` |
| Run / Debug | `Shift+F10` / `Shift+F9` | `Ctrl+R` / `Ctrl+D` |
| Project / Terminal tool window | `Alt+1` / `Alt+F12` | `Cmd+1` / `Alt+F12` |
| New Scratch File | `Ctrl+Alt+Shift+Insert` | `Cmd+Shift+N` |
| Run Command (Command Line Tools Console) | `Ctrl+Shift+X` | `Cmd+Shift+X` |

## Settings | Keymap

![Keymap settings](docs/screenshots/keymap-settings.png)

- **Keymap** (`keymap.active`): *PHPStorm (Windows/Linux)*, *PHPStorm (macOS)*, the
  [other keymaps](#other-keymaps) and [your own keymaps](#your-own-keymaps). Until you pick one,
  Forge uses the PHPStorm keymap of your platform (`auto`). You can use a macOS keymap on Linux
  and vice versa. A derived keymap shows **Based on** with its parent.
- The **gear** next to it: **Duplicate…**, **Derive…**, **Rename…** and **Delete** (your own
  keymaps only) and **Restore Defaults**.
- The tree groups actions like PHPStorm: Main Menu (File, Edit, View, Navigate, Code,
  Refactor, Run, Git, Window, …), Editor Actions, Debugger Actions, Other and Plugins.
  Changed actions are highlighted.
- **Search actions** filters by name; **Find Actions by Shortcut** (the keyboard icon) filters
  by pressing the keys.

### Changing a shortcut

Select an action and press `Enter`, double-click it or use **Edit Shortcuts**:

- **Add Keyboard Shortcut** opens a dialog: press the keys (**First stroke**), optionally a
  **Second stroke** for a chord such as `Ctrl+K Ctrl+C`. The dialog lists conflicts ("The
  shortcut is already assigned to other actions") before you confirm; **Remove Others** takes
  the shortcut away from them.
- **Add Mouse Shortcut** opens the **Mouse Shortcut** dialog: choose **Single click** or
  **Double click**, then click in the pad with the mouse button and modifier keys to use, or
  turn the wheel while holding a modifier. See [mouse shortcuts](#mouse-shortcuts).
- **Remove *shortcut*** removes one shortcut.
- **Reset Shortcuts** restores the defaults of the action; the page can also reset all changes.

![Conflict](docs/screenshots/keymap-shortcut-conflict.png)

Changes are stored in the settings as you make them, so they live in `settings.toml` and not
in browser storage: `keymap.overrides.default` / `keymap.overrides.macOS` for the PHPStorm
keymaps, `keymap.overrides.bundled` for the other bundled keymaps (one entry per action: the
action id followed by its shortcuts, separated by tabs) and `keymap.custom` for your own
keymaps. Changes to a bundled keymap belong to that keymap only: switching to another keymap
does not carry them over.

> **Note:** importing PHPStorm keymap files (`.xml`) is not available yet.

## Other keymaps

Like PHPStorm, Forge bundles keymaps for the shortcuts of other editors. Each one is derived
from a PHPStorm keymap: it changes the shortcuts the other editor is known for and keeps
PHPStorm's for everything else, and shortcuts the editor uses for something else are taken away
from the PHPStorm actions so nothing fires twice.

![VS Code keymap](docs/screenshots/keymap-vscode.png)

| Keymap | Based on | Examples |
| --- | --- | --- |
| VS Code | PHPStorm (Windows/Linux) | `Ctrl+Shift+P` Find Action, `Ctrl+P` Go to File, `F2` Rename, `Ctrl+D` next occurrence, `F12` declaration, `Ctrl+K` chords |
| VS Code (macOS) | PHPStorm (macOS) | `Cmd+Shift+P`, `Cmd+P`, `Cmd+D`, `F12` |
| Eclipse | PHPStorm (Windows/Linux) | `Ctrl+Shift+R` Go to File, `Ctrl+Shift+T` Go to Class, `Ctrl+1` quick fix, `F3` declaration, `Ctrl+D` delete line |
| Eclipse (macOS) | PHPStorm (macOS) | `Cmd+Shift+R`, `Cmd+Shift+T`, `Cmd+1`, `F3`, `Cmd+D` |
| Sublime Text | PHPStorm (Windows/Linux) | `Ctrl+P` Go to File, `Ctrl+Shift+P` Find Action, `Ctrl+R` file structure, `Ctrl+D` next occurrence |
| Sublime Text (macOS) | PHPStorm (macOS) | `Cmd+P`, `Cmd+Shift+P`, `Cmd+R`, `Cmd+D` |
| Emacs | PHPStorm (Windows/Linux) | `Ctrl+X Ctrl+S` save, `Ctrl+X Ctrl+F` open, `Ctrl+S` find, `Alt+X` Find Action, `Ctrl+X 2` / `Ctrl+X 3` split |

Caret movement and text editing keys (`Ctrl+A`, `Ctrl+F`, … in Emacs) belong to the editor
itself and keep their usual meaning in every keymap; for modal editing use
[Vim emulation](docs/guide/user/vim-emulation.md).

## Your own keymaps

The gear next to the keymap selector makes keymaps of your own (listed under **Custom**):

- **Duplicate…** copies the selected keymap with all its shortcuts, including your changes.
- **Derive…** makes a keymap that follows the selected one and keeps only the shortcuts you
  change in it; later changes to its parent show up in it too.
- **Rename…** and **Delete** work on your own keymaps. Deleting a keymap selects its parent;
  keymaps derived from it keep their shortcuts.

![Keymap actions](docs/screenshots/keymap-derive.png)

## Mouse shortcuts

Actions can have mouse shortcuts, written like PHPStorm's:

| Notation | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `Ctrl+Button1 Click` | `Ctrl` and a click with the left button (`Button2`: middle, `Button3`: right, `Button4`/`Button5`: back and forward) |
| `Alt+Button1 Double Click` | a double click |
| `Ctrl+Wheel Up`, `Shift+Wheel Down` | turning the wheel while holding modifiers |

The PHPStorm keymaps bind **Declaration or Usages** to `Ctrl+Button1 Click` (macOS
`Cmd+Button1 Click`) and `Button2 Click` (middle click), and **Implementation(s)** to
`Ctrl+Alt+Button1 Click`. In the editor they act on the clicked symbol; rebinding them in the
keymap changes what the click does. Plain left clicks, double clicks, right clicks and plain
wheel turns cannot be bound, so selecting text, context menus and scrolling keep working.
Mouse shortcuts are ignored in text fields and the terminal.

![Mouse Shortcut](docs/screenshots/keymap-mouse-shortcut.png)

## How shortcuts are written

| Notation | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `Ctrl+Shift+A` | keys pressed together |
| `Ctrl+K Ctrl+C` | a chord: the first stroke, then the second |
| `Double Shift` | press `Shift` twice quickly |
| `Ctrl+Button1 Click` | a [mouse shortcut](#mouse-shortcuts) |
| `Cmd`, `Opt`/`Alt` | macOS modifiers |

Shortcuts use the physical key position, so they work with any keyboard layout (on a German
keyboard `Ctrl+Z` is the key labelled Z).

## Focus contexts

The same keys can mean different things depending on what has focus: the **editor**, a text
**input**, a **tool window** (for example `Alt+Insert` adds a row in a database grid but opens
Generate in the editor), or the **terminal**. In the terminal, plain `Ctrl`+letter,
`Alt`+letter and `Escape` go to the shell; function keys, `Alt`+digit, `Ctrl+Shift` and
`Ctrl+Alt` combinations still reach the IDE.

## Plugin actions

Plugins add their own actions under **Plugins** (and some under Main Menu), for example:

| Action | Default shortcut |
| --- | --- |
| Command Line Tool Support: Run Command… | `Ctrl+Shift+X` (macOS `Cmd+Shift+X`) |
| Terminal: New Terminal Tab | `Ctrl+Shift+T` (macOS `Cmd+T`), in the terminal |
| Database: Execute | `Ctrl+Enter` (macOS `Cmd+Enter`), in a console |
| Database: Submit / Add Row / Delete Rows / Revert Selected | `Ctrl+Enter` / `Alt+Insert` / `Ctrl+Y` / `Ctrl+Alt+Z` in a data grid |
| Database: Jump to Query Console… | `Ctrl+Shift+F10` in the Database tool window |
| Symfony: Run Console Command…, Symfony Routes | none |
| Doctrine Entities, npm tool window, Reload npm Scripts | none |

All of them can be rebound like PHPStorm actions.

## Tips

- **Find Action** (`Ctrl+Shift+A`, macOS `Cmd+Shift+A`) runs any action by name and shows its
  shortcut — the quickest way to learn them.
- In menus and popups the underlined letter (mnemonic) picks an entry.
- Shortcuts use the physical key position, so they work with any keyboard layout.
- Change any shortcut in Settings | Keymap; see [Keymap](docs/guide/user/keymap.md).

## Find Action

**Shortcut:** `Ctrl+Shift+A` · macOS `Cmd+Shift+A` · action id `GotoAction`

Finds any action by name and runs it (Find Action).

**Menu:** Navigate | Action…; Help | Find Action…

![Find Action](docs/screenshots/docs-find-action.png)

## Basic Completion

**Shortcut:** `Ctrl+Space`, `Shift+Space` · macOS `Ctrl+Space`, `Shift+Space` · action id `CodeCompletion`

Opens code completion at the caret; also offers words from the document.

**Menu:** Code | Code Completion | Basic Completion

More: [Editor](docs/guide/user/editor.md#code-completion)

## Cyclic Expand Word

**Shortcut:** `Alt+/` · macOS `Alt+/` · action id `HippieCompletion`

Completes the word at the caret with the nearest word of the file that starts with it (above the caret first, then below, then the other open files); press again to cycle.

**Menu:** Code | Code Completion | Cyclic Expand Word

More: [Editor](docs/guide/user/editor.md#cyclic-expand-word)

## Cyclic Expand Word (Backward)

**Shortcut:** `Alt+Shift+/` · macOS `Alt+Shift+/` · action id `HippieBackwardCompletion`

Like Cyclic Expand Word, but looks below the caret first and cycles the other way.

**Menu:** Code | Code Completion | Cyclic Expand Word (Backward)

More: [Editor](docs/guide/user/editor.md#cyclic-expand-word)

## Complete Current Statement

**Shortcut:** `Ctrl+Shift+Enter` · macOS `Cmd+Shift+Enter` · action id `EditorCompleteStatement`

Closes open brackets, adds the missing `;` (PHP, JavaScript, TypeScript) or `then … end` (Lua), opens the block of control statements and moves the caret on.

More: [Editor](docs/guide/user/editor.md#complete-current-statement)

## Parameter Info

**Shortcut:** `Ctrl+P` · macOS `Cmd+P` · action id `ParameterInfo`

Shows the parameters of the call at the caret, the current one in bold.

**Menu:** View | Parameter Info

More: [Editor](docs/guide/user/editor.md#parameter-info)

## Quick Documentation

**Shortcut:** `Ctrl+Q` · macOS `F1`, `Ctrl+J` · action id `QuickJavaDoc`

Shows the documentation of the symbol at the caret in a popup. Press it again to move the
documentation to the Documentation tool window.

**Menu:** View | Quick Documentation

![Quick Documentation](docs/screenshots/quick-documentation.png)

More: [Editor](docs/guide/user/editor.md#quick-documentation)

## External Documentation

**Shortcut:** `Shift+F1` · macOS `Shift+F1` · action id `ExternalJavaDoc`

Opens the online documentation of the symbol at the caret in the browser (php.net, Laravel API,
MDN, Vue, React, Lua manual).

**Menu:** View | External Documentation

More: [Editor](docs/guide/user/editor.md#external-documentation)

## Quick Definition

**Shortcut:** `Ctrl+Shift+I` · macOS `Alt+Space`, `Cmd+Y` · action id `QuickImplementations`

Shows the source of the declaration at the caret in a popup, with its docblock.

**Menu:** View | Quick Definition

![Quick Definition](docs/screenshots/quick-definition.png)

More: [Editor](docs/guide/user/editor.md#quick-definition)

## Type Info

**Shortcut:** `Ctrl+Shift+P` · macOS `Ctrl+Shift+P` · action id `ExpressionTypeInfo`

Shows the type of the expression at the caret.

**Menu:** View | Type Info

More: [Editor](docs/guide/user/editor.md#type-info-context-info-and-error-description)

## Context Info

**Shortcut:** `Alt+Q` · macOS `Ctrl+Shift+Q` · action id `EditorContextInfo`

Shows the headers of the class and method that enclose the caret at the top of the editor.

**Menu:** View | Context Info

More: [Editor](docs/guide/user/editor.md#type-info-context-info-and-error-description)

## Toggle Rendered View

**Shortcut:** `Ctrl+Alt+Q` · macOS `Ctrl+Alt+Q` · action id `ToggleRenderedDocPresentation`

**Menu:** Tools | Render All Doc Comments (the whole file)

## Generate

**Shortcut:** `Alt+Insert` · macOS `Cmd+N` · action id `Generate`

![Generate…](docs/screenshots/docs-generate.png)

More: [PHP](docs/guide/user/php.md#generate)

## Insert Live Template

**Shortcut:** `Ctrl+J` · macOS `Cmd+J` · action id `InsertLiveTemplate`

Lists the live templates that apply at the caret, filtered by the word before it; type to
narrow the list and press `Enter` to insert. Typing an abbreviation and pressing `Tab` expands
it directly.

**Menu:** Code | Insert Live Template…

![Insert Live Template](docs/screenshots/live-template-insert.png)

More: [Live templates](docs/guide/user/live-templates.md#expanding-a-template)

## Surround With

**Shortcut:** `Ctrl+Alt+T` · macOS `Cmd+Alt+T` · action id `SurroundWith`

Wraps the selected lines (or the caret line) in `if`, `if / else`, loops, `try / catch`, a
function, braces, a region or a live template that uses `$SELECTION$`.

**Menu:** Code | Surround With…

![Surround With](docs/screenshots/surround-with.png)

More: [Live templates](docs/guide/user/live-templates.md#surround-with)

## Surround with Live Template

**Shortcut:** `Ctrl+Alt+J` · macOS `Cmd+Alt+J` · action id `SurroundWithLiveTemplate`

Like Surround With, but lists only the live templates that use `$SELECTION$`.

**Menu:** Code | Surround with Live Template…

More: [Live templates](docs/guide/user/live-templates.md#surround-with)

## Unwrap/Remove

**Shortcut:** `Ctrl+Shift+Delete` · macOS `Cmd+Shift+Delete` · action id `Unwrap`

Lists the statements around the caret: unwrap one (keep the body the caret is in) or remove
an `else`, `elseif`, `catch` or `finally` branch. The editor previews the change.

**Menu:** Code | Unwrap/Remove…

![Unwrap/Remove](docs/screenshots/unwrap-remove.png)

More: [Live templates](docs/guide/user/live-templates.md#unwrapremove)

## Expand Emmet abbreviation

**Shortcut:** `Tab` (Settings | Editor | Emmet: `Tab`, `Enter` or `Space`)

Expands the Emmet abbreviation before the caret in HTML-like files, PHP, JSX and CSS:
`ul>li.item$*3`, `a{Home}`, `m10-20`, `df`. Live templates and postfix templates win when they
match; without an abbreviation the key does what it always does.

![An Emmet abbreviation expanded](docs/screenshots/emmet-expand.png)

More: [Emmet and color previews](docs/guide/user/emmet-and-colors.md)

## Surround with Emmet

**Shortcut:** none by default (also the **Emmet** entry of `Ctrl+Alt+J`) · action id `SurroundWithEmmet`

Wraps the selection, or the current line, with an abbreviation entered in a popup that
previews the result: `div.card`, `ul>li*` (one item per line), `a` around a URL.

![Surround with Emmet](docs/screenshots/emmet-surround.png)

More: [Emmet and color previews](docs/guide/user/emmet-and-colors.md#surround-with-emmet)

## Update Tag with Emmet

**Shortcut:** none by default · action id `EmmetUpdateTag`

Renames the tag around the caret and adds the id, classes and attributes of an abbreviation
(`section.hero[role=banner]`).

More: [Emmet and color previews](docs/guide/user/emmet-and-colors.md#update-tag-remove-tag-and-edit-points)

## Remove Tag

**Shortcut:** none by default · action id `EmmetRemoveTag`

Removes the tag around the caret and keeps its content, one indentation level further out.

More: [Emmet and color previews](docs/guide/user/emmet-and-colors.md#update-tag-remove-tag-and-edit-points)

## Next Emmet Edit Point

**Shortcut:** `Alt+Shift+]` · macOS `Ctrl+Alt+]` · action id `EmmetNextEditPoint`

Moves the caret to the next empty attribute value, empty element or empty line.

More: [Emmet and color previews](docs/guide/user/emmet-and-colors.md#update-tag-remove-tag-and-edit-points)

## Previous Emmet Edit Point

**Shortcut:** `Alt+Shift+[` · macOS `Ctrl+Alt+[` · action id `EmmetPreviousEditPoint`

More: [Emmet and color previews](docs/guide/user/emmet-and-colors.md#update-tag-remove-tag-and-edit-points)

![The color picker](docs/screenshots/color-picker.png)

## Duplicate Line or Selection

**Shortcut:** `Ctrl+D` · macOS `Cmd+D` · action id `EditorDuplicate`

## Go to Declaration or Usages

**Shortcut:** `Ctrl+B` · macOS `Cmd+B` · action id `GotoDeclaration`

Jumps to the declaration of the symbol at the caret (also `Ctrl+Click` and middle click); on a declaration it shows its usages; several targets open the Choose Declaration popup. PHP's own classes and functions open read-only in the PHP stubs.

**Menu:** Navigate | Declaration or Usages

![Ctrl+hover on \Throwable](docs/screenshots/php-nav-ctrl-hover.png)

More: [Editor](docs/guide/user/editor.md#go-to-declaration), [PHP navigation](docs/guide/user/php.md#navigation)

## Go to Implementation(s)

**Shortcut:** `Ctrl+Alt+B` · macOS `Cmd+Alt+B` · action id `GotoImplementation`

Lists the classes implementing or extending the class or interface at the caret, or the methods overriding the method (also `Ctrl+Alt+Click`).

**Menu:** Navigate | Implementation(s)

More: [Editor](docs/guide/user/editor.md#implementation-type-declaration-super-method)

## Go to Type Declaration

**Shortcut:** `Ctrl+Shift+B` · macOS `Cmd+Shift+B` · action id `GotoTypeDeclaration`

Jumps to the class of the variable, property or method return type at the caret.

**Menu:** Navigate | Type Declaration

More: [Editor](docs/guide/user/editor.md#implementation-type-declaration-super-method)

## Go to Super Method

**Shortcut:** `Ctrl+U` · macOS `Cmd+U` · action id `GotoSuperMethod`

Jumps to the method the current method overrides or implements; on a class, to its parent class and interfaces.

**Menu:** Navigate | Super Method

More: [Editor](docs/guide/user/editor.md#implementation-type-declaration-super-method)

## Type Hierarchy

**Shortcut:** `Ctrl+H` · macOS `Ctrl+H` · action id `TypeHierarchy`

Shows the class at the caret in the Hierarchy tool window: its parent classes and subtypes (Class Hierarchy), its supertypes or its subtypes.

**Menu:** Navigate | Type Hierarchy

More: [Type, Method and Call Hierarchy](docs/guide/user/hierarchies.md#type-hierarchy)

![Type Hierarchy](docs/screenshots/hierarchy-type.png)

## Method Hierarchy

**Shortcut:** `Ctrl+Shift+H` · macOS `Cmd+Shift+H` · action id `MethodHierarchy`

Shows which classes define the method at the caret, which inherit it and which should define it.

**Menu:** Navigate | Method Hierarchy

More: [Type, Method and Call Hierarchy](docs/guide/user/hierarchies.md#method-hierarchy)

## Call Hierarchy

**Shortcut:** `Ctrl+Alt+H` · macOS `Ctrl+Alt+H` · action id `CallHierarchy`

Shows the callers (or callees) of the method or function at the caret, one level per expanded node, with the call sites.

**Menu:** Navigate | Call Hierarchy

More: [Type, Method and Call Hierarchy](docs/guide/user/hierarchies.md#call-hierarchy)

## Back

**Shortcut:** `Ctrl+Alt+Left` · macOS `Cmd+[`, `Cmd+Alt+Left` · action id `Back`

Goes back to the previous caret location in your navigation history.

**Menu:** Navigate | Back

More: [Editor](docs/guide/user/editor.md#go-to-declaration)

## Forward

**Shortcut:** `Ctrl+Alt+Right` · macOS `Cmd+]`, `Cmd+Alt+Right` · action id `Forward`

Goes forward in the navigation history.

**Menu:** Navigate | Forward

More: [Editor](docs/guide/user/editor.md#go-to-declaration)

## Last Edit Location

**Shortcut:** `Ctrl+Shift+Backspace` · macOS `Cmd+Shift+Backspace` · action id `JumpToLastChange`

Goes back to the previous place where you changed text, across files. This edit history is separate from Back/Forward: edits a line or two apart count as one place, places follow later edits, renames and deletions, and the place the caret is already at is skipped. Recent Locations' **Show changed only** lists the same places.

**Menu:** Navigate | Last Edit Location

More: [Workbench](docs/guide/user/workbench.md#recent-files-and-switcher)

## Next Edit Location

**Shortcut:** none by default · action id `JumpToNextChange`

Goes forward again through the edit history after Last Edit Location. A new edit starts over at the newest place.

**Menu:** Navigate | Next Edit Location

More: [Workbench](docs/guide/user/workbench.md#recent-files-and-switcher)

## Select In

**Shortcut:** `Alt+F1` · macOS `Alt+F1` · action id `SelectIn`

Shows the current file somewhere else. Pick a target with its number, the arrow keys and `Enter`, or a click:

| Target | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Project View | Opens the Project tool window and selects the file. |
| Commit | Selects the file in the Commit tool window (only when it has local changes). |
| Structure | Opens the Structure tool window with the member at the caret selected. |
| File Structure | Opens the File Structure popup (`Ctrl+F12`). |
| Navigation Bar | Focuses the navigation bar (`Alt+Home`). |
| Git Log | Opens the Git log filtered to the file's history (Git projects). |
| Explorer / Finder / File Manager | Shows the file selected in the system file manager (local projects). |
| Terminal | Opens a terminal tab in the file's folder. |

From the Project view (with the focus in the tree) the targets apply to the selected file and Project View is left out.

**Menu:** Navigate | Select In...

![Select In](docs/screenshots/select-in.png)

More: [Project view](docs/guide/user/workbench.md#project-view)

## Next Method

**Shortcut:** `Alt+Down` · macOS `Ctrl+Down` · action id `MethodDown`

Moves the caret to the name of the next class, interface, trait, enum, function or method, or to the closing brace of a class. Works in every language with Sticky Lines: PHP, JavaScript/TypeScript (also in Vue and HTML scripts), CSS/SCSS/Less rules, Lua and other brace languages.

**Menu:** Navigate | Next Method

More: [Code structure](docs/guide/user/code-structure.md)

## Previous Method

**Shortcut:** `Alt+Up` · macOS `Ctrl+Up` · action id `MethodUp`

Moves the caret to the previous class, function, method or CSS rule.

**Menu:** Navigate | Previous Method

More: [Code structure](docs/guide/user/code-structure.md)

## Next Change

**Shortcut:** `Ctrl+Alt+Shift+Down` · macOS `Ctrl+Alt+Shift+Down` · action id `VcsShowNextChangeMarker`

Moves the caret to the next block that differs from Git `HEAD` (the gutter change markers), wrapping around at the end of the file, and shows its popup with the old text, **Rollback** and **Show Diff**, like a click on the marker.

**Menu:** Navigate | Next Change

![Next Change](docs/screenshots/next-change.png)

More: [Git change markers](docs/guide/user/git.md#change-markers)

## Previous Change

**Shortcut:** `Ctrl+Alt+Shift+Up` · macOS `Ctrl+Alt+Shift+Up` · action id `VcsShowPrevChangeMarker`

Moves the caret to the previous changed block and shows its popup.

**Menu:** Navigate | Previous Change

More: [Git change markers](docs/guide/user/git.md#change-markers)

## Jump to Navigation Bar

**Shortcut:** `Alt+Home` · macOS `Cmd+Up` · action id `ShowNavBar`

Focuses the navigation bar with the file's folder open; `Left` / `Right` move between the segments, `Down` opens a dropdown, `Enter` opens a file, `Escape` returns to the editor. While the bar is hidden it opens as a popup.

# Shortcuts: Search

| [Find Previous / Move to Previous Occurrence](#find-previous--move-to-previous-occurrence) | `Shift+F3` | `Cmd+Shift+G` |

**Shortcut:** `Ctrl+Alt+F7` · macOS `Cmd+Alt+F7` · action id `ShowUsages`

Shows the usages of the symbol at the caret in a popup; `Enter` opens one, the pin button keeps them in the Find tool window. `Ctrl+Click` on a declaration does the same.

**Menu:** Edit | Find Usages | Show Usages

![Show Usages](docs/screenshots/php-nav-show-usages.png)

## Find Usages in File

Finds the usages of the symbol at the caret in the current file and shows them in the Find tool window.

**Menu:** Edit | Find Usages | Find Usages in File

![Find Usages in File](docs/screenshots/find-usages-in-file.png)

More: [Editor](docs/guide/user/editor.md#find-usages-in-file)

## Highlight Usages in File

**Shortcut:** `Ctrl+Shift+F7` · macOS `Cmd+Shift+F7` · action id `HighlightUsagesInFile`

Highlights the usages of the symbol at the caret in the file (reads and writes in different colors) until `Escape`; `F3` / `Shift+F3` jump between them. On `return` / `throw` it highlights the exit points, on `implements` / `extends` the implementing / overriding methods.

**Menu:** Edit | Find Usages | Highlight Usages in File

![Highlight Usages in File](docs/screenshots/highlight-usages-in-file.png)

More: [Editor](docs/guide/user/editor.md#highlight-usages)

## Find Usages Settings…

**Menu:** Edit | Find Usages | Find Usages Settings…

# Shortcuts: Refactoring

Refactorings and code generation. Windows/Linux shortcuts first, macOS second; both are PHPStorm's defaults and can be changed in Settings | Keymap.

| Action | Windows / Linux | macOS |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [Refactor This…](#refactor-this) | `Ctrl+Alt+Shift+T` | `Ctrl+T` |
| [Rename…](#rename) | `Shift+F6` | `Shift+F6` |
| [Introduce Variable…](#introduce-variable) | `Ctrl+Alt+V` | `Cmd+Alt+V` |
| [Introduce Constant…](#introduce-constant) | `Ctrl+Alt+C` | `Cmd+Alt+C` |
| [Introduce Field…](#introduce-field) | `Ctrl+Alt+F` | `Cmd+Alt+F` |
| [Introduce Parameter…](#introduce-parameter) | `Ctrl+Alt+P` | `Cmd+Alt+P` |
| [Extract Method…](#extract-method) | `Ctrl+Alt+M` | `Cmd+Alt+M` |
| [Inline…](#inline) | `Ctrl+Alt+N` | `Cmd+Alt+N` |
| [Change Signature…](#change-signature) | `Ctrl+F6` | `Cmd+F6` |
| [Move…](#move) | `F6` | `F6` |
| [Copy…](#copy) | `F5` | `F5` |
| [Safe Delete…](#safe-delete) | `Alt+Delete` | `Cmd+Delete` |
| [Extract Interface…](#extract-interface) | — | — |
| [Extract Superclass…](#extract-superclass) | — | — |
| [Extract Component…](#extract-component) | — | — |
| [Pull Members Up…](#pull-members-up) | — | — |
| [Push Members Down…](#push-members-down) | — | — |
| [Make Static…](#make-static) | — | — |
| [Show Context Actions](#show-context-actions) | `Alt+Enter` | `Alt+Enter` |
| [Generate…](#generate) | `Alt+Insert` | `Cmd+N` |
| [Reformat Code](#reformat-code) | `Ctrl+Alt+L` | `Cmd+Alt+L` |

## Rename

**Shortcut:** `Shift+F6` · macOS `Shift+F6` · action id `RenameElement`

In the editor: renames the symbol at the caret in place, in every file of the project; `Enter`
applies, `Escape` cancels, `Shift+F6` again opens the Rename dialog. In the Project view:
renames the selected file or folder. One undo step (`Ctrl+Z`) undoes the whole rename.

**Menu:** Refactor | Rename…

![In-place rename](docs/screenshots/rename-in-place.png)

More: [Editor](docs/guide/user/editor.md#rename), [PHP](docs/guide/user/php.md#rename)

## Refactor This

**Shortcut:** `Ctrl+Alt+Shift+T` · macOS `Ctrl+T` · action id `Refactorings.QuickListPopupAction`

A popup with only the refactorings that apply at the caret or to the selection, with their
shortcuts: on a PHP class Rename, Move, Copy, Safe Delete, Extract Interface / Superclass and Pull
Members Up / Push Members Down; on a method Rename, Change Signature, Move, Safe Delete, Inline,
Pull Up / Push Down and Make Static; on an expression or a selection Introduce Variable /
Constant / Field / Parameter and Extract Method. In JavaScript, TypeScript and Vue files it
offers Rename, Extract Component (for whole elements), Move and Copy, and the language server's
refactorings worded like PHPStorm (see [WebForge](docs/guide/user/webforge.md#language-server-refactorings)). Pick one with its number (`1`-`9`, `0`), the arrow keys and
`Enter`, or a click; typing filters the list (speed search), `Escape` clears the filter.

![Refactor This on a class](docs/screenshots/refactor-this-class.png)

![Refactor This filtered by typing](docs/screenshots/refactor-this-method.png)

**Menu:** Refactor | Refactor This…

## Introduce Variable

**Shortcut:** `Ctrl+Alt+V` · macOS `Cmd+Alt+V` · action id `IntroduceVariable`

Puts the selected expression (or the one picked in the **Expressions** popup when nothing is
selected) into a new local variable. With several occurrences it asks whether to replace this
one or all of them. The name is then edited in place: `Up` / `Down` choose another suggested
name, `Enter` finishes. In the editor this shortcut wins over the Vim toggle.

**Menu:** Refactor | Extract/Introduce | Variable…

![Expressions popup](docs/screenshots/introduce-variable-expressions.png)

More: [PHP](docs/guide/user/php.md#extract-introduce-and-inline)

## Introduce Constant

**Shortcut:** `Ctrl+Alt+C` · macOS `Cmd+Alt+C` · action id `IntroduceConstant`

Turns a constant expression into a class constant (`self::NAME`), or a global `const` outside
classes. The dialog asks for the name, the visibility and whether to replace all occurrences.

**Menu:** Refactor | Extract/Introduce | Constant…

![Introduce Constant](docs/screenshots/introduce-constant-dialog.png)

## Introduce Field

**Shortcut:** `Ctrl+Alt+F` · macOS `Cmd+Alt+F` · action id `IntroduceField`

Moves an expression of a method into a new property (`$this->name`), initialized in the current
method, the field declaration or the constructor.

**Menu:** Refactor | Extract/Introduce | Field…

## Introduce Parameter

**Shortcut:** `Ctrl+Alt+P` · macOS `Cmd+Alt+P` · action id `IntroduceParameter`

Adds a parameter for an expression to the enclosing function or method and passes the
expression at every call (or makes it the parameter's default value).

**Menu:** Refactor | Extract/Introduce | Parameter…

## Extract Method

**Shortcut:** `Ctrl+Alt+M` · macOS `Cmd+Alt+M` · action id `ExtractMethod`

Moves the selected statements or expression into a new method (a function outside classes).
The dialog shows the parameters (reorder and rename them), what is returned, the visibility,
**Declare static** and a signature preview, and offers to replace duplicate fragments.

**Menu:** Refactor | Extract/Introduce | Method…

![Extract Method](docs/screenshots/extract-method-dialog.png)

## Inline

**Shortcut:** `Ctrl+Alt+N` · macOS `Cmd+Alt+N` · action id `Inline`

Replaces a local variable by its value, a method or function call by the body, or a constant by
its value: every reference (removing or keeping the declaration) or only the one at the caret.

**Menu:** Refactor | Inline…

![Inline Method](docs/screenshots/inline-method-dialog.png)

## Change Signature

**Shortcut:** `Ctrl+F6` · macOS `Cmd+F6` · action id `ChangeSignature`

Changes the name, visibility, return type and parameters of a PHP method or function (add,
remove, reorder; type, name, default value and the value new parameters get at call sites) and
updates the overriding methods and every call.

**Menu:** Refactor | Change Signature…

![Change Signature](docs/screenshots/change-signature-dialog.png)

More: [PHP](docs/guide/user/php.md#move-copy-safe-delete-change-signature-and-make-static)

## Move

**Shortcut:** `F6` · macOS `F6` · action id `Move`

In the editor: moves the PHP class at the caret to another namespace and directory (Move
Class), static members to another class (Move Members) or a function to another file. In the
Project view: moves the selected files and folders (also by drag and drop), updating namespaces
and references of PHP classes.

**Menu:** Refactor | Move…

![Move Class](docs/screenshots/move-class-dialog.png)

## Copy

**Shortcut:** `F5` · macOS `F5` · action id `CopyElement`

Copies the PHP class at the caret under a new name (Copy Class), or the selected file or folder
in the Project view.

**Menu:** Refactor | Copy File…

## Safe Delete

**Shortcut:** `Alt+Delete` · macOS `Cmd+Delete` · action id `SafeDelete`

Deletes the element at the caret (or the selected files in the Project view) after checking
that nothing uses it; **Usages Detected** offers View Usages and Delete Anyway.

**Menu:** Refactor | Safe Delete…

![Usages Detected](docs/screenshots/safe-delete-usages-detected.png)

## Extract Interface

**Shortcut:** none by default · action id `ExtractInterface`

In a PHP class or enum: creates an interface (name, namespace, directory) from the PHP Interface
file template that declares the chosen public methods with their PHPDoc and holds the chosen
constants; the class implements it. **Replace class references with interface where possible**
changes parameter types that only need the interface's methods.

**Menu:** Refactor | Extract/Introduce | Interface…

![Extract Interface](docs/screenshots/extract-interface-dialog.png)

## Extract Superclass

**Shortcut:** none by default · action id `ExtractSuperclass`

Moves the chosen members of a PHP class into a new class that the class extends (between it
and its old parent); **Make abstract** keeps a method in the class and declares it abstract in
the superclass.

**Menu:** Refactor | Extract/Introduce | Superclass…

![Extract Superclass](docs/screenshots/extract-superclass-dialog.png)

## Extract Component

**Shortcut:** none by default · action id `WebForge.ExtractComponent`

Moves the selected Vue template elements or React JSX into a new component file with props for
the names they use; the parent renders and imports it. See
[WebForge](docs/guide/user/webforge.md#extract-component).

**Menu:** Refactor | Extract/Introduce | Component…

![Extract Component](docs/screenshots/extract-component-vue-dialog.png)

## Pull Members Up

**Shortcut:** none by default · action id `MembersPullUp`

Moves members into a superclass or interface of the class (interfaces get declarations), with
**Make abstract**; members a chosen one uses are highlighted, problems are listed before the
change.

**Menu:** Refactor | Pull Members Up…

![Pull Members Up](docs/screenshots/pull-members-up-dialog.png)

## Push Members Down

**Shortcut:** none by default · action id `MemberPushDown`

Copies members into every direct subclass and removes them from the class (**Keep abstract**
leaves an abstract declaration).

**Menu:** Refactor | Push Members Down…

## Make Static

**Shortcut:** none by default · action id `MakeStatic`

Makes a PHP instance method static, passing the object or the fields it reads as parameters,
and updates its calls.

**Menu:** Refactor | Make Static…

![Make Method Static](docs/screenshots/make-static-dialog.png)

## Show Context Actions

**Shortcut:** `Alt+Enter` · macOS `Alt+Enter` · action id `ShowIntentionActions`

Opens the intention popup at the caret: quick fixes, intentions and refactorings of the
language servers and Forge's PHP intentions. `Right` opens an entry's sub-menu.

**Menu:** Code | Show Context Actions

![Context actions](docs/screenshots/context-actions.png)

More: [Editor](docs/guide/user/editor.md#show-context-actions)

## Generate

**Shortcut:** `Alt+Insert` · macOS `Cmd+N` · action id `Generate`

In PHP files: generates a constructor, getters, setters, overrides, `__toString()` or a PHPDoc block.

**Menu:** Code | Generate…

![Generate…](docs/screenshots/docs-generate.png)

More: [PHP](docs/guide/user/php.md#generate)

## Reformat Code

**Shortcut:** `Ctrl+Alt+L` · macOS `Cmd+Alt+L` · action id `ReformatCode`

Formats the file with the language server's formatter (StyLua for Lua).

**Menu:** Code | Reformat Code

More: [Editor](docs/guide/user/editor.md#reformat-code)

# Color schemes

The color scheme decides how the editor draws code: the colors of keywords, strings, comments
and the other token kinds, the editor background, the caret, the caret row, the selection,
line numbers and search results. Like in PHPStorm it is separate from the UI theme
(Settings | Appearance & Behavior | Appearance | Theme, see
[Settings and themes](docs/guide/user/settings-and-themes.md#themes)).

![Color Scheme settings](docs/screenshots/color-scheme-settings.png)

## Choosing a scheme

Settings | Editor | **Color Scheme** | **Scheme** (`editor.colorScheme.active`):

| Scheme | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Follow the theme | the default: Ember with dark themes, Anvil with light ones, and the theme's own token colors (the Solarized themes bring their own) |
| Ember | Forge's dark scheme |
| Anvil | Forge's light scheme |
| *your schemes* | listed under **Custom** |

A scheme you select explicitly stays the same when you switch the UI theme, so you can, for
example, use the dark Ember editor with the light Anvil UI.

## Your own schemes

Ember and Anvil are bundled and cannot be changed. The **gear** next to the selector has:

- **Duplicate…**: copy the selected scheme into a new one and select it. Change it from there.
- **Rename…**, **Restore Defaults** (back to the colors of its parent, Ember or Anvil) and
  **Delete** for your own schemes.
- **Import Scheme…** and **Export…** (see below).

## Editing attributes

The list on the left holds the attributes in two groups:

- **General**: Default text (editor foreground and background), Caret, Caret row, Selection
  background, Line number, Search result.
- **Language Defaults**: Keyword, String, Number, Comment, Variable, Function, Class name,
  Property and attribute, Operator sign, Markup tag. Every language uses them (PHP, HTML, CSS,
  JavaScript, TypeScript, Lua, SQL, Markdown, …).

For the selected attribute you can set, where it applies:

- **Bold** and **Italic**;
- **Foreground** and **Background**: tick the box and pick a color; untick it to use the
  default text color or no background;
- **Effects**: Underscored, Bold underscored, Underwaved, Strikeout, Dotted line or Bordered,
  with its own color.

Changed attributes are highlighted in the list; **Reset to Ember** (or Anvil) gives one back
its parent's value. Changes are saved as you make them and show up in every open editor right
away.

The **preview** below shows a PHP class and some HTML in the scheme. Click a word in it to
select its attribute.

![Editing a scheme](docs/screenshots/color-scheme-edit.png)

## Import and export

- **Import Scheme…** reads an IntelliJ color scheme file (`.icls`, as exported by PHPStorm,
  IntelliJ IDEA, WebStorm or downloaded from a theme site) into a new scheme and selects it.
  IntelliJ's attributes are mapped onto Forge's (for example `DEFAULT_KEYWORD` or
  `PHP_KEYWORD` → Keyword, `PHP_VAR` / `DEFAULT_LOCAL_VARIABLE` → Variable,
  `CARET_ROW_COLOR` → Caret row); references to other attributes (`baseAttributes`) are
  followed. What the file does not set comes from Ember when its parent is Darcula (or another
  dark scheme) and from Anvil otherwise.
- **Export…** writes the selected scheme as an `.icls` file with every attribute, so it looks
  the same when you import it into a JetBrains IDE.

> **Note:** attributes Forge does not have (for example language-specific ones such as PHP
> heredoc colors, or the console colors) are ignored on import.

## Where schemes are stored

Your schemes are user settings (`editor.colorScheme.schemes`, one entry per scheme with its
name, its parent and the changed attributes), so they are part of `settings.toml`, of
**Export Settings** (group Editor) and of the [settings reference](docs/guide/reference/settings.md).
