# Composer

Forge works with [Composer](https://getcomposer.org) the way PHPStorm does: composer.json gets
a toolbar with the Composer commands, outdated packages are marked, package names and version
constraints complete from [Packagist](https://packagist.org), Tools | Composer | Add
Dependency… searches and installs packages, and `composer audit` reports security advisories
as problems. The Composer plugin (`forge.composer`, part of PHPForge) is active in projects
with a composer.json.

Composer runs on the project's machine (also in [remote projects](docs/guide/user/remote-development.md)) and
its output goes to the [Run tool window](docs/guide/user/run-debug.md). Which composer.json is the project's
and which Composer runs is set in
[Settings | Languages & Frameworks | PHP | Composer](#settings).

![composer.json with the Composer toolbar, outdated packages and the Update package quick fix](docs/screenshots/composer-editor.png)

## The composer.json toolbar

A composer.json of the project (not the ones inside `vendor/`) shows the Composer toolbar
above the editor:

| Action | Runs | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Install | `composer install` | installs the packages of composer.lock (creates it when it is missing) |
| Update | `composer update` | updates all packages within their constraints and writes composer.lock |
| Validate | `composer validate` | checks composer.json and composer.lock |
| Show Outdated | `composer outdated --direct` | lists the direct dependencies that have newer releases |
| Audit | `composer audit` | checks the installed packages for security advisories, see [Composer audit](#composer-audit) |
| Add Dependency… | | opens [Manage Composer Dependencies](#manage-composer-dependencies) |

The toolbar also says how many packages have updates, and the gear opens the Composer
settings. The same actions are in **Tools | Composer** and in Find Action (`Ctrl+Shift+A`,
"Composer"); they have no default shortcut, assign one in [Settings | Keymap](docs/guide/user/keymap.md).

Every command runs in its own tab of the Run tool window ("composer install"); Rerun and Stop
work as for any run. When Composer is done, composer.json and composer.lock reload in open
editors and the markers below are computed again.

![composer install in the Run tool window](docs/screenshots/composer-install.png)

## Outdated packages

Forge compares the installed version of every package in `require` and `require-dev`
(from composer.lock, or `vendor/composer/installed.json` when there is no lock file) with the
latest stable release on Packagist. An outdated package gets

- an arrow icon in the gutter; click it to update the package,
- a weak warning on its constraint: "Package 'laravel/framework' is outdated: v12.1.0 is
  installed, v12.3.0 is available",
- the quick fix **Update 'laravel/framework' to v12.3.0** on `Alt+Enter`.

When the constraint allows the new release (Composer's `semver-safe-update`), the update
runs `composer update <package> --with-dependencies`. When it does not
(`update-possible`, e.g. a new major version), it runs `composer require <package>:<new
constraint>` (with `--dev` in `require-dev`), which also rewrites the constraint in
composer.json; the new constraint is what Composer itself would write (`^13.0`).

Platform requirements (`php`, `ext-*`, `lib-*`) are not checked. Without network the markers
use the releases Forge saw last (see [Packagist access](#packagist-access)).

## Completion and documentation

In `require` and `require-dev`:

- **Package names** complete from the installed packages and a Packagist search for what you
  typed (description on the right), plus `php` and `ext-…` extensions. Packages already in
  the file are not offered again. Choosing a package writes `"vendor/package": ""` and
  continues with the version.
- **Version constraints** complete with the recommended constraint of the latest release
  (`^12.3`, "latest: v12.3.0"), one caret constraint per release line (`^11.44`), the released
  versions (the installed one is marked "installed") and `*`.
- **Hover** over a package name or constraint shows the package's description, the installed
  and the latest version and links to its homepage, source repository and Packagist page.

Completion of the other composer.json keys (`autoload`, `config`, …) comes from the
[JSON Schema](docs/guide/user/json-schema.md) support.

![Version completion](docs/screenshots/composer-completion-versions.png)

![Package documentation on hover](docs/screenshots/composer-hover.png)

## Manage Composer Dependencies

**Tools | Composer | Add Dependency…** (or "Add Dependency…" in the toolbar) opens PHPStorm's
Manage Composer Dependencies dialog:

- **Search** Packagist as you type; the list shows each package's description, downloads and
  stars, and marks installed and abandoned packages. `Up`/`Down` move through the results.
- **Description**: the selected package's description and links (Homepage, Source,
  Packagist).
- **Version to install**: "Latest (Composer chooses)", the recommended constraint
  (`^4.0 (recommended)`) or any released version.
- **Development (require-dev)** adds the package to `require-dev`.
- **Install** (or `Enter`, or a double click) runs `composer require vendor/package:<version>`
  in the Run tool window.
- **Installed Packages** lists the packages composer.json requires with their constraint and
  installed version. **Update** runs `composer update <package> --with-dependencies`,
  **Remove** runs `composer remove <package>`. The list reloads when Composer is done.

![Manage Composer Dependencies](docs/screenshots/composer-dependencies.png)

## Composer audit

**Tools | Composer | Audit** (or "Audit" in the toolbar) runs `composer audit --format=json`
(with `--locked` when there is a composer.lock) on the project's machine. The result is shown

- in the **Vulnerable Dependencies** tab of the [Problems tool window](docs/guide/user/editor.md#problems) (`Alt+6`):
  package, advisory (CVE or Packagist advisory id, linking to the advisory), affected
  versions, severity and title; click a row to go to the package; the refresh button runs the
  audit again,
- as errors on the package in composer.json (direct dependencies) and in composer.lock (every
  affected package), so they also appear under Current File and Project Errors,
- as warnings for abandoned packages ("Package swiftmailer/swiftmailer is abandoned, use
  symfony/mailer instead"),
- in a balloon: "Found 2 security vulnerability advisories affecting 2 packages".

![Vulnerable Dependencies tab of the Problems tool window](docs/screenshots/composer-audit.png)

## Settings

Settings | Languages & Frameworks | PHP | Composer:

| Option | Setting | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Path to composer.json | `php.composer.json` | `composer.json` | relative to the project root; the toolbar, Tools \| Composer and the dialog work on this file |
| Path to composer (Execution) | `php.composer.executable` | `composer` | a composer executable, or a `composer.phar` that runs with the [PHP interpreter](docs/guide/user/php.md#settings--languages--frameworks--php) (`php.interpreter`) |
| Download composer.phar from getcomposer.org | | | downloads the latest stable composer.phar, see below |
| Synchronize IDE settings with composer.json | `php.composer.syncWithComposerJson` | on | the PHP language level follows `require.php` |
| Add packages as libraries | `php.composer.addPackagesAsLibraries` | on | classes in `vendor/` are resolved for navigation and completion |
| Check for package updates on project open | `php.composer.checkUpdates` | off | runs `composer outdated --direct` when the project opens and lists the updates in a balloon |
| Use Packagist for completion, versions and outdated packages | `php.composer.packagist` | on | see [Packagist access](#packagist-access) |

![Settings | PHP | Composer](docs/screenshots/composer-settings.png)

### Download composer.phar

Without Composer on your machine, click **Download composer.phar from getcomposer.org**.
Forge asks first; after you click **Download** it fetches
`https://getcomposer.org/download/latest-stable/composer.phar`, checks it against the SHA-256
sum getcomposer.org publishes next to it (`composer.phar.sha256sum`), saves it in Forge's data
directory (`<data dir>/forge/composer/composer.phar`, see
[File locations](docs/guide/reference/file-locations.md)) and puts the path into "Path to composer";
**Apply** saves it. A file with the wrong checksum is not saved. Nothing is downloaded without
your click, and composer.phar is never bundled with Forge.

> **Note:** the downloaded composer.phar is on your machine. For a
> [remote project](docs/guide/user/remote-development.md) set "Path to composer" to a Composer on the remote
> host.

### Packagist access

Package names, versions, descriptions and the outdated markers come from Packagist's API
(`https://repo.packagist.org/p2/<vendor>/<package>.json` and `https://packagist.org/search.json`).
Forge reaches it from its own process (not from the UI), with the system proxy settings, and
caches the answers in `<cache dir>/forge/packagist` (package metadata for 6 hours, searches
for one hour), never in the project. Without network the cached answers are used; with
nothing cached, completion falls back to the installed packages and the outdated markers stay
away.

Turn off "Use Packagist for completion, versions and outdated packages" and Forge never
contacts Packagist: completion uses the installed packages only, there are no outdated
markers, and the dialog's search is unavailable. Composer itself still downloads packages
when you run it.

## Composer scripts

Scripts of composer.json run with a **Composer Script** run configuration
(`composer run-script <script>`), see [Run/Debug configurations](docs/guide/user/run-debug.md). It uses the
same "Path to composer", so a downloaded composer.phar works there too.


---

Source: docs/guide/user/laravel.md

# Laravel

The Laravel plugin (`forge.laravel`, PHPForge pack) activates in projects that require
`laravel/framework` or have an `artisan` file. It analyses the project statically in Rust (no
need to boot the application) and reloads when files change.

The status bar shows **Laravel 12** (the installed version); its tooltip counts routes, models,
views, components and config keys. Click it to open Settings | Languages & Frameworks | PHP |
Laravel.

## Blade

`*.blade.php` files are highlighted as Blade: HTML with echoes (`{{ }}`, `{!! !!}`), comments
(`{{-- --}}`), directives (`@foreach (...)`), `@php` blocks, components (`<x-alert :type="$t">`,
`<livewire:counter>`) and embedded `<script>`/`<style>`. PHP inside is highlighted as PHP.

![Blade](docs/screenshots/laravel-blade.png)

- Directives are completed, including the closing directive (`@foreach` … `@endforeach`).
- Custom directives registered with `Blade::directive()` or `Blade::if()` in the project are
  highlighted and completed like built-in ones. Add others in Settings | … | Laravel |
  **Additional Blade directives** (`laravel.blade.customDirectives`, names without `@`).

![Blade directives](docs/screenshots/laravel-blade-directives.png)

## Completion and Go to Declaration

In PHP and Blade files, Laravel completion appears next to the language server's, and
`Ctrl+B` / `Ctrl+Click` tries Laravel targets first:

| Where | Completes | Ctrl+B goes to |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `route('…')`, `to_route('…')` | route names | the route definition |
| `view('…')`, `@include('…')`, `@extends`, `View::make` | view names | the Blade file |
| `<x-…>` tags | Blade components (anonymous, class-based, Livewire) | the component |
| `config('…')` | config keys from `config/*.php` | the key in the config file |
| `env('…')` | keys from `.env` | the line in `.env` |
| `__('…')`, `trans('…')`, `@lang` | translation keys (PHP and JSON language files) | the translation |
| `->where('…')`, `orderBy`, `pluck` and other query builder calls | database columns, read from the migrations | the migration |
| `with('…')`, `load('…')` | Eloquent relations | the relation method |
| `$model->…` | model attributes (columns, `$fillable`, casts, accessors) and relations | the declaration |
| `Model::…` | local scopes | the `scope…` method |
| `[Controller::class, '…']` | controller methods | the method |
| custom Blade directives | | the `Blade::directive` call |

![Route completion](docs/screenshots/laravel-route-completion.png)

![Column completion](docs/screenshots/laravel-column-completion.png)

When a name has several targets (a view in two places, a component with a class and a
template), a **Choose Declaration** popup lists them.

![Go to view](docs/screenshots/laravel-goto-view.png)

Turn completion off with **Complete routes, views, config, translations and model attributes**
(`laravel.completion.enabled`) and **Complete database columns in query builder calls**
(`laravel.completion.columns`).

## ide.json

Packages and projects describe extra completions in an `ide.json` file (the format Laravel IDE
plugins such as Laravel Idea document). Forge reads the project's `ide.json` and the
`ide.json` of every installed package (`vendor/<vendor>/<package>/ide.json`):

- **completions:** `staticStrings` (a fixed list), `directoryFiles` (files of a folder, without
  `suffixToClear`) and the project's own lists `routeName`, `viewName`, `configKey`,
  `translationKey`, `envKey` and `validationRule`, offered where a `condition` applies:
  `functionNames` or `methodNames` (with `classFqn` / `classParentFqn`) and the 1-based
  `parameters`. Setting: **Complete values from ide.json files**
  (`laravel.completion.ideJson`).
- **codeGenerations:** listed in the Overview of the Laravel tool window. **Generate…** asks for
  a class name (`Orders/Invoice`), fills the stub templates (`${INPUT_CLASS|className|upperCamelCase}`,
  `${NAMESPACE}`, `${CLASS}`, with the `classSuffix`) and creates the files that do not exist
  yet below `App\<appNamespace>`.

```json
{
  "completions": [
    {
      "complete": "staticStrings",
      "options": { "strings": ["pending", "paid", "shipped"] },
      "condition": [{ "functionNames": ["order_status"], "parameters": [1] }]
    }
  ]
}
```

## Gutter icons

- **Route** icons next to controller actions that a route points to; click to go to the
  route definition (`laravel.gutter.routes`).
- **View** icons next to `view()` calls and Blade includes; click to open the template
  (`laravel.gutter.views`).

![Laravel gutter icons](docs/screenshots/laravel-gutter.png)

## Routes tool window

The **Routes** tool window (bottom) lists every route with **Method**, **URI**, **Name**,
**Action** and **Middleware**.

![Routes](docs/screenshots/laravel-routes.png)

- Type in the search field to filter by URI, name, action or middleware; `Up`/`Down` and
  `Enter` work in the list.
- Clicking a row opens the controller method (or the route definition for closures); the
  arrow button at the end of a row opens the route definition.
- **Refresh Routes** re-reads them.

Routes come from one of two sources, chosen with **Read routes from**
(`laravel.routes.source`, can be stored per project):

| Value | Source |
| --- | --- |
| `auto` (default) | `php artisan route:list --json` when a `vendor/` folder exists, else static analysis |
| `artisan` | always `php artisan route:list --json`; also sees routes registered by packages, but needs a bootable application |
| `static` | Forge reads `routes/*.php` itself: verbs, `match`, `view`, `redirect`, `resource`/`apiResource`, groups with prefix/name/middleware/controller, included files and the `api` prefix |

With artisan, the source locations from static analysis are kept so navigation still works.

## Laravel tool window

The **Laravel** tool window (bottom; **Tools | Laravel | Show Laravel Tool Window**) has two tabs.

**Overview:** the application (name, Laravel and PHP version, environment, debug, URL from
`.env` and `composer.json`), counts of routes, models, artisan commands, views, Blade components,
translations, config keys and log files, the Eloquent models with their tables, the
application's artisan commands (`app/Console/Commands` and `routes/console.php`; the run button
opens Run Command with the command typed in) and what `ide.json` contributes.

![Laravel tool window](docs/screenshots/laravel-tool-window-overview.png)

**Logs** (**Tools | Laravel | Show Logs**): the entries of `storage/logs/*.log` (the newest file
first; the last 2 MB of large files), parsed in Rust from Monolog's line format into level,
time, channel, message and context. Click an entry to expand the exception and its stack trace;
`file:line` links open the file, also for logs written in a container (`/var/www/html/app/…`
is mapped into the project), and vendor frames are dimmed.

![Laravel logs](docs/screenshots/laravel-logs.png)

- the level filter shows a level and the more severe ones;
- the search field filters messages, exceptions and context;
- **Follow** reloads the log every two seconds and scrolls to new entries (default:
  **Follow log files**, `laravel.logs.follow`).

Reading logs does not run project code, so the tool window also works in Safe Mode.

## Run Artisan Command

Artisan commands run in the Command Line Tools Console: **Tools | Run Command…**
(`Ctrl+Shift+X`, macOS `Cmd+Shift+X`) with the alias `a`, for example `a make:model Order -m`.
Laravel projects get the Artisan tool automatically. Forge completes the commands of
`php artisan list --format=json` (or Laravel's standard commands when the application cannot
boot), their options and arguments, and shows each command's help. **Tools | Laravel | Run
Artisan Command…** opens the popup with `a ` typed in. See
[Command Line Tool Support](docs/guide/user/command-line-tools.md).

![Artisan commands in the Run Command popup](docs/screenshots/cli-tools-commands.png)

The output goes to the Command Line Tools Console tool window, with clickable paths of the
generated files.

![Artisan output in the Command Line Tools Console](docs/screenshots/cli-tools-console.png)

For commands you run often, create an **Artisan** run configuration (Run | Edit
Configurations), which can also be debugged with Xdebug. See
[Run/Debug configurations](docs/guide/user/run-debug.md).

## Database

Laravel's `DB_*` variables in `.env` are offered as a data source in the Database tool window.
See [Database tools](docs/guide/user/database.md).

## Settings | Languages & Frameworks | PHP | Laravel

![Laravel settings](docs/screenshots/laravel-settings.png)

| Option | Setting | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Read routes from | `laravel.routes.source` | `auto` |
| Complete routes, views, config, translations and model attributes | `laravel.completion.enabled` | on |
| Complete database columns in query builder calls | `laravel.completion.columns` | on |
| Complete values from ide.json files | `laravel.completion.ideJson` | on |
| Follow log files | `laravel.logs.follow` | on |
| Show route icons for controller actions | `laravel.gutter.routes` | on |
| Show view icons for `view()` calls and Blade includes | `laravel.gutter.views` | on |
| Additional Blade directives | `laravel.blade.customDirectives` | empty |

## Remote projects

In [remote projects](docs/guide/user/remote-development.md) the analysis runs in the Forge agent on the host
(completion, navigation and gutter icons cost one round trip), and artisan commands run on the
host.

# Symfony

The Symfony plugin (`forge.symfony`, PHPForge pack) activates in projects that require
`symfony/framework-bundle` or have `bin/console` together with `config/bundles.php`. It reads
the project statically and, when present, the compiled container in
`var/cache/<env>/*Container.xml`, which also knows the services and parameters of every bundle.

The status bar shows **Symfony 7.2 · dev** (version and kernel environment). Its menu has
**Show Routes**, **Show Services**, **Run Console Command…**, **Refresh Symfony Index** and
**Symfony Settings…**.

![Symfony status menu](docs/screenshots/symfony-status-menu.png)

## What Forge knows about the project

| Area | Read from |
| --- | --- |
| Services, aliases, `_defaults`, autowired `resource:` folders | `config/services*.yaml`, merged with the compiled container XML |
| Parameters | the same files |
| Routes | `#[Route]` attributes, legacy `@Route` annotations and YAML route files |
| Templates | `templates/` (setting `symfony.templatesDirectory`), and which controller renders which template |
| Twig tags, filters, functions and tests | Twig core, the Symfony bridge and the project's Twig extensions |
| Console commands | the project's commands (`src/`), then framework and bundle commands |
| Translations | `translations/<domain>.<locale>.{yaml,yml,xlf,xliff,php,json}` (also ICU files `<domain>+intl-icu.<locale>.*`); the folder, `default_locale` and `enabled_locales` come from `config/packages/{framework,translation}.yaml` |
| Form types | the core types and their options, plus the project's types: `configureOptions()` (`setDefaults`, `setDefined`, `setRequired`, `define`), `getParent()` and `data_class` |
| Event listeners | `getSubscribedEvents()` of event subscribers, `#[AsEventListener]` on classes and methods, `kernel.event_listener` tags in `config/services*.yaml`; the project's event classes and `*Events` constants |

The index is cached for a few seconds and rebuilt when files change; **Refresh Symfony Index**
rescans now.

## Completion and Go to Declaration

| Where | Completes and navigates to |
| --- | --- |
| `generateUrl('…')`, `redirectToRoute('…')`, `$router->generate('…')`, Twig `path('…')` / `url('…')` | route names |
| `render('…')`, `renderView`, Twig `{% extends %}`, `{% include %}`, `{% embed %}`, `{% import %}`, `{% from %}`, `{% use %}` | templates |
| `@service_id` in YAML, `#[Autowire(service: '…')]`, `$container->get('…')`, `service('…')` in PHP config | service ids |
| `%parameter%` in YAML, `getParameter('…')` | parameters |
| Twig files | tags, filters, functions, tests and variables |
| `->trans('…')`, `t('…')`, `new TranslatableMessage('…')`, Twig `{{ '…'\|trans }}`, `{% trans %}…{% endtrans %}`, Twig `t('…')` | translation keys of the domain (with the text of the default locale); `Ctrl+B` lists the key in every locale |
| the domain argument (`->trans('key', [], '…')`, `\|trans({}, '…')`, `{% trans from '…' %}`, `{% trans_default_domain '…' %}`) | translation domains |
| `->add('field', TextType::class, ['…' => …])` | the options of the form type, including inherited ones (`FormType`, `ChoiceType`, …) and the project type's own options |
| `->add('…')` in a form type with a `data_class` | the properties of the data class |
| `#[AsEventListener(event: '…')]`, `addListener('…')`, keys of `getSubscribedEvents()`, `event:` of a listener tag in YAML | event names (`kernel.*`, `console.*`, `form.*`, security events and the project's) |

![Twig completion](docs/screenshots/symfony-twig-completion.png)

![Twig filters](docs/screenshots/symfony-twig-filters.png)

`Ctrl+B` / `Ctrl+Click` on any of these opens the declaration (the controller action, the
template, the service definition or class, the parameter, the translation, the entity
property, the listeners of an event). `Ctrl+B` on `XType` in `createForm(XType::class)` or
`->add('field', XType::class)` opens the form type, and on a method name in
`getSubscribedEvents()` the listener method.

![Form option completion](docs/screenshots/symfony-form-options.png)

## Translations

![Translation keys folded to their text](docs/screenshots/symfony-translation-folding.png)

- **Folding:** translation keys show the text of the default locale in place of the key, like
  PHPStorm (`'order.title'|trans` reads `Order #%id%`). Put the caret on the text (or click it)
  to see and edit the key. Setting: **Show translated text in place of translation keys**
  (`symfony.translations.folding`).
- **Inspection:** a key that no catalogue of its domain has is a warning, a key missing in some
  of the domain's locales a weak warning (for example "Translation 'order.back' is missing for
  locale de"). Setting: **Report missing translation keys and locales**
  (`symfony.translations.inspection`).
- **Create translation key** (`Alt+Enter` on the key) adds the key to the domain's catalogues
  of the missing locales: nested under the existing parent keys in YAML, as a `<trans-unit>` in
  XLIFF (1.2 and 2.0), as an array entry in PHP and as a property in JSON. A locale without a
  catalogue gets a new `translations/<domain>.<locale>.<ext>` in the format the project uses
  most. The key is used as the text until you translate it.

![Translation key completion](docs/screenshots/symfony-translation-completion.png)

In `config/services*.yaml` (file type "Symfony Services"), service ids, parameters and tags are
completed, and `@service` and `%parameter%` references are highlighted.

## Line markers

With **Show line markers for routes, templates and commands** (`symfony.gutterIcons`):

- a **route** marker on controller actions (click: the route);
- **go to template** next to `render()` calls;
- **rendered by** on Twig templates (click: the controller);
- a **run** marker on console commands (click: run it);
- **listens to** on event listener methods (subscriber methods, `#[AsEventListener]`), with the
  priority (click: the event class);
- **N listeners** on the project's event classes, on event name constants and on
  `->dispatch(new XEvent(…))` calls (click: the listener, or a chooser when there are several).

## Symfony tool window

The **Symfony** tool window (bottom) has five tabs:

| Tab | Columns | Filter |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Routes | Name, Method, Path, Controller | name, path or controller |
| Services | Service ID, Class, Tags (public/private icon) | id, class or tag |
| Parameters | Name, Value | parameter |
| Translations | Key, Domain, one column per locale (missing texts are marked) | key or text, domain, **Only missing** |
| Events | Event, Listener, Priority, Registered by (subscriber, `#[AsEventListener]`, `services.yaml`) | event or listener |

Clicking a row opens its definition (in the Translations tab: double-click a locale's cell to
open the key in that catalogue).

![Symfony translations](docs/screenshots/symfony-translations-tab.png)

![Symfony events](docs/screenshots/symfony-events.png)

![Symfony routes](docs/screenshots/symfony-routes.png)

![Symfony services](docs/screenshots/symfony-services.png)

## Run Console Command

**Run Console Command…** (Find Action, the status bar menu or the tool window) opens a popup:
type a command name, `Tab` completes it, arguments after the name are passed on, `Enter` runs
it with `bin/console` (setting `symfony.consolePath`) in the configured environment.

![Console command](docs/screenshots/symfony-console.png)

The output is shown in the Symfony tool window with **Rerun** and **Close**.

![Console output](docs/screenshots/symfony-console-run.png)

## Settings | Languages & Frameworks | PHP | Symfony

![Symfony settings](docs/screenshots/symfony-settings.png)

| Option | Setting | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Environment (`dev`, `test`, `prod`) — kernel environment for the compiled container and console commands | `symfony.environment` | `dev` |
| App directory — scanned for controllers, commands and Twig extensions | `symfony.appDirectory` | `src` |
| Templates directory | `symfony.templatesDirectory` | `templates` |
| Console — path to the console script | `symfony.consolePath` | `bin/console` |
| Container XML — empty: `var/cache/<environment>/*Container.xml` | `symfony.containerXml` | empty |
| Show line markers for routes, templates and commands | `symfony.gutterIcons` | on |
| Complete Twig tags, filters and functions | `symfony.twigCompletion` | on |
| Show translated text in place of translation keys | `symfony.translations.folding` | on |
| Report missing translation keys and locales | `symfony.translations.inspection` | on |

The project settings (environment, folders, console, container) can be stored per project.

## Doctrine

Symfony projects usually use Doctrine; see [Doctrine and DQL](docs/guide/user/doctrine.md). Symfony's
`DATABASE_URL` in `.env` is offered as a data source in the [Database](docs/guide/user/database.md) tool window.

In [remote projects](docs/guide/user/remote-development.md) the analysis runs in the Forge agent on the host and
console commands run there as well.

# WordPress

The WordPress plugin (`forge.wordpress`, PHPForge pack) activates in projects that use
WordPress:

| Project | Recognised by |
| --- | --- |
| A WordPress site | `wp-config.php`, `wp-config-sample.php` or `wp-includes/` (the version comes from `wp-includes/version.php`) |
| A Composer install (Bedrock and similar) | a `composer.json` that requires `johnpbloch/wordpress…` or any `roots/*` package |
| A content folder | `wp-content/` |
| A plugin | a PHP file in the project root with a `Plugin Name:` header |
| A theme | a `style.css` with a `Theme Name:` header |

The status bar shows the WordPress icon. Settings live in **Settings | Languages & Frameworks |
PHP | WordPress**.

![WordPress hooks tool window](docs/screenshots/wordpress-hooks.png)

## Hooks

Forge indexes every `add_action`, `add_filter`, `do_action`, `apply_filters` (plus the
`_ref_array` and `_deprecated` variants), `remove_action` / `remove_filter` /
`remove_all_*`, `has_action` / `has_filter`, `did_action` and `doing_action` call of the
project's PHP files (`vendor/` and `node_modules/` excluded). When the project contains
WordPress itself, the core hooks are indexed too.

Hook names built from variables are kept as patterns: `do_action( "save_post_{$post->post_type}" )`
fires for `add_action( 'save_post_book', … )`, and `'manage_' . $screen . '_columns'`
becomes `manage_{$screen}_columns`.

| Where | What Forge does |
| --- | --- |
| The hook name in `add_action( '…' )`, `do_action( '…' )`, … | **Completion** of hook names: the project's hooks first (actions in action functions, filters in filter functions; for registrations the hooks that fire), then frequently used WordPress core hooks with a short summary |
| `Ctrl+B` / `Ctrl+Click` on a registered hook name | the `do_action` / `apply_filters` calls that fire it |
| `Ctrl+B` on a fired hook name | the registered callbacks (`add_action`, `add_filter`) |
| `Ctrl+B` on a callback name (`'acme_boot'`, `[ $this, 'register' ]`) | the function or method |
| `Ctrl+B` on a WordPress function (`add_action`, `get_option`) | its declaration in the WordPress stubs, when they are installed |
| `Alt+F7` / `Ctrl+Alt+F7` on a hook name | **Find Usages**: every registration, invocation, removal and check, grouped as *Hook registration*, *Hook invocation* and *Function call* in the Find tool window |

![Hook name completion](docs/screenshots/wordpress-hook-completion.png)

![Find Usages of a hook](docs/screenshots/wordpress-usages.png)

`Ctrl+B` on the pattern `"acme_events_label_{$date}"` lands on the `add_filter(
'acme_events_label_2026-12-24', … )` it runs:

![Go to Declaration on a dynamic hook](docs/screenshots/wordpress-goto-hook.png)

### Gutter icons

With **Show gutter icons for hooks** (`wordpress.gutterIcons`):

- an **anchor** next to each `add_action` / `add_filter`: "Action 'init' is fired in 2
  places" (click: go there), "WordPress core action 'init': …" for core hooks the project
  does not contain, or "… is not fired in the project";
- a **lightning bolt** next to each `do_action` / `apply_filters`: "3 callbacks for
  'save_post'" (click: the callbacks; several open a chooser).

With Code Vision on (Settings | Editor | Inlay Hints), "fired in 2 places" and "3 callbacks"
also appear above the line.

![Hook gutter icons](docs/screenshots/wordpress-gutter.png)

### WordPress tool window

**View | Tool Windows | WordPress** (or **Tools | WordPress | Show Hooks**) lists the project's
hooks with their kind, the number of registered callbacks and invocations and where they fire.
Filter by name or file and by **All / Actions / Filters**; double-click opens where the hook
fires. The toolbar shows how WP-CLI is run and whether the stubs are installed; the footer
says what was detected (site, plugin, theme) and how many files were indexed.
**Refresh** rescans (the index is otherwise reused for a few seconds).

![WordPress tool window, light theme](docs/screenshots/wordpress-hooks-light.png)

## WordPress stubs

Go to Declaration on WordPress functions uses
[`php-stubs/wordpress-stubs`](https://packagist.org/packages/php-stubs/wordpress-stubs) when it
is installed in `vendor/`. Forge never ships the stubs. When they are missing, a notification
offers **Install with Composer** (`composer require --dev php-stubs/wordpress-stubs`, run
through the Run tool window, so you see what happens) or **Don't ask again**
(`wordpress.offerStubs`). **Tools | WordPress | Install WordPress Stubs…** does the same later.

## WP-CLI

**Tools | WP-CLI…** opens the [Command Line Tools Console](docs/guide/user/command-line-tools.md) with `wp `
typed in: commands, subcommands, options and their values complete from `wp cli cmd-dump`,
which Forge caches in its cache folder until `composer.lock` changes. Forge finds WP-CLI as
`vendor/bin/wp` or `wp-cli.phar` in the project, else `wp` on `PATH`; configure another path in
**Settings | Tools | Command Line Tool Support**.

![WP-CLI in the Command Line Tools Console](docs/screenshots/wordpress-wp-cli.png)

WP-CLI runs project code, so it is refused while the project is in
[Safe Mode](docs/guide/user/project-trust.md).

## Code style

**Settings | Editor | Code Style | PHP › Set from… › WordPress** applies the WordPress Coding
Standards layout: tabs, spaces inside parentheses (`foo( $bar )`), long array syntax, braces
at the end of the line and spaces around concatenation.

The Yoda condition rule is an inspection: with **Suggest Yoda conditions**
(`wordpress.yodaConditions`) a comparison like `$status === 'publish'` gets a weak warning
"Use Yoda condition", and `Alt+Enter` › **Flip to Yoda condition** turns it into
`'publish' === $status`. Only simple comparisons are reported: a variable (with property and
array access) against a string, a number, `true`, `false` or `null` with `==`, `!=`, `===`
or `!==`.

![Yoda condition quick-fix](docs/screenshots/wordpress-yoda.png)

## File templates

**File | New** offers two WordPress templates in WordPress projects (see
[File templates](docs/guide/user/file-templates.md)):

| Template | Creates |
| --- | --- |
| **WordPress Plugin** | `<name>.php` with the plugin header (`Plugin Name`, `Version`, `Requires at least`, `Requires PHP`, `Author`, `License`, `Text Domain`), the `ABSPATH` guard and an `init` callback |
| **WordPress Theme Stylesheet** | `style.css` with the theme header (`Theme Name` from the project name, `Text Domain`, …) |

## Settings

| Setting | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `wordpress.hookCompletion` | on | Complete hook names in hook functions |
| `wordpress.gutterIcons` | on | Gutter icons on registrations and invocations |
| `wordpress.yodaConditions` | on | The "Use Yoda condition" weak warning |
| `wordpress.offerStubs` | on | Offer to install the WordPress stubs (per project) |

See also: [Drupal, Joomla and Shopware](docs/guide/user/cms.md), [PHP](docs/guide/user/php.md),
[Code style](docs/guide/user/editor.md), [Command Line Tool Support](docs/guide/user/command-line-tools.md).

# Drupal, Joomla and Shopware

One plugin, **Drupal, Joomla and Shopware** (`forge.cms`, PHPForge pack), covers the basics
of the three CMS. It is a single plugin because each part is small and shares detection and
the run actions; it activates only when the project uses one of them. WordPress has its own,
larger plugin: see [WordPress](docs/guide/user/wordpress.md).

## Detection

| CMS | Recognised by |
| --- | --- |
| Drupal | `drupal/core`, `drupal/core-recommended` (composer.json or composer.lock), `core/lib/Drupal.php` (also below `web/`), or a module / theme / profile with a `<name>.info.yml` that has `core_version_requirement` |
| Joomla | `administrator/manifests/files/joomla.xml` (with the version), or an extension's XML manifest `<extension type="component|module|plugin|template|package">` in the project root |
| Shopware 6 | `shopware/core`, `shopware/platform` or `shopware/storefront` in composer.json (the version from composer.lock), or a plugin with `"type": "shopware-platform-plugin"` |
| Shopware 5 | `engine/Shopware/Kernel.php` |

The status bar shows the CMS with its icon and version (for example **Drupal 11**); clicking it
opens Settings | Plugins. Settings live in **Settings | Languages & Frameworks | PHP | Drupal,
Joomla and Shopware**.

## File types and templates

| Files | Opened as |
| --- | --- |
| Drupal `*.module`, `*.install`, `*.theme`, `*.profile`, `*.engine`, `*.inc` | PHP (while the plugin is active) |
| Drupal `*.info.yml`, `*.routing.yml`, `*.services.yml`, `*.libraries.yml` | YAML |
| Drupal and Shopware 6 `*.html.twig` | Twig over HTML; Shopware's `sw_extends`, `sw_include`, `sw_icon`, `sw_thumbnails` and `sw_silent_feature_call` are highlighted as tags |
| Shopware 5 `*.tpl` | Smarty |
| Joomla extension manifests (`*.xml`) | XML |

See [File types](docs/guide/user/file-types.md) and the template data languages there.

## Drupal hooks

In a module's `.module`, `.install`, `.theme`, `.profile` or `.inc` file, typing a function
name after `function` completes **hook implementations** named `<module>_<hook>`: the module
is the nearest folder with an `.info.yml` (else the file name). Choosing one inserts the
hook's parameters and an empty body, for example

```php
function acme_tools_form_alter(&$form, \Drupal\Core\Form\FormStateInterface $form_state, $form_id) {

}
```

The list holds about 45 frequently used core hooks (`hook_form_alter`,
`hook_form_FORM_ID_alter`, `hook_theme`, `hook_preprocess_HOOK`, `hook_entity_presave`,
`hook_ENTITY_TYPE_insert`, `hook_cron`, `hook_install`, `hook_update_N`, …), each with a short
summary written for Forge.

![Drupal hook completion](docs/screenshots/drupal-hook-completion.png)

Existing implementations, including the ones with placeholders (`acme_tools_form_user_login_form_alter`
implements `hook_form_FORM_ID_alter`, `acme_tools_node_presave` `hook_ENTITY_TYPE_presave`), get
a **book** icon in the gutter ("Implements hook_form_alter(): …"). Clicking it, or `Ctrl+B` on
the function name, opens the hook's documentation: the `hook_…` function in the project's own
`*.api.php` files (Drupal core ships them), else the hook's page on api.drupal.org.

| Setting | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `cms.drupal.hookCompletion` | on | Complete hook implementations after `function` |
| `cms.drupal.gutterIcons` | on | Gutter icons on hook implementations |

## Drush and the Shopware console

| Action | Opens |
| --- | --- |
| **Tools \| Drush…** | the [Command Line Tools Console](docs/guide/user/command-line-tools.md) with `drush ` typed in (Drush from `vendor/bin/drush`, else `drush` on `PATH`) |
| **Tools \| Shopware Console…** | the same console with the alias of `bin/console` typed in (Symfony Console format) |

Commands, options and arguments complete from the tool's own command list, cached in Forge's
cache folder. Both run project code and are refused while the project is in
[Safe Mode](docs/guide/user/project-trust.md).

See also: [WordPress](docs/guide/user/wordpress.md), [Symfony](docs/guide/user/symfony.md), [PHP](docs/guide/user/php.md).

Source: docs/guide/user/doctrine.md

# Doctrine and DQL

The Doctrine plugin (`forge.doctrine`, PHPForge pack) activates in projects that require
`doctrine/orm`, with or without Symfony.

## Entity mappings

Forge reads entity mappings from:

- PHP 8 attributes (`#[ORM\Entity]`, `#[ORM\Column]`, `#[ORM\ManyToOne]`, …),
- legacy docblock annotations (`@ORM\Entity`, `@ORM\Column`, …) when a class has no mapping
  attributes (setting **Read legacy @ORM annotations**, `doctrine.annotations`),
- XML (`*.orm.xml`) and YAML (`*.orm.yml`) mapping files,

including embeddables, mapped superclasses, fields with type, column, length, nullable,
unique, id and generated flags, and associations (`ManyToOne`, `OneToMany`, `ManyToMany`,
`OneToOne`) with `mappedBy`/`inversedBy`. Repositories are linked to their entity.

## Doctrine tool window

The **Doctrine** tool window (right stripe) lists every entity with its table, fields and
associations. Filter by entity or field name; click an entry to open its declaration;
**Refresh** re-reads the mappings (also **Refresh Doctrine Entities** in Find Action).

![Doctrine entities](docs/screenshots/doctrine-entities.png)

## DQL in PHP strings

DQL is recognized inside:

- `createQuery('…')`, including concatenated strings, heredocs and `Entity::class`
  interpolation;
- QueryBuilder calls such as `select`, `from`, `join`/`leftJoin`/`innerJoin`, `where`/`andWhere`/
  `orWhere`, `orderBy`, `groupBy`, `having`, and `expr()` fragments, with the aliases that the
  builder chain declares (`createQueryBuilder('o')`, `join('o.customer', 'c')`).

There it provides:

| Feature | Setting |
| --- | --- |
| DQL highlighting of keywords, entities, aliases, fields, parameters | `doctrine.dqlInjection` |
| Completion of entities, aliases, fields, associations, embedded fields, keywords and functions | `doctrine.dqlCompletion` |
| Warnings for unknown entities and fields | `doctrine.dqlInspections` |
| `Ctrl+B` on an entity, alias or field opens its mapping | — |

![DQL completion in a QueryBuilder chain](docs/screenshots/symfony-dql-querybuilder.png)

![DQL completion in createQuery](docs/screenshots/symfony-dql-completion.png)

The highlighting is computed in the background shortly after each edit, so it may lag a
keystroke behind while you type.

## Line markers

Entities and repositories get gutter icons that link them: entity → repository and
repository → entity.

## Settings | Languages & Frameworks | PHP | Doctrine

![Doctrine settings](docs/screenshots/doctrine-settings.png)

| Option | Setting | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Entity source directories — scanned for `#[ORM\Entity]` classes and repositories | `doctrine.sourceDirectories` | `src` |
| Mapping file directories — `*.orm.xml` and `*.orm.yml` | `doctrine.mappingDirectories` | `config/doctrine`, `src/Resources/config/doctrine` |
| Read legacy @ORM annotations | `doctrine.annotations` | on |
| Highlight DQL in createQuery() and QueryBuilder strings | `doctrine.dqlInjection` | on |
| Complete entities, aliases and fields in DQL | `doctrine.dqlCompletion` | on |
| Report unknown entities and fields | `doctrine.dqlInspections` | on |

The directory settings and annotations can be stored per project.

In [remote projects](docs/guide/user/remote-development.md) the mappings are read by the Forge agent on the
host; everything above works the same.

# WebForge

The **WebForge** pack brings web development to Forge. Its plugins activate per project:

| Plugin | Id | Active for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| HTML, CSS & JavaScript | `forge.web` | projects with JavaScript, TypeScript, HTML or CSS |
| React | `forge.react` | `react` or `next` in `package.json` |
| Vue.js | `forge.vue` | `vue` or `nuxt` |
| Angular | `forge.angular` | `@angular/core` or `angular.json` |

Editing intelligence comes from the web language servers of the catalog: TypeScript
(`typescript-language-server` or `vtsls`), Vue (Volar), the Angular Language Service, HTML,
CSS, ESLint and Tailwind CSS. Install them from Settings | Languages & Frameworks |
**TypeScript** (the "Language Services" list) or the Language Servers page. See
[Language servers](docs/guide/user/language-servers.md).

## npm scripts

### npm tool window

The **npm** tool window (left stripe) lists every `package.json` of the project (also in
workspaces and sub-folders) with its scripts and the package manager it uses.

![npm tool window](docs/screenshots/webforge-npm-tool-window.png)

- **Double-click** a script to run it. It runs as a temporary **npm** run configuration in the
  Run tool window.
- The toolbar has **Reload Scripts**, **Run**, **Debug**, **Expand All**, **Collapse All** and
  **Settings**; the context menu has **Jump to Source**.
- **Install Dependencies** (Find Action) runs the package manager's install in the root
  package.

![Running a script](docs/screenshots/webforge-npm-run.png)

### Run icons in package.json

Every script in `package.json` gets a ▶ icon in the gutter (setting
`web.npm.gutterIcons`). Click it for **Run** and **Debug**.

![Gutter menu](docs/screenshots/webforge-npm-gutter-menu.png)

### Package managers

The package manager of a package is chosen from, in this order:

1. Settings | Languages & Frameworks | Node.js | **Package manager** (`web.packageManager`)
   when it is not `auto`;
2. the `packageManager` field of `package.json` (e.g. `pnpm@9.15.4`);
3. a lock file in the package's folder or a parent: `pnpm-lock.yaml`, `yarn.lock`,
   `bun.lock`/`bun.lockb`, `package-lock.json`;
4. npm.

npm, pnpm, yarn and bun are supported. Script arguments are passed after `--` for npm only.

### Debugging scripts

**Debug** on an npm script sets `NODE_OPTIONS` to the value of **Node options when debugging
scripts** (`web.npm.debugArguments`, default `--inspect`). Attach Chrome DevTools
(`chrome://inspect`) or another inspector client to the printed port.

> **Note:** Forge has no built-in JavaScript debugger yet; Debug only starts Node with the
> inspector enabled.

### Settings | Languages & Frameworks | Node.js

![Node.js settings](docs/screenshots/webforge-settings-node.png)

| Option | Setting | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Package manager (`auto`, `npm`, `pnpm`, `yarn`, `bun`) | `web.packageManager` | `auto` |
| Show run icons next to scripts in package.json | `web.npm.gutterIcons` | on |
| Node options when debugging scripts | `web.npm.debugArguments` | `--inspect` |

## Component navigation

`Ctrl+B` / `Ctrl+Click` resolves components through your imports (relative paths,
`tsconfig`/`jsconfig` `paths` aliases, index files, barrel re-exports and **workspace
packages** imported by name — resolved through their `package.json` `exports`, `module`, `main`
or `types`, falling back to the sources when `dist/` is not built) before the language server
is asked. Several targets open the **Choose Declaration** popup. Turn it off with Settings | Languages & Frameworks | TypeScript | **Navigate
from JSX and template tags to components, props and events** (`web.navigation.components`).

### React

- On `<UserCard` in JSX: opens the component (function or class component, also anonymous
  default exports such as `export default () => …`, which are named after their file).
- On a prop (`title=`): opens the prop's declaration.
- On a component's own name: lists the JSX tags that use it (**Usages of …**).

![React Go to Declaration](docs/screenshots/webforge-react-goto.png)

![React usages](docs/screenshots/webforge-react-usages.png)

### Vue.js

Single-file components with `<script setup>` or the Options API:

- `<UserCard>` and `<user-card>` resolve through the script's imports, barrel files, or
  project-wide (global registration, Nuxt auto-imports);
- `:title` and `@select` go to the prop or emit;
- on a component's own name or block tag: its usages.

![Vue navigation](docs/screenshots/webforge-vue-goto.png)

### Angular

- Element and attribute selectors in templates go to the component or directive.
- `[input]` and `(output)` bindings go to the input or output (decorators or signal
  functions).
- `| pipe` goes to the pipe.
- `templateUrl` and `styleUrls`/`styleUrl` strings open the files (**Choose Stylesheet** when
  there are several).
- **Line markers** link a component class with its template and styles, and a template back
  to its component (setting **Show line markers between components, templates and styles**,
  `angular.gutterIcons`).

![Angular gutter](docs/screenshots/webforge-angular-gutter.png)

![Angular template navigation](docs/screenshots/webforge-angular-template.png)

When several targets match, a **Choose Declaration** popup lists them.

## Refactoring

### Extract Component

Select whole elements of a Vue `<template>` or JSX elements in a React component and choose
Refactor | Extract/Introduce | **Component…** (also in Refactor This, `Ctrl+Alt+Shift+T`, and
`Alt+Enter`). The dialog asks for the component name (PascalCase) and the directory and shows
the props the new component gets: every name the markup takes from its parent (`{{ total }}`,
`:user="user"`, `@click="save"`, `{items.map(...)}`, `onClick={() => remove(item)}`). Names
bound inside the selection (`v-for` aliases, slot props, arrow function parameters) are not
props, and components and helpers the parent imports are imported by the new component
(relative imports are rewritten for its folder).

- **Vue**: a new `.vue` file with the markup in its `<template>` and `defineProps([...])` in a
  `<script setup>` (the `lang` of the parent's script), or `props` / `components` for the
  Options API. The parent renders `<NewComponent :total="total" />` and imports it (Options API:
  also registers it in `components`).
- **React**: a new `.jsx` / `.tsx` file with `export default function NewComponent({ ... })`
  returning the markup (several elements are wrapped in `<>…</>`, TypeScript gets a props
  interface). The parent renders `<NewComponent total={total} />` and imports it in its own
  import style.

The new file and the parent's changes are one undo step; **Preview** shows them first. The
analysis is Forge's own (Rust), so it needs no language server and works in remote projects.

![Extract Component (Vue)](docs/screenshots/extract-component-vue-dialog.png)

![The extracted React component](docs/screenshots/extract-component-react-result.png)

### Language server refactorings

In JavaScript and TypeScript files Refactor This adds the refactorings of the TypeScript
language server for the caret or selection, worded like PHPStorm where it has its own name:
**Extract Method** (function in module scope, method in class), **Introduce Constant**,
**Extract Type Alias** / **Extract Interface**, **Inline Variable**, **Move to New File**,
**Convert to function declaration** / **expression**, and the conversions the server offers as
they are (convert to arrow function, async function, template string, destructured parameters
or object, named / namespace imports, optional chain). `Alt+Enter` shows them with the same
wording. Introduce Variable, Extract Method and Inline (`Ctrl+Alt+V`, `Ctrl+Alt+M`,
`Ctrl+Alt+N`) use the server's refactorings directly.

![Refactor This on JSX](docs/screenshots/refactor-this-react.png)

| Option | Setting | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Navigate from JSX and template tags to components, props and events | `web.navigation.components` | on |
| Show line markers between components, templates and styles (Angular) | `angular.gutterIcons` | on |

Below these options, **Language Services** shows the web language servers (JavaScript &
TypeScript, Vue, Angular, HTML & CSS) with the same controls as the Language Servers page.

# LuaForge

**LuaForge** (plugin `forge.lua`) supports Lua 5.1–5.4 and LuaJIT, LÖVE games and Neovim
configurations and plugins. It activates in [Lua projects](docs/guide/getting-started/project-detection.md):
Lua files in the root, two or more in a folder, `.luarc.json`, `.luacheckrc`, `stylua.toml`,
`selene.toml` or a `*.rockspec`. LÖVE is detected from `conf.lua` (or a `main.lua` using
`love.`), Neovim from `init.lua` next to `lua/`, or `lua/` + `plugin/`.

## The Lua index

Forge indexes every Lua file in Rust (also in [remote projects](docs/guide/user/remote-development.md)):
locals with their scopes, parameters, globals, table fields, functions and methods
(`function M.f`, `function M:f`, `M.f = function`), `require` calls and each module's `return`.
Doc comments (`---`) are parsed as EmmyLua/LuaLS annotations: `@class`, `@field`, `@param`,
`@return`, `@type`, `@alias` (with `---|` values), `@deprecated`, `@see`.

Types are followed across files: `---@class`, `---@type`, `---@param`, the `---@return` of
called functions (`Class.new()` without annotations returns the class), `setmetatable` and class
parents.

**Reindex Lua Files** (Find Action) rebuilds the index.

### Modules and `require`

`require("a.b")` is resolved through `package.path`-like templates, in this order:
Settings | Languages & Frameworks | Lua | **Module search paths** (`lua.requirePaths`, e.g.
`scripts/?.lua`), `runtime.path` from `.luarc.json`, then `?.lua`, `?/init.lua`, `lua/?.lua`,
`src/?.lua` and `lib/?.lua`.

## Navigation and search

- `Ctrl+B` / `Ctrl+Click` on a local, global, field, method or `require` string opens its
  declaration (tried before lua-language-server).
- **Go to Class** (`Ctrl+N`) finds `---@class` types, aliases and modules; **Go to Symbol**
  (`Ctrl+Alt+Shift+N`) finds functions and fields.
- **Structure** (`Alt+7`) shows the functions, tables and classes of the current file.

![Go to require](docs/screenshots/lua-goto-require.png)

![Structure](docs/screenshots/lua-structure.png)

## Hover documentation

Hovering shows the signature and annotations of functions, classes and fields. When
lua-language-server runs and answers, its hover is shown instead.

![Lua hover](docs/screenshots/lua-hover.png)

## lua-language-server

lua-language-server comes from the [language server catalog](docs/guide/user/language-servers.md). Install it
with your package manager (`brew install lua-language-server`, `sudo pacman -S
lua-language-server`) or from its releases.

| Option (Settings | Languages & Frameworks | Lua) | Setting | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Lua environment: `auto`, `plain`, `love`, `neovim` — adds the APIs of LÖVE (`love.*`) or Neovim (`vim.*`); `auto` detects them from the project | `langservers.lua.environment` | `auto` |
| Lua version (Lua 5.1–5.4, LuaJIT), used with plain Lua; LÖVE and Neovim run LuaJIT | `langservers.lua.version` | Lua 5.4 |
| lua-language-server executable (empty: PATH, Mason or Forge's server folder) | `langservers.servers.lua-language-server.path` | empty |
| Library paths (`workspace.library`), e.g. `~/.luarocks/share/lua/5.4` | `langservers.lua.libraries` | empty |

## StyLua

**Reformat Code** (`Ctrl+Alt+L`) formats Lua files with StyLua when it is installed; the
project's `stylua.toml` is honoured. Without one, StyLua gets the Lua
[code style](docs/guide/user/editor.md#code-style) (indent, hard wrap, quotes, call parentheses, simple
statements on one line) on its command line. Settings: **Reformat Code with StyLua**
(`lua.stylua.enabled`, on) and **StyLua executable** (`lua.stylua.path`, `stylua`). In a
[remote project](docs/guide/user/remote-development.md) StyLua runs on the host (install it there).

## Running Lua

Files with a main chunk get a ▶ icon in the gutter, and `Ctrl+Shift+F10` runs the current
file. Both create a **Lua Script** run configuration that runs
`<interpreter> <interpreter options> <file> <arguments>`. The interpreter defaults to
Settings | Languages & Frameworks | Lua | **Lua interpreter** (`lua.interpreter`, `lua`; e.g.
`luajit`, `love` or a full path). LÖVE games run as `love <dir>`.

![Run Lua](docs/screenshots/lua-run.png)

## Settings summary

![Lua settings](docs/screenshots/lua-settings.png)

See the [settings reference](docs/guide/reference/settings.md#languages--frameworks--lua) for every key.
