# Git

The Git plugin (`forge.git`) drives the `git` command line (no libgit2) and works in any project
that is a Git repository (also when the project is a sub-folder of the repository). The
current branch is shown in the main toolbar and the status bar.

## Get from VCS

**Git ▸ Clone…** (`Git.Clone`), **VCS ▸ Get from Version Control…** / **File ▸ New ▸ Project
from Version Control…** (`Vcs.Checkout`) and **Get from VCS** on the Welcome screen open **Get
from Version Control**:

![Get from Version Control](docs/screenshots/git-clone-url.png)

- **Repository URL**: the URL (`https://…`, `git@host:owner/repo.git`, `ssh://…` or a local
  path) and the **Directory** (by default `<Settings | System | default project directory>/<name
  from the URL>`; the folder button picks another one). **Test** runs `git ls-remote` and shows
  "Connection successful" or git's error.
- **GitHub**, **GitLab** and **Forgejo / Gitea** list the repositories of your
  [code host accounts](docs/guide/user/code-hosts.md) (owned, member and collaborator repositories, recently
  active first) with a search field; double-click a repository to clone it. Without an account
  the page offers **Log In…**.

  ![Repositories of an account](docs/screenshots/git-clone-account.png)

- **Clone to**: **This computer**, the host of the open remote project or a saved SSH
  connection (Settings | Tools | SSH Configurations). Remote clones run `git clone` on that host
  through the Forge agent; the folder button browses the host.
- **Clone** shows git's progress (Receiving objects, Resolving deltas, …) with **Cancel**; a
  cancelled clone removes the half-cloned folder. Afterwards the project opens; with a project
  open, Forge asks **Open Project** (**This Window**; **New Window** comes with several project
  windows).

![Clone progress](docs/screenshots/git-clone-progress.png)

Credentials: for HTTPS URLs on the server of one of your code host accounts, Forge gives git
that account's token (from the OS keychain) for this one `git clone` / `git ls-remote` through a
`-c credential.helper=…` that reads it from the environment. Nothing is written to git config or
a credential store, and the token is never on the command line. SSH URLs use your SSH keys and
SSH agent (on a remote host: the host's keys and agent); Forge never asks for passwords in a
terminal, so a missing key fails with git's message.

## Commit tool window

**Commit…** (`Ctrl+K`, macOS `Cmd+K`) opens the **Commit** tool window (`Alt+0`, left stripe).

![Commit tool window](docs/screenshots/vcs-commit.png)

- The changes are listed in their [changelists](#changelists) (**Changes** is the default
  one) and **Unversioned Files**, as trees grouped by folder. Tick the files to include; new
  changes of the active changelist are ticked. Double-click a file (or **Show Diff**,
  `Ctrl+D`) to see its diff.
- Toolbar: **Refresh** (`Ctrl+F5`), **Rollback…** (`Ctrl+Alt+Z`, discards the changes of the
  selected files after a confirmation), **Show Diff**, **Expand All**, **Collapse All**,
  **New Changelist…**.
- Write the **Commit Message**. **Amend** amends the last commit (its message is loaded).
  **Sign-off** adds a `Signed-off-by` line (`git commit --signoff`; the same option as
  Settings | Version Control | Git | Sign-off commits).
- **Commit** (`Ctrl+Enter` in the message) or **Commit and Push…**. The gear next to them
  opens the [Commit Options](#commit-options-and-commit-checks).
- While there are shelved changes or stashes, the header shows the tabs **Changes**, **Shelf**
  and **Stash** (see [Shelf](#shelf) and [Stash](#stash)).

![Commit message inspections](docs/screenshots/vcs-commit-inspections.png)

While you type, the message is checked like in PHPStorm (Settings | Version Control | Git |
Commit Message Inspections): the subject line is at most `vcs.git.commit.subjectMaxLength`
characters (72), a blank line separates subject and body
(`vcs.git.commit.blankLineAfterSubject`) and body lines stay within
`vcs.git.commit.bodyRightMargin` columns (72). Problems are listed below the message; they do
not block the commit. Lines starting with `#` are ignored. Typos and grammar problems in the
message are underlined and listed too, with their fixes on click (see
[Spelling and grammar](docs/guide/user/spelling-and-grammar.md#commit-messages)).

Before committing files with Windows line separators (CRLF), Forge asks whether to **Commit As
Is** (`vcs.git.commit.warnOnCrlf`), unless git converts them itself (`core.autocrlf` is `true`
or `input`).

> **Note:** "Commit Message History" (`Ctrl+M`) is not available yet.

### Changelists

![Changelists](docs/screenshots/git-changelists.png)

Changelists group local changes, like in PHPStorm. **Changes** is the default changelist; the
**active** changelist is shown in bold and receives new changes. Forge keeps the changelists
per project in its data directory (`changelists.json`, see
[File locations](docs/guide/reference/file-locations.md)), never in the project, and git knows
nothing about them.

- **New Changelist…** (toolbar, context menu, Git ▸ Uncommitted Changes): name, comment and
  **Set active**. The comment of the active changelist becomes the commit message draft.
- Right-click a changelist: **Commit…** (ticks exactly its files), **Rollback…**,
  **Edit Changelist…** (also double-click), **Delete Changelist** (its changes move to the
  active list; the active list cannot be deleted), **Set Active Changelist**,
  **Shelve Changes…** and **Create Patch…**.
- **Move to Another Changelist…** (`F6` in the Commit tool window, file context menu) moves
  the selected file to an existing or a new changelist. Files can also be **dragged** onto a
  changelist.

![Move to Another Changelist](docs/screenshots/git-move-to-changelist.png)

Settings | Version Control | Changelists | **Create changelists automatically**
(`vcs.changelists.createAutomatically`, on by default): applied patches and unshelved changes
go to a new changelist named after the patch or the shelved changes.

### Partial commits

Single changes (hunks) of a file can be committed while the rest stays local, like PHPStorm's
partial commits:

- While the Commit tool window is open, the editor shows a checkbox at every change of a
  tracked file (next to the [change markers](#change-markers)). Untick a change to leave it
  out of the next commit. Unsaved edits count.
- The diff of a file opened from the Commit tool window has the same checkboxes.
- A partly included file shows a half-ticked checkbox in the Commit tool window.
- Click a change marker and choose **Move to Another Changelist…** to move only that change;
  the file then shows in both changelists with the number of its changes in each. Changes moved
  to a list that is not active are left out of the commit.

![Partial commit checkboxes in the editor](docs/screenshots/git-partial-commit-gutter.png)

![Partial commit in the diff](docs/screenshots/git-partial-commit-diff.png)

Forge builds the commit in the index without touching your files: it saves what was staged,
writes the committed version of each partly included file (HEAD plus the included changes),
commits, then restores the index, so the excluded changes stay local changes. This works in
remote projects too, since git runs on the project's host.

### Commit options and commit checks

![Commit Options](docs/screenshots/git-commit-options.png)

The gear next to **Commit and Push…** opens the **Commit Options**:

- **Git**: **Author** (`Name <email>` for this commit only), **Sign-off commit**,
  **Amend commit** and **Run Git hooks** (off commits with `--no-verify`, so `pre-commit` and
  `commit-msg` hooks are skipped).
- **Commit Checks**, run on the ticked files before committing:
  - **Reformat code**, **Rearrange code**, **Optimize imports** and **Cleanup** change the
    files like the [Actions on Save](docs/guide/user/actions-on-save.md) (Reformat uses the formatter of the
    file type; the other three are PHP actions);
  - **Analyze code** collects the errors and warnings of the language servers and
    inspections. When there are any, Forge asks: *"N errors and M warnings found"* —
    **Review** (opens the Problems tool window and does not commit) or **Commit Anyway**;
  - **Check TODO** looks for TODO items (the patterns of the [TODO](docs/guide/user/todo.md) tool window) in
    the added and changed lines, with **Review** (opens the TODO tool window) or
    **Commit Anyway**.
- **Advanced Commit Checks**: **Run Tests** runs the chosen run configuration and asks
  **Review** or **Commit Anyway** when it fails.

The checks are settings (Settings | Version Control | Commit, `vcs.commit.*`), so they stay as
you leave them. "Update copyright" is not available.

### Commit Message History

**Commit Message History** (`Ctrl+M`, macOS `Cmd+M`, in the commit message, or the clock icon
above it; `Vcs.ShowMessageHistory`) lists recent messages: the ones committed from Forge in this
project, then your own recent commits (`git log --author=<your email>`). Type to filter, `Up` /
`Down` select (the preview shows the whole message), `Enter` or a click puts the message into
the commit message, `Escape` closes the popup.

![Commit Message History](docs/screenshots/git-message-history.png)

The history is kept per project in Forge's data directory
(`<data dir>/forge/projects/<project>/commit-messages.json`), never in the project. Settings |
Version Control | Commit | **Commit message history size** (`vcs.commit.messageHistorySize`,
20) limits it.

### Signing commits with GPG or SSH keys

Settings | Version Control | Git | **Sign commits with GPG/SSH key**
(`vcs.git.commit.gpgSign`, per project) signs the commits Forge makes (`git commit -S`).
**Configure GPG Key…** shows the signing setup in git config (`user.signingkey`, `gpg.format`,
`commit.gpgsign`; read-only) and lets you choose a key:

![Configure GPG Key](docs/screenshots/git-signing-settings.png)

- **Use the key from git config**: git signs with `user.signingkey` (or its default key).
- **GPG keys**: your secret keys from `gpg --list-secret-keys` (expired and revoked keys are
  shown but cannot be chosen).
- **SSH keys**: the public keys in `~/.ssh/*.pub` (`gpg.format=ssh`).

The choice is stored in the Forge setting `vcs.git.commit.signingKey` (`openpgp:<key id>` or
`ssh:<public key file>`) and applied to each commit with `-c user.signingkey=… -c gpg.format=…`
only; Forge never changes git config. For remote projects the keys are listed and used on the
host. GPG asks for a passphrase through your `gpg-agent` pinentry as usual.

The [Log](#log) marks signed commits with a shield: green for a verified signature, yellow for
a signature that cannot be checked (unknown or untrusted key, expired), red for a bad or revoked
one. The commit details name the signer and the key.

### AI commit messages

Click **Generate Commit Message with AI** (the sparkle icon above the message). Forge sends the
diff of the **ticked** files (new files included), the file list and the branch name to your
default AI provider and fills in the message: an imperative subject of at most 72 characters,
optionally a blank line and a short body. Large diffs are shortened so every file keeps a share
(about 14,000 characters in total).

Configure the provider in Settings | Tools | AI Providers; you can pick a separate model for
commit messages there. See [AI](docs/guide/user/ai.md#providers).

## Diff viewer

![Diff viewer](docs/screenshots/vcs-diff.png)

| Action | Key |
| --- | --- |
| Next / Previous Difference | `F7` / `Shift+F7` |
| Compare Next / Previous File | `Alt+Right` / `Alt+Left` |
| Jump to Source | `F4` |
| Close | `Escape` |

The toolbar also has viewer, whitespace and highlighting options and **Collapse Unchanged
Fragments**. Each changed block has a "Revert" arrow that replaces your side with the left
side.

## In the editor

### Change markers

Lines that differ from `HEAD` are marked in the gutter: added, modified and deleted. Click a
marker to see the old text and choose **Rollback** (`Ctrl+Alt+Z`) or **Show Diff** (`Ctrl+D`).
**Next Change** / **Previous Change** (`Ctrl+Alt+Shift+Down` / `Ctrl+Alt+Shift+Up`, Navigate
menu) move the caret to the next or previous changed block, wrapping around at the end of the
file, and open the same popup.

![Next Change popup](docs/screenshots/next-change.png)

### Blame

Right-click the gutter and choose **Annotate with Git Blame** (also in the editor context menu
under Git, and in Find Action). The gutter then shows author and date per line, colored by
age; click an entry for the commit details. **Close Annotations** hides it.

![Blame](docs/screenshots/vcs-blame.png)

The caret line also shows an inline blame hint at its end: "Marlon, 2 days ago • message".

## Branches

Click the branch widget in the toolbar (or **Branches…** in Find Action) to open **Git
Branches**:

![Branches](docs/screenshots/vcs-branches.png)

- At the top: **Update Project…** (`Ctrl+T`), **Commit…** (`Ctrl+K`), **Push…**
  (`Ctrl+Shift+K`), **New Branch…** and **Checkout Tag or Revision…**.
- **Local** and **Remote** branches with a search field ("Search for branches and actions").
- A branch's submenu: for the current branch **New Branch from '…'…**, **Push…** and
  **Update**; for other branches **Checkout**, **New Branch from '…'…**, **Compare with
  'current'** (the Git log of the commits of the branch that are not in the current branch,
  ready to [cherry-pick](#cherry-pick-revert-and-undo)), **Rebase 'current' onto '…'**,
  **Merge '…' into 'current'** and, for local branches, **Delete** (with "Force delete" for
  unmerged branches). For a local branch that no worktree has checked out, **New Worktree…**
  creates a [worktree](#worktrees) for it.
- Branches checked out in another worktree are marked **worktree**; clicking them (or **Open
  Worktree** in their submenu) opens that worktree instead of checking them out.

**New Branch…** asks for the name and whether to check it out.

![Branch in another worktree](docs/screenshots/git-branches-worktree.png)

## Worktrees

The **Worktrees** tab of the **Git** tool window (**Git.Show.Worktrees**) lists the repository's
worktrees (`git worktree list`): path, branch (or "detached") and revision; the main worktree
and the one of this project are marked.

![Worktrees](docs/screenshots/git-worktrees.png)

- **New Worktree…** (`+`, **Git ▸ New Worktree…**, `Git.Worktree.Create`): a **new branch**
  based on a branch of your choice, or an **existing branch** that is not checked out anywhere,
  and the **Directory** (suggested next to the main worktree: `<repo>-<branch>`). "Open the
  worktree after creating it" opens it as the project.

  ![New Worktree](docs/screenshots/git-new-worktree.png)

- **Open** (or double-click) opens a worktree as the project (on the same host for remote
  projects).
- **Lock…** / **Unlock** (`git worktree lock --reason`), **Remove…** (asks again with "Force
  Remove" when the worktree has local changes or is locked) and **Prune Worktrees** (forgets
  worktrees whose folder is gone, shown struck through).

## Push, update and fetch

| Action | Shortcut | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Push… | `Ctrl+Shift+K` (macOS `Cmd+Shift+K`) | pushes the current branch |
| Update Project… | `Ctrl+T` (macOS `Cmd+T`) | pulls the current branch with the update method |
| Fetch | Find Action | fetches all remotes |

Results appear as balloons ("Pushed", "Project updated", "All files are up to date", or the
error). Git runs with `ssh -o BatchMode=yes`, so SSH remotes need a key in your ssh-agent (or
without passphrase); Forge cannot answer password prompts.

![Git settings](docs/screenshots/settings-git.png)

Settings | Version Control | Git:

| Option | Setting | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Path to Git executable | `vcs.git.path` | `git` (the one on `PATH`; `FORGE_GIT` also overrides it). Remote projects always use the git of their host. |
| Update method: Merge, Rebase or Branch default (`pull.rebase` of the branch) | `vcs.git.updateMethod` | Merge |
| Fetch remotes automatically, every n minutes | `vcs.git.autoFetch`, `vcs.git.autoFetchInterval` | on, 10 |
| Add the 'cherry-picked from <hash>' suffix when picking commits pushed to protected branches (`git cherry-pick -x`) | `vcs.git.cherryPickSuffix` | on |
| Protected branches: names or patterns with `*`, separated by `;`. The Log never rewrites commits pushed to them. | `vcs.git.protectedBranches` | `master;main` |

Automatic fetching runs in the background while the branch has an upstream; failures
(offline, missing credentials) are ignored.

## Pull, merge and rebase

![Pull dialog](docs/screenshots/git-pull-dialog.png)

- **Git ▸ Pull…** (`Git.Pull`) opens **Pull to main**: the remote (`origin`), the branch (or
  several, separated by spaces) and **Modify options**: `--rebase`, `--ff-only`, `--no-ff`,
  `--squash`, `--no-commit` and `--no-verify`. Options that cannot be combined are greyed out;
  chosen options appear as chips you can remove with ×.
- **Git ▸ Merge…** (`Git.Merge`) opens **Merge into main**: the branch to merge and the options
  `--no-ff`, `--ff-only`, `--squash`, `-m` (shows a field for the merge commit message),
  `--no-commit`, `--no-verify` and `--allow-unrelated-histories`.
- **Git ▸ Rebase…** (`Git.Rebase`) opens **Rebase main**: the upstream (or new base) and the
  options `--onto` (adds the *from* field: only the commits after it are moved onto the new
  base), **Select another branch to rebase**, `--rebase-merges`, `--keep-empty`, `--root` and
  `--update-refs`. For an interactive rebase use
  [Interactively Rebase from Here…](#interactive-rebase) in the Log.

![Merge dialog](docs/screenshots/git-merge-dialog.png)

![Rebase dialog](docs/screenshots/git-rebase-dialog.png)

When an operation stops with conflicts, the [Conflicts dialog](#merge-conflicts) opens. While a
rebase or merge waits for you, the branch widgets in the toolbar and the status bar say
**Rebasing main** (or **Merging main**) and the Git menu offers **Continue Rebase**, **Skip
Commit** and **Abort Rebase** (`Git.Rebase.Continue`, `Git.Rebase.Skip`, `Git.Rebase.Abort`), or
**Abort Merge** (`Git.Merge.Abort`). Continuing may stop at the next conflict, which opens the
Conflicts dialog again.

![Rebase in progress](docs/screenshots/git-rebasing.png)

## Reset HEAD, tags and remotes

**Git ▸ Reset HEAD…** (`Git.Reset`) resets the current branch to a commit (`HEAD`, `HEAD~2`, a
hash, a branch or tag; **Validate** shows the hash) with one of the reset types:

| Type | What happens |
| --- | --- |
| Soft | Files won't change, differences will be staged for commit. |
| Mixed | Files won't change, differences won't be staged. |
| Hard | Files will be reverted to the state of the selected commit. Any local changes are lost. |
| Keep | Files will be reverted to the state of the selected commit, but local changes are kept intact. |

![Reset dialog](docs/screenshots/git-reset-dialog.png)

**Git ▸ New Tag…** (`Git.CreateNewTag`) opens **Tag**: the tag name, **Force** (replace an
existing tag), the commit (default `HEAD`, with **Validate**) and an optional **Message**, which
makes it an annotated tag.

![Tag dialog](docs/screenshots/git-tag-dialog.png)

**Git ▸ Manage Remotes…** (`Git.Configure.Remotes`) lists the remotes with their URLs. **+** adds
one (**Define Remote**: name and URL), the pencil (or a double-click) edits the name and URL,
the bin removes it.

![Git Remotes](docs/screenshots/git-remotes-dialog.png)

## Stash

**Git ▸ Uncommitted Changes ▸ Stash Changes…** (`Git.Stash`) shows the Git root and the current
branch, asks for a **Message** and offers **Keep index** (staged changes stay staged and in the
working tree). **Create Stash** runs `git stash push`.

![Stash dialog](docs/screenshots/git-stash-dialog.png)

**Unstash Changes…** (`Git.Unstash`) lists the stashes of the repository:

- **View** lists the files of the selected stash; a double-click (or the diff icon) shows the
  diff between the stash's base and the stashed version.
- **Drop** removes the selected stash, **Clear** all of them (both ask first).
- **Pop stash** removes the stash after applying it; **Reinstate index** restores what was
  staged. **As new branch** creates a branch at the stash's base commit, checks it out and pops
  the stash there (`git stash branch`).
- The button reads **Apply Stash**, **Pop Stash** or **Branch**. Conflicts open the Conflicts
  dialog.

![Unstash dialog](docs/screenshots/git-unstash-dialog.png)

The **Stash** tab of the Commit tool window (shown while there are stashes) lists them too:
expand a stash to see its files, double-click a file (or **Show Diff**, `Ctrl+D`) for its diff,
and **Apply**, **Pop** or **Drop** the selected stash from the toolbar.

![Stash tab](docs/screenshots/git-stash-tab.png)

## Shelf

The shelf keeps changes aside without git, like PHPStorm's shelf. Forge stores it per project in
its data directory (`<data dir>/forge/projects/<project>/shelf`, see
[File locations](docs/guide/reference/file-locations.md)); nothing is written into the project.

- **Git ▸ Uncommitted Changes ▸ Shelve Changes…** (`ChangesView.Shelve`) lists the local
  changes (new files included) with checkboxes and a **Comment**. **Shelve Changes** saves the
  ticked files as a patch and rolls them back (new files are removed).
- **Show Shelf** (`Vcs.Show.Shelf`) opens the **Shelf** tab of the Commit tool window. Expand a
  shelved changelist to see its files; `Ctrl`-click selects several.
- Toolbar: **Unshelve…** (`ShelveChanges.UnshelveWithDialog`), **Unshelve Silently**,
  **Delete**, **Show Diff** (`Ctrl+D`, also a double-click on a file) and **Rename**.
- **Unshelve Changes** lists the files with checkboxes, preselected from the selection, so you
  can unshelve part of a changelist. **Remove successfully applied files from the shelf** drops
  them from the shelf afterwards. New files come back as added files.
- A shelved patch that no longer applies cleanly is merged three-way; conflicts open the
  Conflicts dialog and the changes stay on the shelf.

![Shelve Changes](docs/screenshots/git-shelve-dialog.png)

![Shelf tab](docs/screenshots/git-shelf-tab.png)

![Unshelve Changes](docs/screenshots/git-unshelve-dialog.png)

In remote projects git runs on the remote host; the shelf stays on your machine.

## Patches

**Git ▸ Patch** creates and applies patches, like PHPStorm.

**Create Patch…** (Git ▸ Patch, the context menu of changelists and files, the Git log's
commit menu) writes the selected changes, or the changes of the selected commits, as a
unified diff (`git diff --binary`, new files included) with paths relative to the project
root: **Save to file** (a relative name is saved in the project; **Browse…** picks any file in
the desktop app) or **Copy patch to clipboard**. **Reverse patch** swaps both sides.

![Create Patch](docs/screenshots/git-create-patch.png)

**Apply Patch…** picks a patch file, **Apply Patch from Clipboard…** reads the clipboard. Git
patches and patches of other tools (`diff -u`, `svn diff`, PHPStorm) are accepted. The
preview lists every file with its added and removed lines; double-click a file (or its diff
button) to compare the current and the patched version. **Base directory** sets where the
paths start (default: the project root), **Changelist** where the changes go.

![Apply Patch](docs/screenshots/git-apply-patch.png)

Files that no longer fit (marked with a warning) are merged three-way when the patch names the
original versions (patches made by git and Forge do); conflicts open the
[merge conflict](#merge-conflicts) resolver. Files that cannot be merged are reported and left
unchanged. New files are added to git.

## Merge conflicts

When a merge, rebase, update (pull), cherry-pick, unstash or unshelve stops with conflicts, Forge opens
the **Conflicts** dialog. Later you get it with **Git ▸ Resolve Conflicts…** (Find Action:
`Git.ResolveConflicts`), the **Resolve** link of the **Merge conflicts** balloon, or the
**Resolve** link of the **Merge Conflicts** node in the Commit tool window.

![Conflicts dialog](docs/screenshots/merge-conflicts-dialog.png)

- The header says what is going on ("Merging branch feature into branch main").
- **Yours** and **Theirs** show how each side changed a file: Modified, Added or Deleted. In a
  rebase, *yours* is the commit being replayed and *theirs* the branch you rebase onto, like
  in PHPStorm.
- **Accept Yours** / **Accept Theirs** take that side's version of the selected files (a side
  that deleted the file deletes it) and mark them resolved (`git add` / `git rm`).
- **Merge…** (or a double-click) opens the merge window. For a file deleted on one side it asks
  **Keep File** or **Accept Deletion**; for a binary file, which version to keep.
- **Group files by directory** shows the files under their folders.

Until they are resolved, conflicted files are red in the Project view (and their folders), the
editor tabs and the **Merge Conflicts** node of the Commit tool window. An editor of such a file
shows the banner **File has merge conflicts** with a **Resolve…** link to the merge window.

![Conflicts in the Commit tool window and the editor](docs/screenshots/merge-conflicts-commit.png)

### Merge window

**Merge Revisions for …** shows your version (**Changes from main**) on the left, the editable
**Result** in the middle and the other side (**Changes from feature**) on the right. The result
starts with the common base version; the three panes scroll together and bands connect the
changes.

![Merge window](docs/screenshots/merge-window.png)

- Colours: blue for modified, green for inserted, grey for deleted lines, red for conflicts.
  Handled changes lose their colour.
- `»` / `«` next to a change applies it to the result; `×` ignores it. After you applied one
  side of a conflict, the arrow of the other side appends its text after the first.
- Toolbar: **Previous / Next Difference** (`Shift+F7` / `F7`), **Apply Non-Conflicting
  Changes from the Left Side**, **Apply All Non-Conflicting Changes**, **Apply Non-Conflicting
  Changes from the Right Side**, **Resolve Simple Conflicts** (the magic wand) and **Compare
  Contents** (left, base, right and result side by side in the diff viewer). The counter on the
  right shows the unresolved changes: "3 changes. 2 conflicts".
- **Resolve Simple Conflicts** merges conflicts where both sides changed *different* words of
  the same lines (`$price * $qty` → `$netPrice * $qty` and `$price * $quantity` become
  `$netPrice * $quantity`). Conflicts where both sides changed the same words stay for you.
- Edit the result freely; `Ctrl+Z` also undoes applied changes.
- **Accept Left** / **Accept Right** take one side for the whole file. **Apply** writes the
  result and marks the file resolved (`git add`); with unresolved changes left it asks first
  ("There are unresolved changes"). **Cancel** (`Escape`) asks before it discards your edits.

![Merge window after applying changes](docs/screenshots/merge-window-resolved.png)

Files with `\r\n` line separators keep them. In remote projects the stage versions are read
and the result is written on the remote host. When the last conflict is resolved, Forge
reminds you to commit (merge, cherry-pick) or continue the rebase.

## Log

The **Git** tool window (`Alt+9`, bottom) has a **Log** tab with the commit graph, the
[Worktrees](#worktrees) tab and a **Console** tab with the git commands Forge ran.

![Git log](docs/screenshots/vcs-log.png)

- Filter by text or hash, branch, user, date and paths; **Show all branches**. Click
  **HEAD (Current Branch)** in the branches pane to see only the current branch.
- Select a commit to see its changed files; open their diffs from there. `Ctrl+click` and
  `Shift+click` select several commits; `Up`/`Down` move the selection, `Left`/`Right` go to the
  child / parent commit.
- **Fetch All Remotes** and **Refresh** (`Ctrl+F5`) in the toolbar.
- Signed commits show a shield after the subject (see
  [Signing commits](#signing-commits-with-gpg-or-ssh-keys)); the details name the signer.

### Log actions

Right-click commits for PHPStorm's Log context menu. Every action is also in Find Action and
the keymap (Settings | Keymap) under its PHPStorm id and works on the selection of the Log.

![Log context menu](docs/screenshots/git-log-context-menu.png)

| Action | Id | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Copy Revision Number | `Vcs.CopyRevisionNumberAction` | copies the full hashes |
| Create Patch… | `Vcs.Log.CreatePatch` | writes the changes of the selected commits as a patch file into the project |
| Cherry-Pick | `Vcs.CherryPick` | applies commits of other branches to the current branch (oldest first) |
| Checkout Revision | `Git.CheckoutRevision` | detached HEAD at the commit |
| Show Repository at Revision | `Git.BrowseRepoAtRevision` | lists the files of the commit; opens them read-only |
| Compare with Local | `Vcs.Log.CompareWithLocal` | the files that differ between the commit and the working tree |
| Reset Current Branch to Here… | `Git.Reset.In.Log` | the [Reset dialog](#reset-head-tags-and-remotes) with the commit |
| Revert Commit | `Git.Revert.In.Log` | new commits that undo the selected ones |
| Undo Commit… | `Git.Uncommit` | removes the last, unpushed commit and keeps its changes |
| Edit Commit Message… | `Git.Reword.Commit` | rewords a commit |
| Fixup… / Squash Into… | `Git.Fixup.To.Commit`, `Git.Squash.Into.Commit` | commit the local changes as `fixup! <subject>` / `squash! <subject>` |
| Squash Commits… | `Git.Squash.Commits` | several selected commits become one, with an editable message |
| Drop Commits | `Git.Drop.Commits` | removes commits from the branch |
| Interactively Rebase from Here… | `Git.Interactive.Rebase` | the [Rebasing Commits](#interactive-rebase) dialog |
| New Branch… / New Tag… | | a branch or tag at the commit |
| Go to Child Commit / Go to Parent Commit | `Vcs.Log.GoToChild`, `Vcs.Log.GoToParent` | selects the neighbour in the Log |

![Several commits selected](docs/screenshots/git-log-multiple-commits.png)

Actions that cannot run are greyed out; hover them for the reason, like PHPStorm:

- The actions that rewrite history (Undo, Edit Commit Message, Fixup, Squash, Drop, the
  interactive rebase) need commits of the current branch, no merge commits in between and no
  operation in progress.
- Commits already pushed to a **protected branch** (Settings | Version Control | Git,
  `master;main` by default) are never rewritten: "The selected commit is already pushed to
  protected branch 'origin/main'". Commits pushed to other branches can be rewritten after a
  warning (you will need a force push).
- **Undo Commit** is available only for the last commit of the current branch and only while
  it is not pushed. The changes go back to the Commit tool window (the "Changes" changelist)
  and the message into the commit message field.

![Pushed commit warning](docs/screenshots/git-log-pushed-warning.png)

After a rewrite a balloon offers **Undo**, which moves the branch back as long as nothing
changed since. Local changes are kept (`git rebase --autostash`).

![Edit Commit Message](docs/screenshots/git-edit-commit-message.png)

### Cherry-pick, revert and undo

**Cherry-Pick** applies the selected commits to the current branch, oldest first. Commits whose
changes are already in the branch are skipped. With "Add the 'cherry-picked from <hash>'
suffix…" on, commits that are pushed to a protected branch get git's "(cherry picked from
commit …)" line. **Revert Commit** creates one revert commit per selected commit. A cherry-pick
or revert that stops with conflicts opens the [Conflicts dialog](#merge-conflicts); commit the
result to finish it, or abort it from the Git menu.

### Interactive rebase

**Interactively Rebase from Here…** opens **Rebasing Commits** with the commits from the
selected one up to `HEAD` (newest at the top):

![Rebasing Commits](docs/screenshots/git-interactive-rebase.png)

- The toolbar sets the action of the selected commits: **Pick**, **Edit** (stop after the
  commit to amend it), **Reword** (new message), **Squash** (meld into the older commit below
  and combine the messages), **Fixup** (meld and keep the older message) and **Drop**. With
  several commits selected, **Squash** becomes **Unite**: the commits are moved together and
  squashed into the oldest of them.
- Reorder commits by drag and drop or with **Move Up** / **Move Down** (`Alt+Up` / `Alt+Down`,
  `Git.Interactive.Rebase.MoveUp` / `Git.Interactive.Rebase.MoveDown`).
- For a reworded commit or a squash the right side is the message editor; otherwise it shows
  the commit's files and message. **Reset** restores the initial plan.
- `fixup!`, `squash!` and `amend!` commits (from **Fixup…** / **Squash Into…**) start right
  after the commit they target, like `git rebase --autosquash`.

**Start Rebasing** (`Ctrl+Enter`) runs `git rebase -i`. Forge writes the todo list itself and
applies new messages with `exec` steps, so git never opens an editor; this also works in
remote projects. When the rebase stops at an **Edit** step or with conflicts, the branch widget
shows **Rebasing …**, conflicts open the [Conflicts dialog](#merge-conflicts), and **Git ▸
Continue Rebase / Skip Commit / Abort Rebase** take it from there.

![After the rebase](docs/screenshots/git-interactive-rebase-done.png)

## File and folder history

**Show History** (Git ▸ Current File, the editor's and the Project view's Git submenu) opens a
**History: <name>** tab in the Git tool window, next to **Log**. For a file it lists every
commit that changed it and follows renames (the old path is shown next to the message); for a
folder, every commit that changed something below it.

![File history](docs/screenshots/file-history.png)

- The table has the commit message, author, date and hash. Below it are the full message and,
  for a folder, the files the commit changed (click one to preview it).
- The right side previews the file's change in the selected commit.
- Toolbar and right-click menu:

| Action | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Show Diff (`Ctrl+D`, double-click) | the file's change in the commit in the diff viewer |
| Compare with Local | the revision against your working copy (editable) |
| Get | replaces your working copy with the revision, after a confirmation |
| Annotate Revision | opens the file as it was in the revision, read-only, with its blame |
| Checkout Revision | checks out the commit (detached HEAD) |
| Copy Revision Number | copies the full hash |

![History context menu](docs/screenshots/file-history-menu.png)

Close a history tab with its **×** or a middle click.

![Folder history](docs/screenshots/folder-history.png)

### History for selection

Select lines in the editor and choose **Show History for Selection** (Git ▸ Current File or the
editor's Git submenu). The **History for Selection** tab lists the commits that changed those
lines (`git log -L`, line numbers as in `HEAD`); the preview shows the block before and after
each commit, so you can follow how it evolved.

![History for selection](docs/screenshots/selection-history.png)

### Annotate Revision

**Annotate Revision** opens the file of that revision in a read-only editor tab named
`User.php (49e9d6ef)` with the blame of the revision in the gutter.

![Annotate Revision](docs/screenshots/annotate-revision.png)

## Compare with Revision and Branch

- **Compare with Revision…** lists the revisions of the file (renames followed) and compares
  the picked one with your version.
- **Compare with Branch…** picks a local or remote branch or a tag. For a file it opens the
  diff; for a folder (Project view) it opens an editor tab with the files that differ between
  the branch and the working tree. Double-click a file (or `Ctrl+D`) for its diff.
- **Show Diff** is PHPStorm's Compare with the Same Repository Version: `HEAD` against your
  version.

## Compare files and folders

In the Project view, select two files or two folders (`Ctrl`+click the second one) and press
`Ctrl+D`, or right-click and choose **Compare Files** / **Compare Directories** (below Reload
from Disk). With one entry selected the item is **Compare With…** and asks for the second file
or folder in a **Select Path** dialog.

![Select Path](docs/screenshots/compare-files.png)

Two files open in the diff viewer; the right side can be edited and is saved when you close
it. Two folders open a folder diff in an editor tab:

![Compare Directories](docs/screenshots/compare-directories.png)

- Every file and folder of both sides with size and date, and an indicator in the middle: `→`
  only on the left, `≠` different, `=` equal, `←` only on the right. Folders can be collapsed.
- The filter buttons in the toolbar show or hide each kind, with their counts.
- Double-click a file (or `Ctrl+D`, **Compare Contents**) to open its diff.
- **Copy to Right** / **Copy to Left** copy the selected file or folder to the other side
  (folders are merged; replacing a different file asks first).
- `.git`, `.hg` and `.svn` folders are not compared.

The folders are read where the project is, so this works in remote projects too.

![Compare Directories, light theme](docs/screenshots/compare-directories-light.png)

## Compare with Clipboard

**Compare with Clipboard** (View menu, editor context menu) compares the clipboard with the
selected text, or with the whole file when nothing is selected; the whole file can then be
edited in the diff viewer.

![Compare with Clipboard](docs/screenshots/compare-with-clipboard.png)

## Code review

Pull and merge requests, issues and CI pipelines of GitHub, GitLab and Forgejo/Gitea are in
[Code hosts](docs/guide/user/code-hosts.md).

## Not available yet

Push All up to Here is not implemented yet. Local History (revisions without commits, labels,
Recent Changes) has its own page: [Local History](docs/guide/user/local-history.md). Projects (cloned repositories,
worktrees) open in the current window until Forge supports several project windows.

Source: docs/guide/user/local-history.md

# Local History

Local History is Forge's own record of how your project files changed, independent of Git.
It works in every project (with or without a repository, local or
[remote](docs/guide/user/remote-development.md)) and lets you look at and restore earlier contents of a file,
a folder or a few lines, even of files you never committed.

![Local History of a file](docs/screenshots/local-history-file.png)

## What is recorded

Forge records the content of a file:

| Event | Shown as |
| --- | --- |
| Every save (`Ctrl+S`, autosave, Actions on Save) | `Saved` |
| A refactoring (rename, move, extract, quick fixes that change several files, Replace in Files, Structural Replace): all files it changes, open editors included, as one change | `Refactoring: Rename spent() to totalSpent()`, `Replace in Files` |
| VCS operations: Update Project / Pull, Checkout, Merge, Rebase, Reset, Rollback, Stash / Unstash, Shelve / Unshelve | `Update from VCS`, `Checkout main`, `Rollback`, `Unshelve <name>`, … |
| Changes made outside Forge (another editor, a terminal, `composer`, a code generator), found by the file watcher | `External change` |
| Creating, deleting, renaming, moving and copying files and folders (Project view, refactorings, file templates) | `Create file A.php`, `Delete Legacy`, `Rename A.php to B.php`, `Move A.php to app/Models` |
| Labels you put | the label's name, in bold |
| Local History's own Revert | `Revert to …` |

Forge also keeps the content of a file when it first opens it, so the first change of a file
can be compared with and reverted to how it was before. A file that changed while Forge was
closed is recorded as an `External change` the next time Forge reads it.

Recording happens in the background: saving never waits for it.

**Not recorded:** files in excluded folders (by default `.git`, `.hg`, `.svn`, `node_modules`,
`vendor` and `.idea`, at any depth), binary files and files larger than the size limit
(1024 KB by default). See [Settings](#settings).

## Show History

Open the history of a file, a folder or the whole project:

- **File | Local History | Show History** (in projects without Git also **VCS | Local History |
  Show History**): the file or folder selected in the Project view, otherwise the file in the
  editor;
- **Project view** context menu ▸ **Local History** ▸ **Show History** (on the project root:
  the whole project);
- **editor** context menu ▸ **Local History** ▸ **Show History**.

The history opens as an editor tab, **Local History: _name_**:

- the **revision list**, newest first: what happened (`Saved`, `Refactoring: …`,
  `External change`, labels in bold) and when. A revision is the state of the file **before**
  that change (for a label: at the label), so the newest revision compared with the current
  version shows the latest change. Renamed and moved files keep their history; the old path
  is shown next to the revision.
- the **diff** of the selected revision against the current version (the editor's text when
  the file is open, unsaved edits included). Double-click a revision or press `Ctrl+D` for the
  full diff viewer.
- **Filter by text** in the toolbar keeps the revisions whose name or content contains the
  text, e.g. a method name you deleted somewhere along the way.

For a **folder**, a revision lists every file in the folder that differs from now: changed
files, files created since (Revert deletes them) and files deleted since (shown struck
through; Revert recreates them). Select a file to see its diff.

![Local History of the project with a deleted file](docs/screenshots/local-history-folder.png)

### Toolbar and context menu

| Action | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| **Revert** | Restores the selected revision: the file gets its old content back. For a folder (after a confirmation) every listed file is restored, deleted files and folders are recreated and files created since are deleted. Unsaved edits are saved first; the revert itself is recorded, so it can be reverted too. |
| **Show Diff** (`Ctrl+D`) | The selected revision against the current version in the diff viewer. |
| **Create Patch…** | The difference between the revision and now as a unified diff (git format), copied to the clipboard or saved to a file. Apply it later with Git ▸ Patch ▸ Apply Patch. |
| **Put Label…** | See [Labels](#labels). |
| **Refresh** | Reloads the list (it also refreshes by itself when something is recorded). |

## Show History for Selection

Select lines in the editor (or put the caret on one line) and choose **Local History ▸ Show
History for Selection** in the editor context menu (action `LocalHistory.ShowSelectionHistory`,
also in Find Action). The **History for Selection** tab lists only the revisions in which those
lines were different, with the lines as they were next to the lines now. The lines are
followed through the file's history, also when code above them was added or removed.

![Show History for Selection](docs/screenshots/local-history-selection.png)

## Labels

**File | Local History | Put Label…** (or the Project view and editor menus, VCS | Local
History in projects without Git, or the tag button in a history tab) names the current moment for the whole
project, e.g. "Before upgrading Laravel". Unsaved edits are saved first.

![Put Label](docs/screenshots/local-history-put-label.png)

Labels appear in bold in the history of every file and folder. Select a label and press
**Revert** to put a file, a folder or (in the project's history, or from Recent Changes) the
whole project back to that moment.

## Recent Changes

**View | Recent Changes** (`Alt+Shift+C`, macOS `Opt+Shift+C`) lists what happened recently in
the whole project, newest first: refactorings, external changes, VCS operations, labels,
created and deleted files; saves in a row are one entry. Type to filter, use the arrow keys and
press `Enter` (or click) to open the change.

![Recent Changes](docs/screenshots/recent-changes.png)

The change opens as a tab with its files and the diff of each file before and after the change.
**Revert** there gives the files the content they had before the change (for a label: the
whole project goes back to the label).

![A recent change with its files](docs/screenshots/recent-change.png)

## Settings

Settings | Version Control | Local History:

| Setting | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Keep local history for (working days) | 5 | Only days on which something was recorded count, like PHPStorm's "working days". Older revisions and labels are removed when a project opens and every few hours. |
| Maximum history size per project (MB) | 512 | When the stored contents grow larger, the oldest revisions are removed first. |
| Do not record files larger than (KB) | 1024 | Binary files are never recorded. |
| Excluded folders | `.git`, `.hg`, `.svn`, `node_modules`, `vendor`, `.idea` | Folder names (at any depth) or project-relative paths like `storage/logs`. |

![Local History settings](docs/screenshots/local-history-settings.png)

## Where it is stored

Local History is kept on this computer, never inside the project:
`<data dir>/forge/projects/<name>-<hash>/local-history/` (see
[File locations](docs/guide/reference/file-locations.md)). `changes.jsonl` lists the changes, one per
line; `content/` holds each file content once (contents are compressed and stored by their
hash, so saving the same text again costs nothing). For a remote project the contents are read
through the SSH connection and stored locally.

> **Note:** Local History is not a backup. It is cleaned up after the configured working days,
> and it is lost when Forge's data directory is deleted. Commit important work.

## Shortcuts and actions

| Action | Action id | Windows / Linux | macOS |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Show History | `LocalHistory.ShowHistory` | — | — |
| Show History for Selection | `LocalHistory.ShowSelectionHistory` | — | — |
| Put Label… | `LocalHistory.PutLabel` | — | — |
| Recent Changes | `RecentChanges` | `Alt+Shift+C` | `Opt+Shift+C` |

Assign shortcuts in Settings | [Keymap](docs/guide/user/keymap.md).

# Code hosts

The plugin **GitLab, Forgejo and GitHub** (`forge.code-hosts`) brings code review into Forge:

| Host | API | Number format | Self-hosted |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| GitLab | REST v4 | `!12` | yes (self-managed, also with a relative URL root or SSH port) |
| Forgejo / Gitea | `/api/v1` | `#12` | yes (e.g. Codeberg) |
| GitHub | REST + GraphQL for review threads | `#12` | GitHub Enterprise Server |

The repository is detected from `git remote -v` (https, ssh and scp-style URLs, nested GitLab
groups); in a [remote project](docs/guide/user/remote-development.md) git runs on the host, while the API calls
go from your machine with your tokens. Wording follows the host: "merge request" on GitLab, "pull request" elsewhere.

## Logging in

Open Settings | Version Control | **GitLab**, **Forgejo / Gitea** or **GitHub** and click
**Log In with Token…**. Enter the **Server** (for self-hosted instances) and an access token:

| Host | Token permissions |
| --- | --- |
| GitLab | scopes `api`, `read_user` |
| Forgejo / Gitea | read/write for repository and issue, read for user |
| GitHub | scopes `repo`, `read:org`, `workflow` (or a fine-grained token with pull request, issue and actions access) |

![Accounts](docs/screenshots/forges-accounts.png)

The token is verified first and then stored in the operating system keychain (service
`forge-forges`), never in a settings file. Accounts themselves (server, user) are kept in
`forges.toml` in Forge's config folder. Without an account, the environment variables
`GITLAB_TOKEN`, `FORGEJO_TOKEN` / `GITEA_TOKEN` and `GITHUB_TOKEN` / `GH_TOKEN` are used for
the public servers ("Token from environment").

Errors are explained in plain words: a rejected token, missing permissions, rate limits (with
the reset time) or an unreachable server.

## Pull Requests tool window

The **Pull Requests** tool window (left stripe, **View Pull/Merge Requests** in Find Action)
has three tabs.

![Merge request list](docs/screenshots/forges-mr-list.png)

### Pull/Merge Requests

- Search, plus filters for **State** (Open, Merged, Closed, All), **Author**, **Label**,
  **Assignee** and **Reviewer**, and **Quick Filters** such as "Assigned to you" and
  "Review requests".
- Each row shows the title, number, author, age, CI status, comment count and avatar.
- Click a request to open it as an editor tab.
- **+** (or **Create Merge Request…** in Find Action) creates one.

### A pull/merge request tab

![Overview](docs/screenshots/forges-mr-overview.png)

- **Overview**: description (Markdown), comments and review threads with **Reply**,
  resolve/unresolve (where the host supports it; Forgejo cannot resolve threads through its
  API), reviewers and approvals, assignees, labels, the pipeline with its jobs, and the merge
  status ("No conflicts with main").
- **Files**: the changed files with their diffs; comment on a line to start a thread.
  **Show Diff (side by side)** opens the diff viewer.
- Actions: **Approve**, **Merge…** (merge commit, **Squash and merge**, **Rebase and
  merge**, "Mark as ready before merging" for drafts, the commit message), **Close**,
  **Check Out** (fetches the source branch and checks it out locally), **Open in Browser** and
  **Refresh**.

![Files](docs/screenshots/forges-mr-files.png)

### Create a pull/merge request

**Create Merge Request…** asks for the **Head branch** and **Base branch**, **Title**,
**Description** (Markdown), **Reviewers**, **Labels** and whether it is a draft.

![Create merge request](docs/screenshots/forges-create-mr.png)

### Issues

Search and filter issues, open one as a tab, read and add comments.

![Issues](docs/screenshots/forges-issues.png)

### Pipelines

CI runs of the repository (GitLab pipelines, GitHub Actions workflow runs, Forgejo/Gitea
Actions runs) with their status and jobs.

## CI status in the status bar

The status bar shows the CI status of the current branch ("CI: Running", "Passed", "Failed").
Settings | Version Control | **Code Hosts** (the account pages are below it):

| Setting | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `vcs.hosts.statusBarPipeline` | `true` | show the CI status of the current branch |
| `vcs.hosts.refreshSeconds` | `120` | refresh requests and pipelines every N seconds; `0` turns automatic refresh off |

# Project trust and Safe Mode

A project can contain code that runs as soon as an IDE touches it: Composer and npm scripts,
run configurations, test suites, build files, language servers or linters installed in
`node_modules` or `vendor`. Like PHPStorm, Forge asks before it opens a project you have not
trusted yet, and opens untrusted projects in **Safe Mode**, where none of their code runs.

## Trust and Open Project?

When you open a folder that is not trusted (Open…, a recent project, `forge path`, Get from
VCS, the Browser Companion), Forge asks first:

![Trust and Open Project dialog](docs/screenshots/trust-open-project.png)

- **Trust Project** opens the project normally and remembers the decision.
- **Preview in Safe Mode** opens it in Safe Mode: you can browse, search and edit the files,
  but nothing of the project runs. You can trust it later from the banner.
- **Don't Open** leaves the current project (or the Welcome screen) as it was.
- **Trust projects in `<parent folder>`** also trusts every project in the folder that
  contains this one (a *trusted location*), for example `~/Projects`. The option is missing
  when the parent is a file system root.

Projects Forge creates itself (File | **New Project…**) are trusted automatically. Reopening
the open project (Repair IDE) does not ask again.

A project passed on the command line while Forge starts (`forge path`) opens right away; when it
is not trusted it opens in Safe Mode and shows the banner.

## Safe Mode

While the project is in Safe Mode, the editor area shows a banner:

![Safe Mode banner](docs/screenshots/safe-mode-banner.png)

Click **Trust Project…** in the banner (or run *Trust Project…* through Find Action,
`Ctrl+Shift+A`) to trust it. The dialog offers the same "Trust projects in …" option:

![Trust Project dialog from the banner](docs/screenshots/safe-mode-trust-dialog.png)

After trusting, everything below is available at once; language servers that were held back
start on the next file you open.

### What does not run in Safe Mode

Forge's backend refuses these commands with an error that names the action, so they stay
blocked even if a plugin or the UI tries to start them:

| Feature | In Safe Mode |
| --- | --- |
| Run/Debug configurations, Before launch tasks, Run Anything, External Tools | not started (every run goes through one place in the backend) |
| Composer and npm scripts, Artisan, Symfony console, Command Line Tool Support | not started; the Run Command popup lists only the built-in Artisan and Symfony commands |
| Test runners (PHPUnit, Pest, Codeception, Behat, PHPSpec, Vitest, Jest) | not started |
| Xdebug: Start Listening, PHP Web Page | refused |
| Composer: Show Outdated, Audit | refused (Composer loads the project's plugins) |
| Laravel routes | parsed from the route files instead of `php artisan route:list` |
| Docker Compose up and Dockerfile ▶ in the gutter, Compose **Up** in Services | refused |
| PHP interpreters: version and `phpinfo()` of an interpreter inside the project or a Docker Compose service | refused |
| Language servers installed in the project (`node_modules/.bin`, `vendor/bin`, …) | not started |
| ESLint, Tailwind CSS, rust-analyzer, Ruby LSP, Java, Kotlin and C# language servers | not started (they load the project's config files or build scripts) |
| Actions on Save: ESLint, Prettier, PHP CS Fixer, Laravel Pint | not run |
| StyLua installed in the project | not run |
| AI agents (Claude Code, Gemini CLI) | not started (they run the project's hooks and MCP servers) |
| Deployment: automatic upload on save | off (the servers and the option come from the project's own files) |
| SSH session to a deployment server (Tools \| Start SSH Session…) | asks first: the server comes from the project's files; your own SSH configurations connect without asking |

What still works: the editor, the Project view, search, the PHP and Lua indexes, Go to
Declaration, completion from the built-in analysis, language servers installed outside the
project (for example Intelephense from npm or Forge's own install), Git, Local History,
databases, the HTTP client and [Deployment](docs/guide/user/deployment.md) actions you start yourself (upload,
download, compare and sync only copy files), and the [Remote Host](docs/guide/user/remote-host-and-ssh.md)
tool window with Edit Remote File.

The **terminal** opens in Safe Mode, because you type the commands yourself. The project's own
settings (`.forge/settings.toml`) cannot choose its shell or environment variables then; your
user settings are used.

> **Note:** Git runs in Safe Mode, like in PHPStorm. Git itself can run programs a repository
> configures in `.git/config` (for example `core.fsmonitor`); Forge does not change that.

## Trusted Locations

Settings | Build, Execution, Deployment | **Trusted Locations** lists the folders whose
projects open without asking, and the projects you trusted one by one:

![Trusted Locations settings page](docs/screenshots/trusted-locations.png)

- **+** adds a folder (`~` is your home folder). Every project inside it, at any depth, is
  trusted. A whole drive or `/` cannot be added.
- **−** removes the selected entry. When nothing trusts the open project any more, it goes
  back to Safe Mode right away.

Changes are saved immediately. Trust decisions are stored in
`<config dir>/forge/trusted-projects.toml` (see [File locations](docs/guide/reference/file-locations.md)),
never in the project and never in the settings files: a project's own `.forge/settings.toml`
cannot trust itself.

## Remote projects

Remote projects (Welcome | Remote Development) use the same rules: the project on the host is
trusted by itself or by a trusted location on the **same host, user and port**, stored as
`user@host:/path`. Because the folder on the host is only known after connecting, Forge opens
an untrusted remote project in Safe Mode first and then asks. **Don't Open** closes the project
and the connection again; nothing of it ran in the meantime. Trusted locations on this machine
never cover remote projects, and the other way round.

Dev containers are built from a folder on this machine, so the **local folder's** trust counts:
Forge asks before the image build and `postCreateCommand` (they run the project's code), refuses
both for an untrusted folder, and the project in the container is trusted with its sources. A
WSL project is trusted by its `\\wsl.localhost\<distro>\…` path. See
[Dev Containers and WSL](docs/guide/user/dev-containers-and-wsl.md).

## Browser mode

The demo projects of browser mode live in `~/Projects`, a trusted location, so they open
normally. Opening any other folder (for example `~/Downloads/legacy-crm` from a screenshot
scenario) shows the dialog, and the run mocks refuse like the desktop app does in Safe Mode.

Source: docs/guide/user/run-debug.md

# Run/Debug configurations

A **run configuration** describes how to start something: a script, a test suite, a command.
Forge's configurations work like PHPStorm's.

> **Note:** nothing runs while the project is in Safe Mode (not trusted yet); trust it with
> **Trust Project…** in the banner, see [Project trust and Safe Mode](docs/guide/user/project-trust.md).

## Run widget

The run widget in the main toolbar shows the selected configuration with **Run** (▶) and
**Debug** (🐞) buttons. Its dropdown lists all configurations and has **Edit
Configurations…**; without configurations it reads **Add Configuration…**.

![Run widget](docs/screenshots/run-toolbar-dropdown.png)

| Action | Windows/Linux | macOS |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Run the selected configuration | `Shift+F10` | `Ctrl+R` |
| Debug the selected configuration | `Shift+F9` | `Ctrl+D` |
| Run… (choose a configuration) | `Alt+Shift+F10` | `Ctrl+Alt+R` |
| Debug… (choose a configuration) | `Alt+Shift+F9` | `Ctrl+Alt+D` |
| Run Context Configuration (the test, script or Lua chunk at the caret) | `Ctrl+Shift+F10` | `Ctrl+Shift+R` |
| Debug Context Configuration | `Ctrl+Shift+F9` | `Ctrl+Shift+D` |
| Stop | `Ctrl+F2` | `Cmd+F2` |
| Rerun | `Ctrl+F5` | `Cmd+R` |
| Edit Configurations… | Find Action | |
| [Run Anything](#run-anything) | `Double Ctrl` | `Double Ctrl` |

In the **Run…** chooser, `Enter` runs and `Shift+Enter` (or holding `Shift`) debugs; it also
offers **Run Shell Command…** and **Edit Configuration…**.

## Run Anything

Press `Ctrl` twice (Tools | Run Anything…) to run almost anything from one popup:

![Run Anything](docs/screenshots/run-anything.png)

- **Recent**: what you ran from Run Anything in this project (kept outside the project, in
  Forge's state directory).
- **Run configurations**: run (or debug) a saved or temporary configuration by name.
- **npm scripts** of every `package.json` with the detected package manager (`pnpm run dev`),
  **Composer scripts** of `composer.json` (`composer test`).
- **PHP files**: type `php ` and part of a file name (`php User`).
- **Composer**, **Artisan** and **Symfony console commands** of
  [Command Line Tool Support](docs/guide/user/command-line-tools.md) (Symfony projects without it use the
  Symfony index);
  other plugins add their commands with `registerRunAnythingProvider`.
- **Commands**: anything else you type runs as a command in the project directory, in the Run
  tool window. When no suggestion starts with what you typed, the command itself is the first
  entry.

![Suggestions for "php art"](docs/screenshots/run-anything-query.png)

`Enter` runs the selected entry. Hold **Shift** to switch to **Debug Anything**: `Shift+Enter`
debugs it (Xdebug for PHP, `--inspect` for npm). Type `?` for help on what can be typed; picking
a help entry fills in its prefix.

![Debug Anything](docs/screenshots/run-anything-debug.png)

Typed commands become [temporary configurations](#temporary-configurations) of the matching
type, so they run like configurations:

| You type | Runs as |
| --- | --- |
| `php [options] script.php [args]` | PHP Script through the project's [CLI interpreter](docs/guide/user/php.md#cli-interpreters) (Docker, SSH, WSL included) |
| `php artisan <command>` | Artisan |
| `composer <command>` | Composer command (`composer` with `php.composer.executable`) |
| `npm`, `pnpm`, `yarn`, `bun` `run <script> [-- args]` or any other command | npm (`npm install lodash`, `yarn add x`) |
| anything else | Shell Script (`/bin/sh -c "<command>"`, `cmd.exe /C` on Windows) in the project directory |

## Run/Debug Configurations dialog

![Run/Debug Configurations](docs/screenshots/run-configurations-dialog.png)

- **+** (`Alt+Insert`) adds a configuration from a type; copy, remove and reorder with the
  toolbar. **Edit configuration templates…** sets the defaults for new configurations of a
  type.
- Common fields: **Name**, **Store as project file**, the type's own fields, **Interpreter**
  and **Interpreter options** (PHP and Lua types), **Arguments**, **Working directory**
  (default: the project root), **Environment variables** and [Before launch](#before-launch)
  tasks.
- The **Command Line** preview shows exactly what will run.

### Configuration types

| Type | Fields | Runs | Debug |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| PHP Script | File | `<php> <options> <file> <arguments>` | Xdebug |
| PHP Built-in Web Server | Host (`localhost`), Port (`8080`), Document root, Use router script, Open in browser after launch | `<php> <options> -S host:port -t <document root> [router]`, then opens `http://host:port/` | Xdebug for every request |
| PHP Web Page | Server (Settings \| PHP \| Servers), Start URL | opens the page in the browser | adds `XDEBUG_SESSION_START=FORGE` |
| PHP HTTP Request | Server (optional), URL, Request method, Headers, Request body | sends the request, the response appears in the Run tool window | adds the `XDEBUG_SESSION` cookie |
| PHPUnit | Test scope: Directory, File, Class, Method or "Defined in the configuration file"; Configuration file (`phpunit.xml` detected); Test runner options | `phpunit --teamcity …` (from `vendor/bin`, or as set in [Settings \| PHP \| Test Frameworks](docs/guide/user/test-frameworks.md#settings--php--test-frameworks)) | Xdebug |
| Pest, Codeception, Behat, PHPSpec | see [PHP test frameworks](docs/guide/user/test-frameworks.md#run-configurations) | `pest --teamcity …`, `codecept run …`, `behat …`, `phpspec run …` | Xdebug |
| Artisan | Command (`migrate --seed`) | `<php> artisan <command>` | Xdebug |
| Composer Script | Script | `composer run <script>` with `php.composer.executable` | Xdebug |
| npm | package.json, Command (`run`, `install`, …), Scripts, Package manager | `npm`/`pnpm`/`yarn`/`bun` | sets `NODE_OPTIONS=--inspect` |
| Shell Script | Execute: Script file or Script text; Script path / text | the shell | — |
| Lua Script | File | `<lua> <options> <file> <arguments>`, LÖVE games as `love <dir>` | — |
| Native Application | Executable, Debugger (LLDB, GDB or a pack's adapter), Stop at the beginning of the program, Launch options (JSON) | `<executable> <program arguments>` | the chosen [debug adapter](docs/guide/user/debugging.md#debug-adapter-sessions) |
| Compound | Configurations, Allow multiple instances | starts every configuration, each in its own Run tab | debugs every member |

The PHP interpreter defaults to the project's CLI interpreter (`php.interpreter`, Settings |
Languages & Frameworks | PHP), the Lua interpreter to `lua.interpreter`. The **Interpreter**
field of PHP Script, PHPUnit and Artisan configurations lists the project default, every
[CLI interpreter](docs/guide/user/php.md#cli-interpreters) and **Custom…** (a path to a local `php`):

![Interpreter of a run configuration](docs/screenshots/php-interpreters-run-config.png)

A Docker, Docker Compose, SSH or WSL interpreter wraps the command line: `docker run --rm …`,
`docker compose run/exec …`, `ssh user@host …` or `wsl.exe -d … --exec php …`, with paths in
the arguments and the working directory mapped into the container or host, the environment
variables passed along (`-e NAME=value`, `env NAME=value`) and the interpreter's
configuration options as `-d name=value`. Paths in the output (stack traces, PHPUnit
failures) are mapped back to project files, so they stay clickable in the Run console.
Composer Script and Composer command configurations run `composer` through an interpreter
when their Interpreter field names one; otherwise they use `php.composer.executable` locally.

![Artisan through a Docker Compose interpreter](docs/screenshots/php-interpreters-run.png)

Debugging (`Shift+F9`) through an interpreter works the same way: Xdebug connects to
`host.docker.internal` from containers (`docker run` adds
`--add-host=host.docker.internal:host-gateway`; Compose services on Linux need an
`extra_hosts: ["host.docker.internal:host-gateway"]` entry), SSH runs forward the debug port
back with `ssh -R 9003:127.0.0.1:9003`, and the run sets `PHP_IDE_CONFIG=serverName=<interpreter>`
so breakpoints use the interpreter's path mappings.

![PHP Built-in Web Server](docs/screenshots/run-builtin-server.png)

The built-in web server runs through the configuration's interpreter too: Docker and Compose
interpreters publish the port (`-p 8080:8080`, the server binds `0.0.0.0` inside the
container), SSH interpreters forward it (`ssh -L 8080:127.0.0.1:8080`), so the page opens on
`localhost` either way.

![PHP Web Page](docs/screenshots/run-web-page.png)

> **Note:** the type "PHP Remote Debug" is declared by the Xdebug plugin but not available yet.
> To debug requests started elsewhere, use
> [Start Listening for PHP Debug Connections](docs/guide/user/debugging.md#listening-for-connections).

### Compound configurations

A **Compound** configuration starts several configurations together, for example the Laravel
server and the Vite dev server. Add the configurations with **+** and order them with the
arrows; a compound may contain other compounds.

![Compound configuration](docs/screenshots/run-configurations-compound.png)

- **Run** starts every member (after its own Before launch tasks), each in its own tab of the
  Run tool window. **Debug** debugs each member that can be debugged.
- **Stop** (`Ctrl+F2` or the toolbar's ■ while the compound is selected) stops all members.
- Without **Allow multiple instances**, running the compound again restarts members that still
  run; with it, new instances start next to them.
- Missing members and cycles are reported before anything starts.

### Before launch

Every configuration (except compounds) can run tasks before it starts. They run one after
another in the listed order; when a task fails (exit code other than 0, a missing
configuration or tool), the launch stops and a balloon says which task failed.

![Before launch tasks](docs/screenshots/run-configurations-before-launch.png)

| Task (**+** menu) | Value | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Run External tool | a tool of [External Tools](#external-tools) | runs the tool and waits for it |
| Run Another Configuration | a configuration | runs it (with its own Before launch tasks) and waits for it; a compound runs each member |
| Launch Web Browser | a URL | opens the URL |
| Run npm script | a script name | `<package manager> run <script>` in the configuration's working directory |
| Run Composer script | a script or command | `composer <script>` |
| Run Artisan command | a command (Laravel projects) | `php artisan <command>` through the configuration's interpreter |
| Run Shell Command… | a command line | runs it with the shell |

Each task runs in its own tab of the Run tool window. Reorder tasks with **↑** / **↓**.

### Where configurations are stored

| | File |
| --- | --- |
| Shared ("Store as project file") | `<project>/.forge/runConfigurations.toml` — commit it to share with your team |
| Local configurations, the selected one, templates | `<project>/.forge/runConfigurations.local.toml` |

## Temporary configurations

Gutter ▶ icons create temporary configurations: tests of PHPUnit, Pest, Codeception, Behat and
PHPSpec ([PHP test frameworks](docs/guide/user/test-frameworks.md#gutter-icons)), `package.json` scripts, Lua
main chunks, scratch files and HTTP requests. A double-click in the npm tool window and
commands run from [Run Anything](#run-anything) do the same.

## External Tools

**Settings | Tools | External Tools** lists programs you start from Forge with arguments
that come from the current file, caret or selection, such as linters, formatters or deploy
scripts. Tools are kept in your user settings (`tools.externalTools`), so they exist in every
project.

![External Tools](docs/screenshots/external-tools-settings.png)

The toolbar adds (**+**), removes, edits (or double-click), copies and moves tools; the check
boxes of tools and groups hide them from menus and the keymap without deleting them.

**Create Tool / Edit Tool**:

![Edit Tool](docs/screenshots/external-tools-edit.png)

- **Name**, **Group** (the submenu it appears in; default "External Tools") and
  **Description**.
- **Program**, **Arguments** and **Working directory** (default `$ProjectFileDir$`). Each can
  contain macros; **Insert Macro…** lists them with a preview of their value for the current
  editor:

  ![Insert Macro](docs/screenshots/external-tools-macros.png)

  | Macro | Value |
  | --- | --- |
  | `$FilePath$`, `$FileDir$`, `$FileName$`, `$FileNameWithoutExtension$`, `$FileNameWithoutAllExtensions$`, `$FileExt$`, `$FileDirName$`, `$FileParentDir$` | the file in the editor, or the file the Project view menu was opened on |
  | `$FilePathRelativeToProjectRoot$`, `$FileDirRelativeToProjectRoot$`, `$FileRelativePath$`, `$FileRelativeDir$` | the same, relative to the project |
  | `$ProjectFileDir$`, `$ContentRoot$`, `$ProjectName$` | the project |
  | `$LineNumber$`, `$ColumnNumber$`, `$SelectedText$`, `$SelectionStartLine$`, `$SelectionEndLine$`, `$SelectionStartColumn$`, `$SelectionEndColumn$` | caret and selection (1-based) |
  | `$ClipboardContent$` | the clipboard text |
  | `$Prompt$` | asks for a value when the tool runs (once per occurrence) |
  | `$PhpExecutable$` | the project's PHP interpreter |
  | `$FileEncoding$`, `$OSName$`, `$UserHome$` | file encoding, operating system, home directory |

  Arguments are split like a shell command line before the macros are expanded, so a path with
  spaces stays one argument. A macro without a value here (`$FilePath$` with no file open) is
  replaced by nothing and reported in a balloon.
- **Advanced Options**: **Synchronize files after execution** (refreshes the Project view),
  **Open console for tool output** (without it the tool runs in the background), **Make console
  active on message in stdout / stderr** (the console appears with the first such message) and
  **Output filters**.
- **Output filters** turn tool output into links: one regular expression per line with
  `$FILE_PATH$`, `$LINE$` and `$COLUMN$`, e.g. `$FILE_PATH$:$LINE$` or
  `^$FILE_PATH$:$LINE$:` for PHPStan's raw format. Everything else is a regular expression
  (escape `(` as `\(`). Invalid filters are reported when you click OK.

  ![Invalid output filter](docs/screenshots/external-tools-light.png)

Run a tool from:

- **Tools | External Tools**, ![Tools | External Tools](docs/screenshots/external-tools-menu.png)
- the editor's context menu (a submenu per group) and the Project view's context menu (the
  macros then use the clicked file), ![Editor context menu](docs/screenshots/external-tools-editor-menu.png)
- a shortcut: each tool is the action `Tool_<group>_<name>` in Settings | Keymap and Find
  Action,
- a [Before launch](#before-launch) task.

The output appears in the Run tool window, with the output filters' matches as links; tools run
on the machine that hosts the project (remote projects included).

![PHPStan run with an output filter](docs/screenshots/external-tools-run.png)

## Run tool window

The **Run** tool window (`Alt+4`) has one tab per run. Tabs can be pinned and closed (`Ctrl+Shift+F4`).

- Output is shown with ANSI colors; `\r` progress lines update in place.
- File references (`app/User.php:42`, stack traces) and URLs are clickable.
- Toolbar: **Rerun**, **Stop**, **Soft-Wrap**, **Scroll to the End**, **Clear All**.
- Typing sends input to the process (stdin).
- Stop sends SIGTERM to the process group, then SIGKILL after 2 seconds (`taskkill /T` on
  Windows).

Settings | Editor | General | Console: **Use soft wraps in console** (`run.console.softWrap`)
and **Override console cycle buffer size (KB)** (`run.console.cycleBufferKb`, 1024): a console
keeps the newest output up to that size and drops the oldest lines.

## Analyze Stack Trace

**Code | Analyze Stack Trace or Thread Dump…** (`AnalyzeStacktraceOnError`, no default
shortcut) opens a dialog to paste a stack trace from a log file, a bug report, an error page or
a server. When the clipboard holds a trace, the dialog starts with it.

![Analyze Stack Trace dialog](docs/screenshots/analyze-stack-trace.png)

**Analyze** opens it in a **Stack Trace** tab of the Run tool window. Every frame that names a
project file is a link to its line; the exception message is red, frames in libraries
(`vendor/`, `node_modules/`) and files outside the project are dimmed. **Rerun** opens the
dialog again with the same text.

![Stack trace in the Run tool window](docs/screenshots/stack-trace-tab.png)

Recognized formats:

| Language | Frames |
| --- | --- |
| PHP | `#0 /var/www/app/User.php(12): …`, `… in /path/File.php:42`, `… on line 7`, Laravel and Symfony exception traces and logs, Xdebug's `0.0012 402456 1. {main}() /path/index.php:0` |
| JavaScript / Node | `at fn (/app/src/cart.ts:10:5)`, `at /app/src/x.js:3:1`, `file:///…`, `webpack:///./src/…` |
| Lua | `main.lua:12: attempt to …`, `lib/util.lua:4: in function 'load'` |
| Others | any `path:line[:column]` or `path(line)` |

A trace copied from a JSON log as one line with escaped line breaks (`\n#1 …`) is split into
lines first.

Paths of a server or container are mapped into the project:

1. the path mappings of the PHP servers (Settings | PHP | Servers,
   [Debugging](docs/guide/user/debugging.md)),
2. the bind mounts of the project's Docker Compose file (`./:/var/www/html`),
3. the project root,
4. otherwise the longest trailing part of the path that exists in the project
   (`/srv/app/releases/42/app/Models/Order.php` → `app/Models/Order.php`).

Files are looked up through the project's backend, so this works in
[remote projects](docs/guide/user/remote-development.md) too. Detecting traces copied to the clipboard outside
Forge automatically is not supported.

## Test results

Test runners that speak TeamCity service messages (PHPUnit with `--teamcity`, Pest, Jest) or
write JUnit reports (Codeception, Behat, PHPSpec) show a **Test Results** tree next to the
console:

![PHPUnit test tree](docs/screenshots/run-phpunit-tree.png)

- Pass/fail/ignored per test with durations; **Show Passed**, **Show Ignored**, **Sort
  Alphabetically**, **Sort by Duration**, **Expand/Collapse All**.
- **Previous/Next Failed Test** and **Rerun Failed Tests**.
- **Toggle Auto-Test** reruns the tests after files are saved, and **Test History** reopens the
  last test runs of the project, see [PHP test frameworks](docs/guide/user/test-frameworks.md#test-history).
- A failed assertion shows a **Comparison Failure** with Expected and Actual.
- Double-click a test to open it.

## Debugging

**Debug** on a PHP configuration (PHP Script, PHPUnit, Artisan, Composer, PHP Built-in Web
Server) starts Forge's Xdebug listener and runs the process with the Xdebug environment
(`XDEBUG_MODE=debug`, `XDEBUG_SESSION`, `XDEBUG_CONFIG`). **Debug** on PHP Web Page, PHP HTTP
Request and requests of `.http` files starts listening and adds the Xdebug trigger to the
request. See [Debugging](docs/guide/user/debugging.md#debugging-web-pages-and-http-requests).

**Debug** on a Native Application configuration, or on a configuration type whose language
pack registers a debug adapter, starts a [debug adapter session](docs/guide/user/debugging.md#debug-adapter-sessions).

> **Note:** Run/Debug configurations work in [remote projects](docs/guide/user/remote-development.md): the
> process runs on the remote host.
