# PHP test frameworks

Forge runs the tests of PHPUnit, Pest, Codeception, Behat and PHPSpec projects the way
PHPStorm does: gutter ▶ icons on every test, a run configuration type per framework, the test
tree in the Run tool window with the results of each test, **Rerun Failed Tests**, the **Test
History** and **auto-test**. Every run goes through the project's
[CLI interpreter](docs/guide/user/php.md#cli-interpreters), so tests run locally, in Docker, Docker Compose,
over SSH or in WSL alike.

![Pest tests from the gutter](docs/screenshots/test-frameworks-pest.png)

## Settings | PHP | Test Frameworks

**Settings | Languages & Frameworks | PHP | Test Frameworks** (`php.testFrameworks`, stored per
project) lists one configuration per framework and interpreter, like PHPStorm:

![Test Frameworks settings](docs/screenshots/test-frameworks-settings.png)

- **+** adds PHPUnit, Pest, Codeception, Behat or PHPSpec, **Local** or **by Remote
  Interpreter** (one of the [CLI interpreters](docs/guide/user/php.md#cli-interpreters)); **−** removes it.
- **<Framework> library**: **Use Composer autoloader** with the path to `vendor/autoload.php`
  (the framework's script in `vendor/bin` is run), or **Path to <executable>** (a script or a
  phar such as `phpunit.phar`).
- **Test Runner**: the **Default configuration file** (`phpunit.xml`, `codeception.yml`,
  `behat.yml`, `phpspec.yml`) and, for PHPUnit and PHPSpec, the **Default bootstrap file**.
  A run configuration's own configuration file wins.
- Frameworks the project uses but that are not configured are listed as **detected**: from
  `require-dev` of composer.json, the scripts in `vendor/bin` and the frameworks'
  configuration files (`tests/Pest.php` for Pest). Changing a detected entry adds it.
- A run uses the entry of its interpreter, else the Local one.

**Auto-test delay (seconds)** (`run.autoTest.delay`, default 3) is on the same page, see
[Auto-test](#auto-test).

## Run configurations

**Run | Edit Configurations…** has a type per framework (PHPUnit is described in
[Run/Debug configurations](docs/guide/user/run-debug.md#configuration-types)). The gutter icons and
**Run Context Configuration** (`Ctrl+Shift+F10`) create temporary configurations of these types.

![A Pest configuration](docs/screenshots/test-frameworks-pest-configuration.png)

| Type | Test scope | Runs | Results |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Pest | Directory, File, Test (a `test()`, `it()` or `describe()` description), Defined in the configuration file | `pest --teamcity [--configuration f] [path] [--filter …]` | streamed TeamCity messages |
| Codeception | Type (suite), Directory, File, Method, Defined in the configuration file; Groups, Environments | `codecept run [suite \| file[:method]] [-g group] [--env env] [-c f] --xml <report>` | the JUnit report read when the run ends |
| Behat | Directory, File, Scenario (feature file and line), Defined in the configuration file; Profile | `behat [--config f] [--profile p] --format=progress --out=std --format=junit --out=<reports>` | progress in the console, the JUnit reports in the tree |
| PHPSpec | Directory, Spec, Example (spec file and line), Defined in the configuration file | `phpspec run --format=junit --no-interaction [--config f] [--bootstrap f] [file[:line]]` | the JUnit document on stdout |

Every type has **Configuration file** and **Test runner options**, plus the common fields
(interpreter, interpreter options, working directory, environment variables, Before launch).
**Debug** (`Shift+F9`) runs the tests with Xdebug.

Codeception and Behat write their JUnit reports into a folder that Forge reads and deletes
when the run ends: the system temp folder when the project and the interpreter are local,
otherwise `.forge/test-reports/` inside the project, which a container or remote host reaches
through the interpreter's path mappings.

## Gutter icons

A green ▶ in the gutter runs or debugs a test, or opens **Modify Run Configuration…**. After a
run the icon shows the test's last result (✓ passed, ✗ failed).

| File | Icons |
| --- | --- |
| PHPUnit test class (`*Test`, extends `…TestCase`) | the class, `test*` methods, `@test` and `#[Test]` methods |
| Pest file | every `test()`, `it()` and `describe()` call, every row of an inline `->with([...])` dataset |
| Codeception `*Cest.php`, `*Cept.php`, `extends \Codeception\Test\Unit` | the class or file, public Cest methods, `test*` methods |
| Behat `.feature` | the feature, every scenario and scenario outline, every example row |
| PHPSpec `*Spec.php` (`extends ObjectBehavior`) | the spec, every `it_*` and `its_*` example |

The tests of a file are found in Rust while you type.

## Test results

The test tree of the Run tool window works for every framework:

![Behat results](docs/screenshots/test-frameworks-behat.png)

- Pass, fail and ignored state with durations, **Show Passed** / **Show Ignored**, sorting,
  **Previous/Next Failed Test** and double-click to open a test. Pest tests open at their
  `test()` / `it()` call, Behat scenarios at their `Scenario:` line, Codeception tests at the
  line of the report.
- A failed comparison shows **<Click to see difference>**.
- **Rerun Failed Tests** runs only the failed tests: PHPUnit and Pest with `--filter`,
  Codeception with `-g failed` (Codeception's list of the failed tests), Behat with `--rerun`,
  PHPSpec the failed spec file.

![Codeception results with auto-test on](docs/screenshots/test-frameworks-codeception.png)

![PHPSpec results](docs/screenshots/test-frameworks-phpspec.png)

### Test History

The **Test History** button (clock with an arrow) in the test tree's toolbar lists the last
ten test runs of the project with their result and time. Picking one opens it in a Run tab
with its tree and failure details; **Rerun** runs its configuration again. Runs are kept in
Forge's data folder (`<data dir>/forge/test-history/<project>/`), never in the project. Find
Action: **Test History…**.

![Test History](docs/screenshots/test-frameworks-history.png)

### Auto-test

**Toggle Auto-Test** in the Run tool window's toolbar (or Find Action) reruns that tab's
configuration automatically after files are saved, once the auto-test delay passed since the
last save (`run.autoTest.delay`, default 3 seconds). A run that is still going finishes first.

## Behat

`.feature` files are highlighted as Gherkin: `Feature`, `Background`, `Scenario`,
`Scenario Outline` and `Examples` headings, the step keywords `Given`, `When`, `Then`, `And`,
`But` and `*`, tags, comments, tables (with the header row of examples), doc strings, quoted
arguments, numbers and `<placeholders>`.

**Go to Declaration** (`Ctrl+B`, `Ctrl+Click`) on a step opens its step definition: the
context method whose pattern matches the step, from a doc comment (`@Given /^I have (\d+)
apples?$/`, `@When I add :product to the basket`) or an attribute (`#[Given('…')]`,
`#[\Behat\Step\Then("…")]`). Turnip patterns support `:placeholders` (a quoted string or a
word), optional parts such as `product(s)` and alternatives such as `buy/purchase`; steps of a
scenario outline match with the values of the first example row. Several matching
definitions open a chooser.

![Go to the step definition](docs/screenshots/test-frameworks-behat-step.png)

> **Note:** Gherkin keywords in other languages (`# language: de`) are not supported yet.

# Command Line Tool Support

The Command Line Tools Console runs the command line tools of a PHP project, like PHPStorm's
Command Line Tool Support: Composer, Laravel Artisan, Symfony Console, WP-CLI, Drush, any tool
built on Symfony Console, and plain PHP scripts. You type a command as
`alias command [arguments]`, for example `c require laravel/sanctum`,
`a make:model Order -m` or `s cache:clear`, and Forge completes commands, options and
arguments as you type.

The feature is the plugin **Command Line Tool Support** (`forge.command-line-tools`) of the
PHPForge pack. It is active in PHP and Composer projects.

## Run Command

**Tools | Run Command…** (`Ctrl+Shift+X`, macOS `Cmd+Shift+X`, action id
`CommandLineToolsAction`) opens the Run Command popup. Its header lists the aliases of the
project's tools.

![Run Command popup with command completion](docs/screenshots/cli-tools-commands.png)

| Key | Action |
| --- | --- |
| typing | completion of the alias, the command, options, option values and arguments |
| `Tab` | insert the selected (or first) completion item |
| `↓` / `↑` | move through the completion list; with no list, browse the history |
| `Enter` | run the command (or insert the item you moved to with the arrow keys) |
| `Ctrl+C` | stop the running command (when nothing is selected in the input) |
| `Esc` | close the completion list, then the popup |

Completion knows:

- **aliases** of the configured tools (also found by the tool's name),
- **commands**, by prefix, by any part (`model` finds `make:model`) and by Symfony-style
  abbreviations (`m:mi` for `make:migration`, `d:s:u` for `doctrine:schema:update`);
  WP-CLI subcommands word by word (`wp plugin list`),
- **options** (`--migration`, `-m`) of the command, the command's own first and the
  application's global ones (`--help`, `--ansi`, `--env`) after them; options you already used
  are not offered again unless they may repeat,
- **option values** that the tool lists (WP-CLI `--format=table|csv|json|…`),
- **arguments**: the expected argument is shown below the input (`<name>: The name of the
  model`); `help <command_name>` completes command names and `list <namespace>` namespaces.

While you type the arguments of a command, the help of the command is shown under the list:
its description, usage, arguments and options, with the argument or option at the cursor
highlighted. Hovering a completion item shows its description.

![Options with the command's help](docs/screenshots/cli-tools-options.png)

## The console and the output

A command's output goes to the **Command Line Tools Console** tool window (one tab per
command), or stays in the popup when the tool's **Show console in** is **Pop-up window**.
The console shows the command line, colored output, clickable file paths (`app/Models/Order.php`
opens in the editor) and URLs, and the exit code (`Process finished with exit code 0`). Input
typed into a running console goes to the command (questions of `make:` commands, `tinker`).

![Command Line Tools Console tool window](docs/screenshots/cli-tools-console.png)

The tool window has an input with completion at the bottom (the completion opens above it),
and a toolbar with **Rerun**, **Stop**, **Scroll to the End**, **Soft-Wrap** and **Clear
All**. Its header has **Reload Command Lists** and a link to the settings. Middle-click or `×`
closes a tab.

Commands run where the project's PHP runs: through the tool's PHP interpreter, or the project
default of Settings | PHP | CLI Interpreter, including Docker, Docker Compose, SSH and WSL
interpreters (see [PHP](docs/guide/user/php.md)). Container paths in the output are mapped back to project
files, so links work there too. Remote projects run the tools on the remote host.

## Command lists and the cache

Forge reads the commands of a tool by running it once:

| Tool | List command |
| --- | --- |
| Composer, Laravel Artisan, Symfony Console, Drush, Tool based on Symfony Console | `<tool> list --format=json` |
| WP-CLI | `wp cli cmd-dump` |
| Tool based on PHP script | none (no completion of commands) |

The result is cached per project and tool in Forge's cache directory
(`<cache dir>/forge/command-line-tools`) and reused until the tool's path, its interpreter or
`composer.lock` changes, so installing or updating packages brings new commands in. **Reload
Command Lists** (in the popup header and the tool window header) lists all tools again. When
Artisan or the Symfony console cannot run (no `vendor/`, a broken application), the standard
commands of Laravel or Symfony are offered instead.

## Settings | Tools | Command Line Tool Support

![Command Line Tool Support settings](docs/screenshots/cli-tools-settings.png)

The table lists the project's tools. Tools the project uses are **auto-detected** (shown in
italics) as long as no tool of that kind or alias is configured:

| Tool | Detected from | Alias | Path |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Composer | `composer.json` | `c` | the Composer executable of Settings \| PHP \| Composer (`composer`) |
| Laravel Artisan | `artisan` | `a` | `artisan` |
| Symfony Console | `bin/console` | `s` | `bin/console` |
| WP-CLI | `wp-cli.phar`, `vendor/bin/wp`, or a WordPress site (`wp-config.php`, `wp-content/`) | `wp` | `wp-cli.phar`, `vendor/bin/wp` or `wp` |
| Drush | `vendor/bin/drush` | `drush` | `vendor/bin/drush` |

**Tools | WP-CLI…** ([WordPress](docs/guide/user/wordpress.md#wp-cli)), **Tools | Drush…** and **Tools |
Shopware Console…** ([Drupal, Joomla and Shopware](docs/guide/user/cms.md#drush-and-the-shopware-console))
open the console with the tool's alias typed in.

**+** opens **Choose Tool to Add** with these tools plus **Tool based on Symfony Console** and
**Tool based on PHP script** (any PHP script, run as `php <script> <arguments>`). **−**
removes a tool, the pencil (or a double-click) edits it; editing an auto-detected tool adds it
to the list. The checkbox turns a tool off. Each tool has:

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Name | shown in the table, the popup header and the tool window |
| Alias | the first word of a command line; unique, without spaces |
| Path | a project script (`artisan`, `bin/console`), a `.phar` (run with PHP) or a program name (`composer`, `wp`) |
| PHP interpreter | the CLI interpreter that runs it; **Project default** uses Settings \| PHP |
| Show console in | **Tool window** or **Pop-up window** |

Scripts and `.phar` files always run with the PHP interpreter. Programs such as `composer` or
`wp` run as they are, and inside the interpreter's environment (for example in the Docker
container) when the tool names an interpreter.

The tools are stored in the project settings (`commandLineTools.tools`), so a team can share
them through `.forge/settings.toml`. **Add the tools the project uses automatically**
(`commandLineTools.autoDetect`) turns auto-detection off.

## Laravel and Symfony

**Tools | Laravel | Run Artisan Command…** opens the Run Command popup with the Artisan alias
typed in. The Symfony plugin keeps its own **Run Console Command…** list with the
application's commands and gutter icons (see [Symfony](docs/guide/user/symfony.md)). For commands you run often
with a debugger, create an **Artisan** or **Composer** run configuration
(see [Run/Debug configurations](docs/guide/user/run-debug.md)).

Source: docs/guide/user/debugging.md

# Debugging

Forge has one debugger for every language. The **Debug** tool window (`Alt+5`), breakpoints in
the editor, stepping, variables, watches, Evaluate Expression and the console work the same
for every session; only how a session starts differs:

- **PHP** uses the Xdebug plugin (`forge.xdebug`, PHPForge pack): a DBGp server for **Xdebug 3**
  that accepts any number of connections at once, from the CLI, a web server, Docker
  containers or another machine.
- **Every other language** uses a **debug adapter** that speaks the
  [Debug Adapter Protocol](https://microsoft.github.io/debug-adapter-protocol/) (DAP), through
  the Debugger plugin (`forge.debugger`). **LLDB** (`lldb-dap`) and **GDB** (14 or newer,
  `gdb -i dap`) are built in for C, C++, Rust, Go and other native code; language packs add
  their own adapters. Adapters are programs installed on your machine; Forge does not bundle
  them. See [Debug adapter sessions](#debug-adapter-sessions) below.

The sections up to [Debug adapter sessions](#debug-adapter-sessions) describe Xdebug; the
breakpoints and the Debug tool window are shared.

## Preparing PHP

Install Xdebug 3 and enable step debugging in your `php.ini` (or the container's):

```ini
zend_extension=xdebug
xdebug.mode=debug
xdebug.client_port=9003
; for web requests: start on every request, or use a browser extension / XDEBUG_SESSION cookie
xdebug.start_with_request=trigger
; when PHP runs in Docker or on another machine
; xdebug.client_host=host.docker.internal
```

Forge listens on port **9003** (`php.debug.port`).

## Two ways to start

### Debug a run configuration

Press **Debug** (`Shift+F9`) on a PHP Script, PHPUnit, Artisan or Composer configuration (or a
gutter ▶ menu). Forge starts listening and runs the process with:

```text
XDEBUG_MODE=debug
XDEBUG_SESSION=FORGE
XDEBUG_CONFIG=client_host=127.0.0.1 client_port=9003 idekey=FORGE
PHP_IDE_CONFIG=serverName=<server>   (when a server is chosen)
```

so no `php.ini` change is needed for CLI scripts and tests.

### Listening for connections

For web requests, click the telephone icon **Start Listening for PHP Debug Connections** in
the main toolbar (action `PhpListenDebugAction`). The status bar shows that Forge is listening;
click again to stop. Then open the page with Xdebug triggered (`XDEBUG_SESSION` cookie, query
parameter or browser extension).

![Incoming connection](docs/screenshots/debugger-incoming.png)

### Debugging web pages and HTTP requests

These configurations start listening by themselves when you press **Debug** (`Shift+F9`):

| Configuration | Debug |
| --- | --- |
| **PHP Built-in Web Server** | runs `php -S host:port -t <document root> [router script]` with the Xdebug environment and `-dxdebug.start_with_request=yes`, so every request it serves is debugged; opens the page in the browser |
| **PHP Web Page** | opens the start URL on a server of Settings \| PHP \| Servers with `?XDEBUG_SESSION_START=FORGE` (Xdebug then sets the `XDEBUG_SESSION` cookie for the following requests) |
| **PHP HTTP Request** | sends the request (method, URL, headers, body) with the cookie `XDEBUG_SESSION=FORGE` |
| Requests in `.http` files | click the gutter ▶ and choose **Debug '…' with Xdebug**: the request is sent with the cookie |

![Debug an .http request](docs/screenshots/http-debug-menu.png)

The Run tool window shows the cookie of a debugged request:

![Debugged request](docs/screenshots/http-debug-run.png)

When a connection comes from an unknown server whose script is not a project file, the
**Incoming Connection From Xdebug** dialog asks which project file the server file maps to and
creates a server with that path mapping. Turn on **Ignore external connections through
unregistered server configurations** (`php.debug.ignoreExternalConnections`) to detach such
connections silently.

## Breakpoints

- Click a line number in a PHP file, or in a file of a debug adapter's languages (`.c`, `.cpp`,
  `.rs`, `.go`, …), or press **Toggle Line Breakpoint** (`Ctrl+F8`, macOS `Cmd+F8`).
- Right-click a breakpoint to set a **condition** (an expression of the file's language; the
  program suspends only when it is true) or disable it.
- **View Breakpoints…** (`Ctrl+Shift+F8`) lists all breakpoints: **PHP Line Breakpoints**,
  **Line Breakpoints** of other languages, **Function Breakpoints**, **Watchpoints**, **PHP
  Exception Breakpoints** (an exception class, or `*` for any) and the exception filters of
  debug adapters (for example LLDB's "C++: on throw").
- **Mute Breakpoints** turns all of them off temporarily.

![Breakpoint condition](docs/screenshots/debugger-condition-popup.png)

![Breakpoints dialog](docs/screenshots/debugger-breakpoints.png)

Breakpoints are stored in `<project>/.forge/breakpoints.json`.

### Breakpoint properties, logpoints and temporary breakpoints

The right side of **View Breakpoints…** (and the popup of a right-click on a breakpoint) has
PHPStorm's properties:

| Property | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| **Enabled** | off keeps the breakpoint without stopping |
| **Suspend execution** | off makes a **logpoint**: Forge logs and lets the script run on (yellow dot) |
| **Condition** | an expression; Xdebug or the debug adapter stops only when it is true |
| **Log: "Breakpoint hit" message** | prints `Breakpoint reached at <file>:<line>` to the session's Console |
| **Log: Stack trace** | prints the frames |
| **Evaluate and log** | evaluates an expression in the frame and prints its value (debug adapters: `{expr}` in the text is replaced, e.g. `i={i} sum={sum}`) |
| **Remove once hit** | a **temporary breakpoint**: removed after it suspended once (dot with a ring) |
| **Pass count** | stops only from the n-th hit on (Xdebug's hit condition `>=`, a DAP hit condition) |

- **Shift+click** on a line number adds a logpoint ("Breakpoint hit" message, no suspend) and
  opens its properties.
- **Toggle Temporary Line Breakpoint** (`Ctrl+Alt+Shift+F8`, macOS `Cmd+Alt+Shift+F8`) adds a
  breakpoint that is removed once hit.
- **PHP Exception Breakpoints** (**+** in the dialog) stop when an exception of the class (or
  a subclass) is thrown; `*` stops on any exception. They have the same log options.

![Logpoint properties](docs/screenshots/debugger-logpoint.png)

Logged lines appear in the **Console** tab of the debug session:

![Logpoint output](docs/screenshots/debugger-logpoint-output.png)

## The Debug tool window

![Paused](docs/screenshots/debugger-paused.png)

While paused, the execution point is highlighted in the editor and variable values are shown
inline at the end of lines (`php.debug.showInlineValues`). The **Debug** tool window (`Alt+5`)
has a tab per session with:

- **Threads & Variables**: the frames on the left (click to switch), variables on the right.
  Arrays and objects expand lazily.
- **Console**: the script's output, logpoint messages, and a field at the bottom that
  evaluates PHP expressions in the selected frame (see below).
- The evaluate field at the top: type an expression and press `Enter` to evaluate it, or
  `Ctrl+Shift+Enter` to add it as a watch.

| Action | Windows/Linux | macOS |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Resume Program | `F9` | `Cmd+Alt+R` |
| Pause Program | toolbar | toolbar |
| Step Over | `F8` | `F8` |
| Step Into | `F7` | `F7` |
| Smart Step Into | `Shift+F7` | `Shift+F7` |
| Force Step Into | `Alt+Shift+F7` | `Alt+Shift+F7` |
| Step Out | `Shift+F8` | `Shift+F8` |
| Run to Cursor | `Alt+F9` | `Alt+F9` |
| Force Run to Cursor | `Ctrl+Alt+F9` | `Cmd+Alt+F9` |
| Evaluate Expression… | `Alt+F8` | `Alt+F8` |
| Quick Evaluate Expression | `Ctrl+Alt+F8` | `Cmd+Alt+F8` |
| Show Execution Point | `Alt+F10` | `Alt+F10` |
| Stop | `Ctrl+F2` | `Cmd+F2` |
| Add to Watches | context menu | context menu |
| Set Value… | `F2` | `F2` |
| Toggle Temporary Line Breakpoint | `Ctrl+Alt+Shift+F8` | `Cmd+Alt+Shift+F8` |

![Evaluate Expression](docs/screenshots/debugger-evaluate.png)

### Variables: Set Value and Copy Value

Right-click a variable or watch for **Set Value…** (`F2`), **Copy Value** (arrays and objects
as `print_r` output), **Copy Name**, **Evaluate Expression…** and **Add to Watches**. Set Value
edits the value in place: type a PHP expression (`'paid'`, `42`, `null`, `$other`) and press
`Enter` (Xdebug's `property_set`); `Escape` cancels. The variables and watches reload after the
change.

![Set Value](docs/screenshots/debugger-set-value.png)

![Variable context menu](docs/screenshots/debugger-variable-menu.png)

### Evaluate Expression and the debugger console

The **Evaluate** dialog (`Alt+F8`) and the field at the bottom of the **Console** tab evaluate a
PHP expression in the selected frame (Xdebug's `eval`). Both complete variable names after `$`
and properties after `->` (from the suspended script, `Enter` or `Tab` accepts) and keep a
history of evaluated expressions: `Up` / `Down` in the field, or the history button. Console
results are trees that expand like variables.

![Debugger console](docs/screenshots/debugger-console.png)

Smart Step Into currently behaves like Step Into. Pause depends on the engine and may
report "Pause is not supported by this engine".

## Debug adapter sessions

A debug adapter session drives the same Debug tool window as Xdebug. What the window offers
depends on the adapter (its capabilities): threads, memory, disassembly and registers appear
only when the adapter supports them.

![Debug adapter session](docs/screenshots/dap-session.png)

### Starting a session

| How | Where |
| --- | --- |
| **Debug** a run configuration (`Shift+F9`) | a **Native Application** configuration (executable, program arguments, working directory, debugger, "Stop at the beginning of the program", launch options as JSON), or a configuration type of a language pack that uses an adapter |
| **Attach to Process…** (`Ctrl+Alt+F5`, macOS `Cmd+Alt+F5`) | Run menu: pick a local process (filter by name, command line or PID) and an adapter that can attach |
| **Attach to DAP Server…** | Run menu: connect to an adapter that already listens on a TCP port (`dlv dap --listen 127.0.0.1:4711`, `debugpy --listen 5678`), with optional attach options as JSON |
| **Debug Core Dump…** | Run menu: open a core file with the executable that crashed (LLDB); nothing runs, frames, variables, memory and registers show the state at the crash |

![Attach to Process](docs/screenshots/dap-attach-process.png)

> **Note:** starting a program under the debugger runs project code, so it is refused in
> [Safe Mode](docs/guide/user/project-trust.md). Attaching to a running process or DAP server and opening a
> core dump are allowed.

Program output and the adapter's messages appear in the **Console** tab. Programs that need a
terminal (the adapter's `runInTerminal` request) are started by Forge with their output in the
console; adapters that start child sessions (`startDebugging`, e.g. for subprocesses) get a
session tab per child.

### Threads, variables and the console

- The frames pane has a thread selector; the thread that stopped is marked "(stopped)".
- Variables expand lazily. Scopes other than the locals (globals, statics) are groups at the
  end of the tree.
- Watches belong to the debugger: PHP sessions keep their watches, a C session has its own.
- The console and Evaluate (`Alt+F8`) evaluate in the adapter's language (LLDB also accepts
  its commands) and complete names while you type.
- Values are shown inline in the editor (`debugger.showInlineValues`).
- **Rerun** in the toolbar restarts the session (in place when the adapter supports it).

### Logpoints and watchpoints

Logpoints (**Suspend execution** off, `Shift`+click on a line number) are evaluated by the
adapter when it supports them, so the program does not stop at all; otherwise Forge logs and
resumes. In **Evaluate and log**, `{expression}` is replaced by its value: `i={i} sum={sum}`
prints `i=2 sum=1`; a plain expression `counter` prints `counter = 6`.

![Logpoint output and completion](docs/screenshots/dap-console-logpoint.png)

![Breakpoints dialog with a logpoint](docs/screenshots/dap-breakpoints.png)

**Add Watchpoint** in the context menu of a variable adds a data breakpoint: the program stops
when the value changes. It is listed under **Watchpoints** in View Breakpoints…, where
**Suspend on** chooses write, read or both (as far as the adapter supports it). **Function
Breakpoints** (**+** in the dialog) stop when a function is entered (`main`,
`MyClass::method`).

### Memory, disassembly and registers

| Tab | Shows |
| --- | --- |
| **Memory** | hex and ASCII from an address; type an address or `&variable`, page with the arrows, or choose **View Memory** on a variable. Double-click a byte to change it (when the adapter can write memory). |
| **Disassembly** | the instructions around the selected frame's instruction pointer with symbols and source lines; **Step Over Instruction** and **Step Into Instruction** step one machine instruction |
| **Registers** | the registers of the selected frame |

![Memory view](docs/screenshots/dap-memory.png)

![Disassembly](docs/screenshots/dap-disassembly.png)

![Registers](docs/screenshots/dap-registers.png)

| Action | Default shortcut |
| --- | --- |
| Attach to Process… | `Ctrl+Alt+F5` (macOS `Cmd+Alt+F5`) |
| Attach to DAP Server…, Debug Core Dump… | Run menu |
| Step Over Instruction, Step Into Instruction | Disassembly tab (assign keys in Settings \| Keymap) |
| Add Watchpoint, Set Execution Point to Cursor | context menu / Find Action |
| Rerun Debug Session | Debug toolbar |

### Settings | Build, Execution, Deployment | Debugger

| Option | Setting | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| LLDB DAP executable | `debugger.lldb.path` | empty: `lldb-dap` on the PATH |
| GDB executable | `debugger.gdb.path` | empty: `gdb` on the PATH |
| Debug adapter request timeout (ms) | `debugger.dap.requestTimeout` | 10000 |
| Log Debug Adapter Protocol messages | `debugger.dap.trace` | off |
| Show variable values in editor while debugging | `debugger.showInlineValues` | on |
| Memory view: bytes per row | `debugger.memory.bytesPerRow` | 16 |

Language packs add their adapters to the same settings page and dialogs (see
[contribution points](docs/guide/developer/contribution-points.md)).

## Servers and path mappings

When PHP runs in a container or on another machine, its file paths differ from yours. Define a
**server** in Settings | Languages & Frameworks | PHP | **Servers**: **Name**, **Host**,
**Port**, **Debugger** (Xdebug) and **Use path mappings**: the project's folders as a tree,
with the **Absolute path on the server** of each mapped folder (usually just the project root,
e.g. `/var/www/html`; a deeper mapping such as `vendor` wins for its files).

![Servers](docs/screenshots/debugger-servers.png)

A session finds its server from `PHP_IDE_CONFIG=serverName=<name>`, otherwise from
`$_SERVER['SERVER_NAME']` and `SERVER_PORT`. Servers are stored in
`<project>/.forge/php-servers.json`.

## Web Server Debug Validation

**Run | Web Server Debug Validation…** (PHPStorm's "Validate Debugger Configuration on Web
Server") checks whether PHP can connect to Forge:

- **Local Web Server or Shared Folder**: Forge writes a temporary script
  `forge_xdebug_validator_*.php` into the project folder that the web server serves (**Path to
  create validation script**, e.g. `public`), requests it under **URL to validation script**
  and deletes it right after the check. Nothing is written before you press **Validate**.
- **CLI Interpreter**: reads `php -i` of a [CLI interpreter](docs/guide/user/php.md#cli-interpreters) (also
  Docker, Compose, SSH or WSL ones).

Each check shows ✓ (fine), ⚠ (works with conditions) or ✗ (must be fixed) with a hint: the
Xdebug version, `xdebug.mode` (must include `debug`), `xdebug.client_host` (localhost cannot
reach Forge from a container or another machine), `xdebug.client_port` (must be Forge's
`php.debug.port`), `xdebug.start_with_request` (`trigger` needs the cookie or
`XDEBUG_SESSION_START`) and the server name used to find path mappings. For CLI interpreters,
Forge sets mode, host, port and session itself for debug runs, so only the extension matters.
The path and URL are remembered per project (`php.debug.validation.documentRoot`,
`php.debug.validation.url`).

![Web Server Debug Validation](docs/screenshots/debugger-validation.png)

## Settings | Languages & Frameworks | PHP | Debug

![Debug settings](docs/screenshots/debugger-settings.png)

| Option | Setting | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Debug port | `php.debug.port` | 9003 |
| Ignore external connections through unregistered server configurations | `php.debug.ignoreExternalConnections` | off |
| Break at first line in PHP scripts | `php.debug.breakAtFirstLine` | off |
| Step out of files that are not mapped into the project | `php.debug.ignoreUnmappedFiles` | on |
| Show variable values in editor while debugging | `php.debug.showInlineValues` | on |
| Max. children (array elements / properties per page) | `php.debug.maxChildren` | 100 |
| Max. depth (levels fetched at once) | `php.debug.maxDepth` | 1 |
| Max. string length (bytes) | `php.debug.maxData` | 65536 |
| Path to create validation script | `php.debug.validation.documentRoot` | `public` |
| URL to validation script | `php.debug.validation.url` | `http://localhost:8080` |

## Remote projects

In a [remote project](docs/guide/user/remote-development.md), **Start Listening** listens on a free local port
and asks the remote host, over SSH, to listen on `127.0.0.1:<php.debug.port>` (9003) and forward
connections to Forge (a reverse tunnel, re-established after reconnects). Configure Xdebug on
the host with `xdebug.client_host=127.0.0.1`. Xdebug's paths are the host's paths, which are the
project's, so no path mappings are needed. The status bar shows that the listener goes through
the host.

![Listening through the host](docs/screenshots/remote-parity-debug-listening.png)

![Remote debug session](docs/screenshots/remote-parity-debug-session.png)

> **Note:** JavaScript and Node.js debugging are not built in; see
> [WebForge](docs/guide/user/webforge.md#debugging-scripts).

# Terminal

The **Terminal** tool window (`Alt+F12`, bottom stripe) runs your shell on a real pseudo
terminal (xterm.js in the UI, a PTY in Rust), so interactive programs such as `vim`, `htop`,
`git rebase -i`, `php artisan tinker` or Claude Code work.

![Terminal tabs](docs/screenshots/terminal-tabs.png)

## Tabs

| Action | Windows/Linux | macOS |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Show/hide the terminal | `Alt+F12` | `Alt+F12` |
| New tab | `Ctrl+Shift+T` | `Cmd+T` |
| Close tab | `Ctrl+Shift+F4` | `Cmd+Shift+F4` |

Tabs are named "Local", "Local (2)", …; while a program runs that sets a title (OSC 0 / OSC 2,
e.g. Claude Code's current task), the tab shows that title instead (**Show application title**).
Double-click a tab or use **Rename Session** to rename it; a renamed tab keeps its name. The arrow next to **+** has **New Tab**, **New Tab in Current Directory**, **SSH Session…**
(see [SSH sessions](#ssh-sessions)), **Rename Session** and **Clear Buffer**. A
tab's context menu has **New Tab**, **New Tab in Current Directory** (the directory the shell
reports, see below), **Rename Session**, **Close Tab** and **Close Other Tabs**. The terminal
area's context menu has **Copy** (`Ctrl+Shift+C`), **Paste** (`Ctrl+Shift+V`), **Select All**
and **Clear Buffer**.

On Windows, the arrow next to **+** also offers `WSL: <distro>` for every WSL distribution: a
shell in that distribution, in the project folder (see
[Dev Containers and WSL](docs/guide/user/dev-containers-and-wsl.md#terminal--wsl)). In projects opened in a dev
container or a WSL distribution, every tab is a shell there.

## Program progress

Programs such as Claude Code, winget or systemd report their progress with the OSC 9;4
sequence. Forge shows it:

- on the **terminal tab**: a ring filled to the percentage, or a spinning arc while the
  program is busy without a percentage;
- in the **status bar** (**Show progress in the status bar**): the ring plus
  "&lt;tab title&gt;: 42%", "Working…", "Error 60%" or "Paused"; click it to show the tab;
- on the **Terminal stripe icon** while the tool window is hidden: the combined progress of
  all tabs (errors first, then paused, then the slowest).

Errors are drawn in the danger color, paused progress in the warning color. The progress
disappears when the program removes it, when the shell shows its next prompt (OSC 133) or
when the shell exits.

![Claude Code with progress](docs/screenshots/terminal-claude-session.png)

![Progress on the stripe icon and in the status bar](docs/screenshots/terminal-progress-hidden.png)

## Notifications and bell

OSC 9 (iTerm2) and OSC 777 (`notify;<title>;<body>`) notifications appear as balloons when
the tab is not visible or Forge is not focused; **Show** opens the tab. The bell flashes the
terminal when the tab is visible and otherwise puts a dot on the tab and on the stripe icon;
with **Audible bell** it also beeps.

## Keyboard

While the terminal has focus, plain `Ctrl`+letter, `Alt`+letter and `Escape` go to the shell
(so `Ctrl+C`, `Ctrl+R`, `Alt+B` behave as in any terminal). Function keys, `Alt`+digit,
`Ctrl+Shift` and `Ctrl+Alt` combinations still reach the IDE, so `Alt+1` or `Shift+Escape`
work from the terminal.

`Shift+Enter` sends ESC CR and `Ctrl+Enter` sends LF, so TUI programs such as Claude Code
insert a newline instead of submitting. On macOS, **Use Option as Meta key** makes `Option`
work as `Alt` in the shell.

## Links

URLs and OSC 8 hyperlinks in the output open with `Ctrl+Click` (`Cmd+Click` on macOS), so a
plain click still selects text; hovering one shows its target at the bottom of the terminal.
Only `http(s)` and `mailto` links open in the browser and `file://` links only open files of
the project; other links are refused. File references such as `app/Models/User.php:42` are
underlined and open in the editor at that line with a click.

## Rendering

The terminal draws with WebGL on the GPU and falls back to the DOM renderer when WebGL is not
available or its context is lost (**Renderer**). Emoji, East Asian characters, braille spinners
and Nerd Font glyphs take the widths modern terminals use (Unicode 15 and grapheme clusters),
and box drawing characters line up without gaps. The font is **Font** (empty: the editor font),
followed by common monospace fonts, Nerd Fonts, color emoji and symbol fonts for missing glyphs.
Settings changes apply to open terminals right away.

## Shell and start directory

The shell is, in this order: Settings | Tools | Terminal | **Shell path**
(`terminal.shellPath`), `$SHELL` on Linux/macOS (then bash, zsh, sh), on Windows PowerShell 7
(`pwsh.exe`), Windows PowerShell or `%ComSpec%`. bash, zsh and fish start as login shells.

New tabs start in the project root unless **Start directory** (`terminal.startDirectory`) is
set; **Environment variables** (`terminal.environment`, one `NAME=value` per entry) are added.

The shell also gets `TERM=xterm-256color`, `COLORTERM=truecolor`, `TERM_PROGRAM=Forge`,
`TERM_PROGRAM_VERSION=<Forge version>` and `FORGE_TERMINAL=1`, and a UTF-8 `LANG` when none is
set. Variables of the terminal Forge itself was started from (kitty, tmux, iTerm2, WezTerm,
Ghostty, …) are removed, so programs do not mistake Forge for that terminal.

Shells that report their directory (OSC 7, or ConEmu's OSC 9;9) let **New Tab in Current
Directory** open the new tab there. Closing a tab ends the shell; a shell that ignores the
hang-up signal is killed after 1.5 seconds.

## Settings | Tools | Terminal

| Option | Setting | Default | Scope |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Shell path | `terminal.shellPath` | system default | user |
| Default tab name | `terminal.tabName` | `Local` | user |
| Audible bell (a short tone when a program rings the bell) | `terminal.audibleBell` | off | user |
| Copy to clipboard on selection | `terminal.copyOnSelection` | off | user |
| Shell integration | `terminal.shellIntegration` | on | user |
| Show application title | `terminal.showApplicationTitle` | on | user |
| Show progress in the status bar | `terminal.showProgressInStatusBar` | on | user |
| Use Option as Meta key (macOS) | `terminal.optionAsMeta` | on | user |
| Cursor shape | `terminal.cursorShape` | Block | user |
| Blinking cursor | `terminal.cursorBlink` | on | user |
| Start directory | `terminal.startDirectory` | project root | user, project |
| Environment variables | `terminal.environment` | empty | user, project |
| Font | `terminal.font.family` | editor font | user |
| Size | `terminal.font.size` | 13 | user |
| Line height | `terminal.font.lineHeight` | 1.2 | user |
| Renderer | `terminal.renderer` | Automatic | user |
| Scrollback buffer | `terminal.scrollback` | 10000 lines | user |

![Terminal settings](docs/screenshots/terminal-settings.png)

## Shell integration

With **Shell integration** on, bash and zsh tell the terminal their working directory (shown
in the tab's tooltip) and where each command starts and ends: finished commands get a mark in
the scrollbar, green when they succeeded and red when they failed. Your own startup files
still run: bash starts with an init file that sources `~/.bashrc` (or the profile files for a
login shell), zsh with a `ZDOTDIR` whose files source yours. The scripts live in
`<cache dir>/forge/shell-integration` of the machine the shell runs on (also on remote hosts).
fish, sh and PowerShell start without it; it applies to new sessions.

## SSH sessions

**Tools | Start SSH Session…** and **SSH Session…** in the new-tab dropdown (the arrow next
to **+**) open a terminal tab on another host over SSH: pick one of your SSH configurations, an
SFTP deployment server of the project or **Edit credentials…**. The tab is named after the
host and runs on a pseudo terminal on the SSH channel, so full-screen programs and resizing
work. See [Remote Host and SSH sessions](docs/guide/user/remote-host-and-ssh.md#ssh-sessions); in Safe Mode a
session to a deployment server asks first.

![SSH session](docs/screenshots/ssh-session-terminal.png)

## Other terminals

The Services tool window opens terminals into Docker containers and Kubernetes pods
(`docker exec`, `kubectl exec`), and in a [remote project](docs/guide/user/remote-development.md) the terminal
runs on the remote host, with the same environment as a local one.

![Remote terminal](docs/screenshots/remote-terminal.png)

In browser mode (`pnpm dev`) the terminal is a small fake shell; `claude` replays a recorded
Claude Code session (`claude --thinking` and `claude --error` show the other progress states),
`Ctrl+C` ends it.

Source: docs/guide/user/database.md

# Database tools and SQL console

The plugin **Database Tools and SQL** (`forge.database`) is Forge's DataGrip part. It supports
**MySQL/MariaDB**, **PostgreSQL** and **SQLite** (through `sqlx`, no JDBC drivers to download).

## Database tool window

The **Database** tool window (right stripe) shows your data sources as a tree:
data source → schema → tables (with comments) → columns, keys and indexes.

![Database tree](docs/screenshots/database-tree.png)

Toolbar: **+** (add data source), **Refresh**, **Data Source Properties** (`Shift+Enter`),
**Jump to Query Console…** (`Ctrl+Shift+F10`), **Collapse All**. Context menu of a node: **New
Query Console**, **Edit Data** (tables), **Go to DDL**, **Copy Name**, **Properties**,
**Refresh**, **Disconnect**, **Delete**.

## Data sources

**New Data Source…** (the **+** button or Find Action) opens **Data Sources and Drivers**:

![Data source dialog](docs/screenshots/database-data-source-dialog.png)

| Field | Notes |
| --- | --- |
| Name, Comment | |
| Driver | MySQL, MariaDB, PostgreSQL, SQLite |
| Host, Port, Database / SQLite file | SQLite files are chosen with a file picker |
| Authentication | User & Password, or none |
| Password | stored in the OS keychain (service `forge-db`), never in project files |
| SSL mode | Disable, Prefer, Require |
| Options | read-only, transaction control (Auto / Manual), connect timeout, startup script |
| Scope | **Project Data Sources** (`<project>/.forge/dataSources.toml`, shareable) or **Global Data Sources** (`dataSources.toml` in Forge's config folder) |

**Test Connection** shows success with the server version, or the error.

### From `.env`

When a project's `.env` has Laravel's `DB_*` variables or Symfony's `DATABASE_URL`, Forge shows
a balloon "Database found in .env" with **Add data source**; the tree also offers **Data
Source from .env**. Turn this off with Settings | Tools | Database | **Suggest data sources
from .env files** (`database.suggestFromEnv`).

## Query console

**New Query Console** on a data source (or **Open Query Console**) opens a console tab:

![Query console](docs/screenshots/database-console.png)

- SQL highlighting for the data source's dialect and completion of keywords, tables and
  columns.
- **Execute** (`Ctrl+Enter`, macOS `Cmd+Enter`) runs the statement at the caret, or the
  selection. Several statements separated by `;` run one after another.
- SQL in PHP and JavaScript strings runs the same way: `Ctrl+Enter` in an injected SQL string
  opens a console with it (see [Language injections](docs/guide/user/language-injections.md#run-injected-sql)).
- Results appear below in tabs (**Output** plus one tab per result set), paged by
  **Result set page size** (`database.pageSize`, 500).
- **Cancel Running Statements** stops a long query.
- **Tx: Auto / Manual** switches the transaction mode; in manual mode use **Commit** and
  **Rollback**.
- The schema selector at the top right sets the current schema.

SQL [scratch files](docs/guide/user/scratches-and-http.md) attached to a data source open as consoles too.

## Data grid and table editor

**Edit Data** (or double-click a table) opens the table in an editor tab with paging (**First,
Previous, Next, Last Page**), a **WHERE** filter and an **ORDER BY** field.

![Editing data](docs/screenshots/database-grid-edit.png)

| Action | Windows/Linux | macOS |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Edit a cell | double-click or `Enter` | same |
| Add Row | `Alt+Insert` | `Cmd+N` |
| Delete Rows | `Ctrl+Y` | `Cmd+Backspace` |
| Revert Selected | `Ctrl+Alt+Z` | `Cmd+Alt+Z` |
| Submit | `Ctrl+Enter` | `Cmd+Enter` |
| Reload Page | toolbar | toolbar |

Cell context menu: **Copy**, **Copy with Header**, **Set NULL**. Changes are applied in one
transaction on **Submit**. Tables without a primary key cannot identify changed rows: only new
rows can be submitted there.

NULL is displayed as `<null>` (**Show NULL as**, `database.showNullAs`). Binary values are shown
as hex.

## Export

**Export Data** (the download icon in a result or table) writes the rows as **CSV**, **JSON**
or SQL **INSERT** statements for the dialect.

## Settings | Tools | Database

| Option | Setting | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Result set page size | `database.pageSize` | 500 |
| Show NULL as | `database.showNullAs` | `<null>` |
| Suggest data sources from .env files | `database.suggestFromEnv` | on |

## Remote projects

In a [remote project](docs/guide/user/remote-development.md), project data sources (and the `.env`
suggestions) are read from the host, and Forge connects to them through an SSH tunnel to their
host and port **as the remote host sees them** — `localhost:3306` means the database on the
server. The data source shows which host it goes through. Global data sources connect directly
from your machine.

![Remote data source](docs/screenshots/remote-parity-data-source-dialog.png)

![Remote database](docs/screenshots/remote-parity-database.png)

> **Note:** SQLite files on the remote host cannot be opened.

# Scratches, consoles and HTTP client

**Scratch files** are throw-away files for experiments, like PHPStorm's "Scratches and
Consoles". They are **global**: they do not belong to a project and are kept in Forge's config
folder (`<config dir>/forge/scratches/`), so they are available in every project.

## Creating scratches

| Action | Windows/Linux | macOS |
| --- | --- | --- |
| New Scratch File… | `Ctrl+Alt+Shift+Insert` | `Cmd+Shift+N` |
| New Scratch Buffer | Find Action | Find Action |

**New Scratch File** asks for the language: type to filter (fuzzy), recently used languages
come first. Every file type with an extension is available.

![New Scratch File](docs/screenshots/scratches-new-popup.png)

New scratches are numbered `scratch.php`, `scratch_1.php`, …; HTTP scratches start as
`rest-api.http`. **Scratch buffers** are plain text files `buffer1.txt` … `buffer5.txt`; after
five, the oldest is reused.

## Scratches and Consoles in the Project view

The bottom of the Project tool window has a **Scratches and Consoles** node with **Scratches**
and **Database Consoles**. A scratch's context menu has **Rename…**, **Delete** and, for SQL
scratches, **Attach Data Source…**.

![Scratches in the Project view](docs/screenshots/scratches-project-view.png)

## Running scratches

Scratches with a runner get a ▶ icon in the gutter; `Ctrl+Shift+F10` runs the current one.
The output appears in the Run tool window.

| Language | Runs with |
| --- | --- |
| PHP | `php.interpreter`, with `-d auto_prepend_file=<project>/vendor/autoload.php` when the open project has an autoloader, so your classes are available |
| JavaScript | `node` |
| TypeScript | `node --experimental-strip-types` (Node 22.6+) |
| Python | `python3` (`python` on Windows) |
| Shell (`.sh`, `.bash`) | `sh` |
| Lua | `lua` |

![PHP scratch run](docs/screenshots/scratches-php-run.png)

Other languages show "Scratches of this language have no runner."

## SQL scratches

A `.sql` scratch can be attached to a data source (**Attach Data Source…**); it then opens as a
query console of that data source with execution, results and transactions. See
[Database tools](docs/guide/user/database.md).

![SQL scratch](docs/screenshots/scratches-sql-console.png)

## HTTP client (`.http` files)

`.http` files hold one or more requests in PHPStorm's HTTP Client format. They work as
scratches (New Scratch File → HTTP Request) and as files in your project. Each request gets a ▶
icon in the gutter; click it and choose **Run** to send the request (`Ctrl+Shift+F10` sends
the request at the caret). The response (status, headers, body) appears
in the Run tool window, followed by the report of its response handler. Project `.http` files
run as an `http-request` run configuration.

The ▶ menu also offers **Debug '…' with Xdebug**: it starts
listening for Xdebug and sends the request with the cookie `XDEBUG_SESSION=FORGE`, so the PHP
application stops at your breakpoints (see
[Debugging](docs/guide/user/debugging.md#debugging-web-pages-and-http-requests)).

![HTTP request](docs/screenshots/scratches-http-request.png)

### Syntax

```http
@host = localhost:8000

### List users
GET http://{{host}}/api/users?page=1
Accept: application/json

###
# @name createUser
POST http://{{host}}/api/users
Content-Type: application/json
Authorization: Bearer {{token}}
X-Request-Id: {{$uuid}}

{ "name": "Ada", "age": {{$random.integer(18, 99)}} }

> {%
  client.global.set("userId", response.body.id);
  client.test("User was created", function () {
    client.assert(response.status === 201, "Expected 201 but got " + response.status);
  });
%}

### Body from a file
POST http://{{host}}/api/import
Content-Type: application/json

< ./import.json

### Long query strings can continue on indented lines
GET https://{{host}}/search
    ?q=forge
    &limit=10
```

- `###` separates requests; text after it names the request. `# @name x` also names one.
- A request is a request line `METHOD URL [HTTP/version]` (the method defaults to `GET`;
  `http://` is added when the URL has no scheme), optional indented `?`/`&` lines continuing the
  query string, headers, a blank line and the body.
- `@name = value` defines a file variable; `{{name}}` uses it in the URL, headers and body.
  Variables may refer to other variables. Unknown variables are left as they are.
- **Body files**: a body line `< ./file.json` inserts the file as it is, `<@ ./file.json` also
  substitutes variables in it. Paths are relative to the `.http` file.
- Comments start with `#` or `//`.

![Body from a file](docs/screenshots/editor-polish-http-body-file.png)

### Dynamic variables

| Variable | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `{{$uuid}}`, `{{$random.uuid}}` | a random UUID |
| `{{$timestamp}}` | Unix time in seconds |
| `{{$isoTimestamp}}` | the current time in ISO 8601 |
| `{{$randomInt}}` | a random integer 0–1000 |
| `{{$random.integer(from, to)}}` | a random integer in the range |

### Environments

Put environment files in the project root, as in PHPStorm:

```json
// http-client.env.json (commit it)
{
  "dev":  { "host": "localhost:8000" },
  "prod": { "host": "shop.example.com" }
}
```

```json
// http-client.private.env.json (keep it out of Git)
{
  "dev": { "token": "s3cret" }
}
```

Every `.http` editor has a toolbar with an **environment selector** listing the environments of
these files. The choice is stored per project in `httpClient.environment` (Settings | Tools |
**HTTP Client**): empty means `dev`, else the first environment; `$none` runs without an
environment. Private values win over public ones.

![Environment selector](docs/screenshots/editor-polish-http-environments.png)

Variable precedence, lowest first: environment < `client.global` (set by handlers) < in-file
`@name = value`.

### Response handlers

A handler after a request, inline `> {% … %}` or in a file `> ./handler.js`, runs when the
response arrives. Forge implements a safe subset of PHPStorm's HTTP Client API without a
JavaScript engine:

- `client.global.set(name, value)`, `get`, `clear`, `clearAll`, `isEmpty` — globals live for
  the IDE session and can be used as `{{name}}` in later requests;
- `client.test(name, function () { … })`, `client.assert(condition, message?)`,
  `client.log(…)`;
- `response.status`, `response.body` (parsed JSON, else text) with `.a.b`, `["a"]`, `[0]`,
  `response.headers.valueOf(name)` / `valuesOf(name)`, `response.contentType.mimeType` /
  `charset`;
- `JSON.stringify` / `JSON.parse`, string and array helpers (`length`, `includes`,
  `startsWith`, `endsWith`, `indexOf`, `toLowerCase`, `toUpperCase`, `trim`);
- `var`/`let`/`const`, `if`/`else`, `return`, functions and arrow functions, literals,
  arithmetic, comparisons, `&&`, `||`, `??` and `?:`.

Loops and anything else stop the script with an error that names the unsupported construct.
Test results and log lines are printed after the response.

![Handler report](docs/screenshots/editor-polish-http-handler.png)

> **Note:** response references (`<> file`) are skipped.

### Remote projects

In a [remote project](docs/guide/user/remote-development.md) environment files and `< file` bodies are read on
the host, and requests are sent **from the host**: Forge forwards a local port through the
project's SSH connection (`direct-tcpip`) to the URL's host and port as the remote host sees
them, so `http://localhost:8000` reaches the server running there. The URL's host stays the
`Host` header and the TLS server name; redirects are not followed. The console says
"Sent from user@host through an SSH tunnel".

Settings | Tools | HTTP Client | **Send requests from** (`httpClient.sendFrom`, per project):
**Remote host** (default) or **This machine**.

![HTTP request sent from the remote host](docs/screenshots/remote-finish-http.png)

Source: docs/guide/user/services.md

# Services

The plugin **Docker and Kubernetes** (`forge.services`) fills the **Services** tool window
(`Alt+8`, macOS `Cmd+8`). It talks to the Docker Engine API directly (Unix socket, Windows
named pipe or TCP with TLS) and to the Kubernetes API with your kubeconfig. The docker CLI is
only used for `docker compose`, image builds and interactive terminals; `kubectl` only for pod
terminals.

![Services](docs/screenshots/services-docker-dashboard.png)

The tree has three roots:

| Root | Children |
| --- | --- |
| **Docker** | Containers, Images, Networks, Volumes |
| **Docker Compose** | compose projects found in the project root and one folder below, with their services and containers |
| **Kubernetes** | contexts → namespaces → Pods, Deployments, Services; the node says where the contexts come from (`~/.kube/config`, or `from host deploy@shop.example.com` in a remote project) |

The status bar shows the Docker connection ("Docker 27.3.1", "Docker: connecting…",
"Docker: not connected"). Forge follows Docker's event stream, so the tree updates by itself,
and retries the connection every 10 seconds.

## Details pane

Selecting a node shows its details on the right, in tabs:

| Tab | Content |
| --- | --- |
| Dashboard | status, image, ports, mounts, networks, environment, labels; tables for compose and Kubernetes objects |
| Log | the log, following new lines; starts with the last `docker.logs.tail` lines (500) |
| Attached Console | output of compose Up/Down, builds and pulls |
| Inspection | the raw JSON (`docker inspect`) |

![Logs](docs/screenshots/services-docker-logs.png)

## Actions

The toolbar and the context menu offer what applies to the selected node:

| Node | Actions |
| --- | --- |
| Docker (not connected) | Connect, Refresh |
| Running container | Stop, Restart, Delete, Show Log, Exec (open a terminal in the container), Pull Image |
| Stopped container | Start, Delete, Show Log, Pull Image |
| Image | Pull, Delete |
| Images group | Pull Image…, Refresh |
| Volume, network | Delete |
| Compose project | Up (Run all services), Stop, Restart, Down (`docker compose down`), Show Log |
| Compose service | Up, Stop, Restart, Down, Show Log, Exec |
| Pod | Delete, Show Log, Exec (`kubectl exec`), Forward Ports… |
| Deployment | Restart Rollout, Show Log (all pods and containers) |

**Exec** opens a terminal tab in the Terminal tool window running `docker exec -it` (or
`kubectl exec -it`) with bash when the container has it, else sh. Containers started with a
TTY also offer an attached console (`docker attach`).

![Exec terminal](docs/screenshots/services-exec-terminal.png)

![Compose](docs/screenshots/services-compose.png)

![Kubernetes pod log](docs/screenshots/services-kubernetes-pod-log.png)

## Kubernetes contexts and namespaces

Above the tree, the **Context** and **Namespace** selectors pick the context to work with:
it becomes the current context in the tree (`current · <server>`), its namespace is loaded
and expanded, and manifests are applied there. The namespace list shows the context's
namespaces once they are listed. Next to the selectors Forge shows where the contexts come
from. The pick lasts for the session; the defaults are the settings below.

![Context selector](docs/screenshots/services-kube-host-contexts.png)

## Applying manifests

A YAML file with Kubernetes objects (`apiVersion` and `kind`, several documents separated by
`---`) gets a ▶ in the gutter on its first object:

| Menu item | Runs |
| --- | --- |
| Apply to '<context>' | `kubectl --context <context> [-n <namespace>] apply -f <file>` |
| Delete from '<context>' | `kubectl --context <context> [-n <namespace>] delete -f <file>` |

`-n` is the selected namespace and is only passed when no object of the file names its own
namespace. The output appears in the **Log** tab of the Kubernetes node. Applying and
deleting manifests runs the project's files against a cluster, so it is refused in Safe Mode
(see [Project trust and Safe Mode](docs/guide/user/project-trust.md)); so are Exec terminals and the Attached
Console of pods. Reading the cluster (the tree, logs, Inspection, port forwards) works in
Safe Mode.

![Apply a manifest](docs/screenshots/services-kube-apply.png)

## Kubernetes pods and deployments

- **Container picker**: a pod with several containers (including init containers) shows a
  container selector on its details. Log, Exec and the Attached Console use the picked container;
  the default is the one named by the `kubectl.kubernetes.io/default-container` annotation, else
  the first container. The Dashboard lists the containers' declared ports.
- **Deployment logs** follow every container of every pod that matches the deployment's
  selector, each line prefixed like `kubectl logs --prefix` (`[pod/<pod>/<container>]`).

![Container picker](docs/screenshots/services-container-picker.png)

![Deployment logs](docs/screenshots/services-deployment-logs.png)

### Port forwarding

**Forward Ports…** on a pod opens a dialog: enter `local:pod` pairs separated by commas, for
example `8080:80, 9000, :5432` (a single port forwards the same port; `:80` picks a free local
port). The pod's declared container ports are offered.

![Forward Ports dialog](docs/screenshots/services-port-forward-dialog.png)

Forge listens on `127.0.0.1:<local>` and opens one connection to the pod per accepted
connection (the Kubernetes port-forward API over WebSocket, no `kubectl` needed). Active
forwards appear in the tree (`⇄ 8080→80`) and on the pod and Kubernetes details, under **Port
Forwarding**, each with **Stop Port Forwarding**.

![Port forwards](docs/screenshots/services-port-forwards.png)

## Compose files and Dockerfiles in the editor

- `compose.yaml` / `docker-compose.yml` get a ▶ in the gutter on `services:` (**Run all
  services**) and on each service (`docker compose up` for that service).
- A `Dockerfile` gets a ▶ on its first `FROM`: **Run on 'Docker'** builds the image and runs a
  container; output appears in Attached Console.

![Compose gutter](docs/screenshots/services-compose-gutter.png)

Compose files support profiles, env files, `${VAR}` interpolation from the project's `.env`
and override files.

## Pulling images and registries

**Pull Image…** (Find Action **Docker.PullImage**, or the Images group) asks for
`repository[:tag]`, e.g. `redis:7-alpine`, and shows the progress.

![Pull image](docs/screenshots/services-pull-image.png)

Private registries: Settings | Build, Execution, Deployment | Docker | **Docker Registry**.
Add the registry (`docker.io`, `ghcr.io`, …), user name and password or access token. The
password goes to the OS keychain (service `forge-containers`); the setting
`docker.registries` only keeps `server<TAB>user`. Without accounts, public images are pulled
anonymously.

## Settings

### Build, Execution, Deployment | Docker

![Docker settings](docs/screenshots/settings-docker.png)

| Option | Setting | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Connect to Docker daemon with (`auto`, `unix`, `pipe`, `tcp`, `ssh`, `context`) | `docker.connection` | `auto` |
| SSH host: `ssh://user@host[:port]` or a `Host` alias of `~/.ssh/config` | `docker.ssh.url` | empty |
| Docker socket on the host (empty: `/var/run/docker.sock`) | `docker.ssh.socketPath` | empty |
| In remote projects, connect to Docker on the remote host | `docker.remoteProjectHost` | on |
| Docker context (`docker context ls`) | `docker.context` | empty |
| Socket path (Unix socket or named pipe; empty: the first existing default) | `docker.socketPath` | empty |
| Engine API URL (TCP) | `docker.tcp.url` | `tcp://localhost:2375` |
| Use TLS (verify the daemon certificate) | `docker.tcp.tls` | off |
| Certificates folder (`ca.pem`, `cert.pem`, `key.pem`) | `docker.tcp.certPath` | empty |
| Docker executable (compose, builds, exec) | `docker.cliPath` | `docker` |
| Show the last log lines | `docker.logs.tail` | 500 |

With `auto`, Forge uses `DOCKER_HOST` when set (also `ssh://` hosts), else the current Docker
context (`DOCKER_CONTEXT` or `currentContext` in `~/.docker/config.json`), else the platform
default socket (`/var/run/docker.sock`, Docker Desktop's `~/.docker/run/docker.sock`, rootless
`$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/docker.sock` or Podman's socket; `\\.\pipe\docker_engine` on Windows).
**Test Connection** checks the settings.

**Docker over SSH** (`ssh`): Forge connects with its own SSH client (keys from ssh-agent and
`~/.ssh`, `~/.ssh/config` aliases) and talks to the remote Docker socket through the SSH
connection; nothing is installed on the host. The host key must already be in `known_hosts`;
unknown keys are refused with their fingerprint. Compose, builds and terminals use the docker
CLI, which reaches `ssh://` hosts itself.

![Docker over SSH](docs/screenshots/settings-docker-ssh.png)

**Docker contexts** (`context`): the page lists the contexts of the Docker CLI
(`~/.docker/contexts`) with **Use**; Forge then connects to that context's endpoint.

![Docker contexts](docs/screenshots/settings-docker-contexts.png)

### Build, Execution, Deployment | Kubernetes

![Kubernetes settings](docs/screenshots/settings-kubernetes.png)

| Option | Setting | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Kubeconfig file (empty: `$KUBECONFIG` or `~/.kube/config`) | `kubernetes.kubeconfig` | empty |
| Default context (empty: the kubeconfig's current-context) | `kubernetes.defaultContext` | empty |
| Default namespace (empty: the context's namespace, else `default`) | `kubernetes.defaultNamespace` | empty |
| kubectl executable (this machine: exec terminals, applying manifests) | `kubernetes.kubectlPath` | `kubectl` |
| In remote projects, use Kubernetes of the project host | `kubernetes.remoteProjectHost` | on |
| kubectl from the project host: `user@host` and the kubectl path there | `kubernetes.hostKubectlPaths` | empty (kubectl from the host's `PATH`) |

Kubernetes authentication supports CA certificates, bearer tokens, client certificates, basic
auth and exec credential plugins (as used by EKS, GKE and AKS).

**kubectl from the Project Host** lists a kubectl per remote host, e.g.
`deploy@shop.example.com` → `/usr/local/bin/kubectl` or `k3s kubectl`. The host of the open
remote project is filled in when you add an entry. Hosts without an entry run `kubectl` from
their `PATH`.

![Kubernetes settings with kubectl per host](docs/screenshots/settings-kubernetes-hosts.png)

> **Note:** port forwarding is available for Kubernetes pods, not for Docker containers.

## Remote projects

In a [remote project](docs/guide/user/remote-development.md) the project's compose files (with `.env` and
override files) are read on the host, and the compose ▶ actions and **Run on 'Docker'** of a
Dockerfile run `docker compose` / `docker build` **on the host**; the console starts with
"Running on user@host in /path".

With **In remote projects, connect to Docker on the remote host** (`docker.remoteProjectHost`,
on) the Docker node shows the host's daemon (`ssh://user@host/var/run/docker.sock`), reached
through the project's own SSH connection: no second login and nothing to set up. Exec terminals
and Attached Console then run `docker` on the host. Turn it off to use the connection configured
above; compose still runs on the host then (against the host's own daemon), while exec terminals
run on this machine.

### Kubernetes in remote projects

With **In remote projects, use Kubernetes of the project host**
(`kubernetes.remoteProjectHost`, on) Kubernetes runs where the project is, like PHPStorm's
remote development: clusters next to the host (a k3s on `127.0.0.1:6443`, a private network,
credential plugins installed there) work without copying anything to this machine.

| | In a remote project |
| --- | --- |
| Contexts | from the host's kubeconfig (`$KUBECONFIG` or `~/.kube/config` on the host), read with `kubectl config view`; the Kubernetes node says `from host deploy@shop.example.com` |
| Namespaces, pods, deployments, services, Inspection | `kubectl get … -o json` on the host |
| Logs | `kubectl logs -f` on the host |
| Exec, Attached Console | a terminal on the host running its kubectl |
| Delete pod, Restart Rollout | `kubectl delete pod`, `kubectl rollout restart` on the host |
| Forward Ports | `kubectl port-forward` on the host (on its `127.0.0.1`); every connection to `127.0.0.1:<local port>` here is tunnelled to it through the project's SSH connection. The forward shows "Forwarding via deploy@shop.example.com". |
| Apply / Delete manifests | `kubectl apply -f` / `delete -f` on the host, in the project folder |

kubectl must be installed on the host; its path is set per host under **kubectl from the
Project Host**. Turn the option off to use this machine's kubeconfig and API access in remote
projects too. Local projects always use this machine's kubeconfig.

![Kubernetes contexts from the project host](docs/screenshots/services-kube-host-contexts.png)

![Compose on the remote host](docs/screenshots/remote-finish-compose.png)

Source: docs/guide/user/remote-development.md

# Remote development

Forge can open a project that lives on another machine, like JetBrains Gateway. It connects over
SSH, installs a small headless **Forge agent** on the host and runs indexing, the PHP language
server, Git, terminals and run configurations **next to the files**. Only the UI runs on your
machine.

## Requirements

| Side | Needs |
| --- | --- |
| Remote host | **Linux** on x86_64 or aarch64, an SSH server, a POSIX shell, write access to `~/.cache`. PHP, Git, Intelephense etc. installed on the host as you would need them locally. |
| Forge | a build that bundles the agents (`pnpm release`), or agent binaries in `FORGE_REMOTE_AGENT_DIR` / an `agents/` folder next to the `forge` binary. See [Release builds](docs/guide/developer/release-builds.md). |

Nothing needs to be installed on the host in advance: Forge uploads the agent itself.

The same agent also runs **in a dev container** (over `docker exec`) and **in a WSL
distribution** (over `wsl.exe`); see [Dev Containers and WSL](docs/guide/user/dev-containers-and-wsl.md). The
Welcome screen's Remote Development section has a page for each: **SSH**, **Dev Containers** and
**WSL**.

## Connecting

Welcome screen → **Remote Development** → **New Connection** (or **New SSH Connection…** in
Find Action).

![Remote Development on the Welcome screen](docs/screenshots/remote-welcome.png)

**Step 1 – Connect to SSH**

![New SSH Connection](docs/screenshots/remote-ssh-dialog.png)

| Field | Notes |
| --- | --- |
| SSH configuration | a saved configuration, a host from `~/.ssh/config` (with `Include`s), or **New connection** |
| Host, Port, Username | |
| Authentication type | **Password**, **Key pair (OpenSSH or PuTTY)** with an optional passphrase, or **OpenSSH config and authentication agent** (ssh-agent plus the `IdentityFile`s of `~/.ssh/config`) |
| Save password / passphrase | stored in the OS keychain (service `forge-ssh`), never in a file |

**Test Connection** shows the host's system and the latency. **Check Connection and Continue**
moves to step 2.

**Step 2 – Choose Project**: browse the host's folders (home, parent, show hidden files) and
double-click the project folder, or type its path, then **Open Project**.

![Choose the project folder](docs/screenshots/remote-folder-chooser.png)

![Project step](docs/screenshots/remote-project-step.png)

### Jump hosts and proxy commands

Hosts from `~/.ssh/config` keep their `ProxyJump` and `ProxyCommand`:

- **ProxyJump**: Forge connects through each hop in turn, tunnelling the next connection
  through the previous one; every hop's host key is checked like the target's.
- **ProxyCommand**: Forge runs the command (with `%h`, `%p`, `%r` and `%n` expanded) and speaks
  SSH over its input and output.

```text
Host shop
    HostName 10.0.0.12
    User deploy
    ProxyJump bastion.example.com
```

### Host keys

Host keys are checked against `~/.ssh/known_hosts`. An **Unknown Host** shows the key type and
fingerprint ("Are you sure you want to continue connecting?"); **Accept New Key** adds it to
`known_hosts`. A **changed** key is reported prominently ("Host Key Has Changed") and must be
confirmed explicitly before the stored key is replaced.

![Fingerprint](docs/screenshots/remote-fingerprint.png)

## The Forge agent

After connecting, Forge probes the host with one shell command (OS, architecture, home folder,
installed agent), uploads the matching agent to `~/.cache/forge-agent/<version>/` when it is
missing or differs (checked by SHA-256), and starts it in a login shell. The agent then serves
the project over the SSH channel.

Set `FORGE_AGENT_LOG=debug` in the host's environment for verbose agent logs (stderr).

## Working in a remote project

![Remote project](docs/screenshots/remote-workbench.png)

The project's root is shown as `user@host:/path`. Recent Projects keeps remote projects with an
**SSH** badge (**Container** and **WSL** for [dev container and WSL projects](docs/guide/user/dev-containers-and-wsl.md));
clicking one reconnects.

A remote project you have not trusted yet opens in Safe Mode and Forge asks "Trust and Open
Project?" right after connecting; trust is kept per host, user, port and folder, see
[Project trust and Safe Mode](docs/guide/user/project-trust.md#remote-projects).

![Recent remote projects](docs/screenshots/remote-open-recent.png)

| Works on the host | |
| --- | --- |
| Project view, editing, saving, file operations, file watching | yes |
| Go to File, Search Everywhere | yes |
| Git (status, commit, diff, blame, branches, log) | yes; output is parsed locally |
| Find in Files | yes, searched on the host |
| Scopes (Find in Files, Find Usages, Structural Search), the Scopes page's file tree | yes, evaluated and listed on the host |
| Structural Search and Replace | yes: the files are parsed on the host; Replace All writes through the agent |
| Analyze Stack Trace | yes: files are looked up on the host; PHP servers' path mappings and Compose bind mounts are read from the host |
| PHP index, Structure, Generate, Intelephense/Phpactor | yes; Intelephense indexes the remote files itself |
| Catalog language servers (TypeScript, YAML, Python, …) | yes: scan, detection and the servers run on the host |
| Installing language servers (Settings, Intelephense offer) | yes: the agent downloads Node.js and the npm servers into Forge's directory on the host, with progress here; the Intelephense licence is accepted on your machine |
| Laravel, Symfony and Doctrine analysis | yes, in the agent; artisan and `bin/console` run on the host |
| WebForge: npm tool window, React / Vue / Angular navigation and gutter icons | yes: `package.json` files, scripts, package managers and components are read in the agent; scripts run on the host |
| LuaForge index | yes, all Lua files are read on the host in one batch |
| StyLua (Reformat Code) | yes, StyLua runs on the host |
| Code hosts (GitLab, Forgejo, GitHub) | yes: the repository is detected with git on the host; API calls go from your machine with your tokens |
| HTTP client (`.http` files) | environment and body files are read on the host; requests are sent **from the host** through an SSH tunnel, so `localhost` URLs reach its services (Settings \| Tools \| HTTP Client \| **Send requests from**) |
| Services: compose files and Dockerfile ▶ | compose files are read on the host and `docker compose` / `docker build` run there; by default Docker of the host is used through the project's SSH connection |
| Services: Kubernetes | contexts come from the host's kubeconfig and `kubectl` runs on the host (tree, logs, exec, apply/delete manifests); port forwards are tunnelled back through the SSH connection, see [Services](docs/guide/user/services.md#kubernetes-in-remote-projects) |
| Browser Companion | files the browser reports (host paths, container paths like `/app/src/…`) open in the remote project |
| Project settings (`.forge/settings.toml`) and other `.forge/` files | yes, read and written on the host |
| Terminal | yes, a shell on the host |
| Run/Debug configurations (run) | yes, processes run on the host |
| Database tools | project data sources connect through an SSH tunnel, see [Database](docs/guide/user/database.md#remote-projects) |
| Xdebug | through a reverse SSH tunnel, see [Xdebug](docs/guide/user/debugging.md#remote-projects) |
| AI Chat (Claude Code, Gemini CLI) | the CLI runs on the host |

![Remote terminal](docs/screenshots/remote-terminal.png)

Every feature works in remote projects. Things that are about your machine stay local on
purpose: code host API calls (your tokens), the keychain, the Intelephense licence prompt and,
when you choose it, HTTP requests ("Send requests from: This machine") and Docker or Kubernetes
of this machine (see [Services](docs/guide/user/services.md#remote-projects)).

![Kubernetes contexts from the project host](docs/screenshots/services-kube-host-contexts.png)

![npm tool window of a remote project](docs/screenshots/remote-finish-npm.png)

![Compose on the remote host](docs/screenshots/remote-finish-compose.png)

![HTTP request sent from the remote host](docs/screenshots/remote-finish-http.png)

![Language server installed on the host](docs/screenshots/remote-finish-langserver.png)

## Connection status and reconnects

The status bar shows the host and latency (pinged every 5 seconds). Click it for the
connection popup.

![Status popup](docs/screenshots/remote-status-popup.png)

When the connection drops, Forge reconnects automatically with a backoff from 1 to 30 seconds
and re-attaches the project ("Reconnecting…", with the next attempt). Host key and
authentication errors stop the retries. **Reconnect to Remote Host** (Find Action) retries now.

![Reconnecting](docs/screenshots/remote-reconnecting.png)

## Saved configurations

Settings | Tools | **SSH Configurations** lists, adds, edits and removes saved configurations.
They are stored in `ssh.toml` in Forge's config folder; secrets stay in the keychain. **Parse
config file `~/.ssh/config`** (on by default) resolves `Host` aliases, jump hosts and proxy
commands from your OpenSSH config. The same configurations connect SFTP deployment servers and
SSH terminal sessions, see [Remote Host and SSH sessions](docs/guide/user/remote-host-and-ssh.md).

![SSH Configurations](docs/screenshots/remote-ssh-settings.png)

## Troubleshooting

See [Troubleshooting: remote agent upload](docs/guide/troubleshooting.md#remote-agent-upload).
