# forge-find

`crates/forge-find` — Find in Files and TODO scanning: query compilation, file masks, line matching and comment patterns (pure, WebAssembly-friendly).

## Purpose

Find in Files (PHPStorm's Ctrl+Shift+F): the search request, file masks and per-line
matching. The crate is pure so the desktop backend (walking the project with
`forge-core`), the remote agent and the browser-mode WebAssembly build share it.

- The query is a literal or a regular expression (`regex` syntax), optionally
  case-sensitive and limited to whole words.
- The file mask is a comma-separated list of globs (`*.php, *.twig`); `!` excludes
  (`!*Test.php`). A glob without `/` matches the file name, otherwise the whole path.
- Matches are reported per line, like PHPStorm's result list: the line text (trimmed and
  cut around the first match) with every match range in it. Columns and ranges are UTF-16
  offsets so the UI can use them directly.

The module `todo` scans for the TODO tool window: `TODO` / `FIXME` style patterns (regular
expressions, PHPStorm's `\btodo\b.*` and `\bfixme\b.*` by default) inside comments only.
`CommentSyntax::for_path` knows the line and block comments and strings of each file type
(PHP, Blade, Twig, C-like languages, markup, CSS/SCSS, hash-comment languages, SQL, Lua);
plain text and Markdown are scanned as a whole. `TodoRequest` can limit the scan to some
`paths` and pass unsaved editor `buffers` that replace the files on disk.

A request may carry a `scope` (`forge_scopes::ScopeFilter`: a predefined scope or a scope
pattern of the Scopes page with its context); `Finder::wants` applies it with the directory,
the path list and the file mask, so the index, the directory walk, the agent and Replace in
Files all honor it.

## Main public items

```rust
pub struct FindRequest { … }
pub struct LineMatch { … }
pub struct FileMatches { … }
pub struct FindResult { … }
pub struct FileMask { … }
pub fn glob_match(glob: &str, text: &str) -> bool { … }
pub struct Finder { … }
pub fn is_binary(bytes: &[u8]) -> bool { … }
pub struct Collector<'a> { … }
pub fn find_in<'t>(
pub mod todo; // TodoRequest, TodoPattern, TodoItem, TodoFile, TodoResult, TodoScanner,
              // TodoCollector, CommentSyntax, scan_todos
```

## Used by

- IPC: `find_in_files` (`app/src-tauri/src/commands/workspace.rs`, a `Backend` method, agent call `FindInFiles`)
  and `todo_scan` (`app/src-tauri/src/commands/workbench.rs`, `Backend::find_todos`, agent call `FindTodos`)
- UI: `app/ui/src/features/find`, `app/ui/src/features/todo`
- Browser mode: built into `forge-wasm`

## Dependencies

- Workspace crates: `forge-scopes`
- External: `regex`, `serde`

## Tests

2 source files, about 1080 lines; 10 unit tests.

# forge-forges

`crates/forge-forges` — Forge IDE code hosts: GitLab, Forgejo/Gitea and GitHub merge requests, issues and pipelines.

## Purpose

Forge code hosts: GitLab (REST v4), Forgejo/Gitea (`/api/v1`) and GitHub (REST, plus
GraphQL for review threads) behind one `CodeHost` trait.

Repositories are detected from `git remote -v` (`remote`); accounts and their tokens
(OS keychain, service `forge-forges`) are managed by `ForgeService`.

## Modules

| Module | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| `accounts.rs` | Code host accounts. The list lives in `<config dir>/forge/forges.toml`; tokens are kept in the OS keychain (service `forge-forges`, account = account id), never in files. |
| `error.rs` |  |
| `forgejo.rs` | Forgejo and Gitea (`/api/v1`, `Authorization: token ...`). Both share the API; Codeberg runs Forgejo. Pull request review comments are grouped into threads by file and line, since the API has no thread objects. |
| `github.rs` | GitHub REST API (github.com and GitHub Enterprise Server, `Authorization: Bearer`). Review threads are rebuilt from `in_reply_to_id`; their resolved state and resolving use the GraphQL API, which REST does not cover. |
| `gitlab.rs` | GitLab REST API v4 (gitlab.com and self-managed). Authentication with a personal access token (`PRIVATE-TOKEN`). Projects are addressed by their URL-encoded full path, so nested groups work without looking up numeric ids. |
| `host.rs` | The `CodeHost` trait implemented by GitLab, Forgejo/Gitea and GitHub. |
| `http.rs` | A small JSON REST client shared by the host implementations: authentication headers, `Link`-header pagination and translating HTTP failures into friendly `HostError`s. |
| `json.rs` | Lenient accessors for API JSON. Hosts differ between versions (fields appear, vanish or become null), so missing values fall back to defaults instead of failing a whole list. |
| `model.rs` | Host-neutral types for merge requests, issues and pipelines. GitHub and Forgejo call merge requests "pull requests"; the UI picks the wording from `HostKind`. |
| `remote.rs` | Detect the code host and project of a repository from its git remotes (`https://`, `ssh://`, scp-like `git@host:path`, nested GitLab groups, self-hosted servers known through accounts). |
| `service.rs` | Accounts plus host construction: the entry point the IDE uses. |

## Main public items

```rust

```

## Used by

- UI: `app/ui/src/features/forges`
- Browser mode: not built to WebAssembly (runtime code); browser mode uses mocks

# forge-injections

`crates/forge-injections` — Language injections: SQL, HTML, CSS, JSON and RegExp inside PHP and JavaScript/TypeScript strings, `// language=` comments, fragment escaping and the injection intentions (pure, WebAssembly-friendly).

## Purpose

Everything behind PHPStorm's IntelliLang that is not per-keystroke highlighting: which string
literals carry another language, the text ranges that belong to it, the value of a literal for
Edit Fragment and Run SQL, escaping typed text back into a literal, and the Alt+Enter
intentions. The editor only colors the ranges with the injected language's CodeMirror parser
(`app/ui/src/features/injections`).

- `lexer`: string literals and comments of PHP (only inside `<?php … ?>`; single and double
  quotes, heredoc and nowdoc with their label, `$var` / `{$expr}` interpolations as gaps) and
  of JavaScript/TypeScript (quotes, template literals with nested `${…}` code, regular
  expression literals skipped). `Host::of_path` picks the lexer from the file name (Blade is
  not a host).
- `rules`: the built-in rules (`RULES`, ids such as `php-sql-calls` or `js-css`) and
  `detect`: literals joined with `.` / `+` are grouped, then the first of a `language=` comment
  (`// language=SQL`, `/* language=JSON */`, `# language=HTML`, `/** @lang SQL */`, first
  literal after it in the same statement), a heredoc label (`<<<SQL`), a call, tagged template
  or assignment rule (`PDO::query()`, `DB::select()`, `preg_match()`, `` sql`…` ``,
  `innerHTML =`), and the text rules (strings starting with a SQL statement or an HTML tag)
  applies. `createQuery()` and `<<<DQL` are left to `phpforge-dql`. PHP patterns are injected
  without their delimiters and flags.
- `escape`: `unescape` (value of a literal plus a value-to-source offset map) and `escape`
  (text typed into a fragment, written for the literal's kind: `\'` in single-quoted PHP,
  `\$` in double-quoted PHP and heredocs, `\n` in JavaScript quotes, `` \` `` and `\$` in
  templates).
- `languages`: the injectable languages (`sql`, `html`, `css`, `json`, `regexp`, `javascript`,
  `xml`) and their aliases (`MySQL`, `PostgreSQL`, `JS`, `Regex`, …).
- `lib`: the API with UTF-16 offsets (CodeMirror's): `find`, `injection_at`, `fragment`,
  `inject` (the `language=` comment to insert, inline `/* … */` when other code precedes the
  string on its line, or the replaced comment), `context_actions` ("Inject language or
  reference", "Edit SQL Fragment", "Un-inject Language" as `forge_codeintel::ContextAction`s),
  `rule_infos`, `languages`. Disabled rules and un-injected places (`path#key`, `key` a hash
  of the literals' source) come with each request.

## Main public items

```rust
pub fn find(req: &FindRequest) -> Vec<Injection> { … }
pub fn injection_at(req: &OffsetRequest) -> Option<Injection> { … }
pub fn fragment(req: &OffsetRequest) -> Option<Fragment> { … }
pub fn inject(req: &InjectRequest) -> Option<Edit> { … }
pub fn context_actions(req: &OffsetRequest) -> Vec<ContextAction> { … }
pub fn escape(kind: LiteralKind, text: &str) -> String { … }
pub fn unescape(kind: LiteralKind, src: &str, from: usize, to: usize) -> (String, Vec<usize>) { … }
pub fn rule_infos() -> Vec<RuleInfo> { … }
pub fn languages() -> Vec<Language> { … }
```

## Used by

- IPC: `injections_find`, `injections_at`, `injections_fragment`, `injections_escape`,
  `injections_inject`, `injections_rules`, `injections_languages`
  (`app/src-tauri/src/commands/injections.rs`); `code_context_actions` adds
  `context_actions` with the `editor.injections.*` settings.
- UI: `app/ui/src/features/injections` (highlighting, Edit Fragment panel, language chooser,
  Run SQL, Settings | Editor | Language Injections). The editor calls `injections_find`,
  `injections_fragment` and `injections_escape` in-process through `forge-wasm` in both modes,
  because highlighting and the fragment editor follow every keystroke.
- Browser mode: built into `forge-wasm` (`injections.rs`), also for `code_context_actions`.

# forge-jsonschema

`crates/forge-jsonschema` — JSON Schema for JSON, JSON5/JSONC and YAML files: position-keeping
parsers, a validator with PHPStorm's messages, completion, hover, Go to Declaration, schema
mappings, bundled schemas and remote schema downloads.

## Purpose

The logic behind [JSON Schema](docs/guide/user/json-schema.md) support. The crate is pure (no file
system or network) and also runs in browser mode through `forge-wasm`; the `remote` cargo
feature adds `remote::RemoteCache`, the download cache the desktop app uses. All public answers
use UTF-16 offsets (CodeMirror positions); internally everything is byte offsets.

## Modules

| Module | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| `tree.rs` | The document tree both parsers produce: `Node { value, start, end, custom_tag }` with `Value::{Null, Bool, Number, String, Array, Object(Vec<Property>), Error}`; a `Property` keeps its key range, the colon and an optional value (a key being typed has none). |
| `json.rs` | Tolerant JSON parser: comments, JSON5 (unquoted keys, single quotes, trailing commas, hex, `Infinity`), and unfinished input (`{"a": 1, "na` is a property `na` without colon). |
| `yaml.rs` | Tolerant YAML parser: block mappings and sequences (`- key: v` compact items), flow collections, plain/quoted/block scalars, comments, documents, anchors, aliases, `<<` merge keys (reported at the `<<` key), tags (`!!str`; other tags mark the node as not judged). YAML 1.2 core schema scalars. |
| `uri.rs` | `$id`/`$ref` resolution (RFC 3986 section 5), fragments, JSON pointer decoding; project files are `project:/<path>`. |
| `schema.rs` | `SchemaDoc` (a parsed schema file with its `$id`s, anchors and external refs), `Registry` (loaded documents, aliases, failed URIs, `missing()`), `Sch` (a subschema with its base URI), `Draft`. |
| `bundled.rs` | The bundled schemas (`schemas/*.json`, compressed by `build.rs`, parsed once) and the URLs they are published under. |
| `validate.rs` | The validator: every keyword of draft 4–2020-12 (see the user page), best-branch reporting for `anyOf`/`oneOf`, evaluated properties/items for `unevaluated*`, ECMAScript patterns through `regex-lite`. |
| `format.rs` | `format` checks: `date-time`, `date`, `time`, `email`, `ipv4`, `ipv6`, `uuid`, `uri`. |
| `navigate.rs` | Schemas at a document path: `$ref`, `allOf`, the `anyOf`/`oneOf` branches compatible with the written value, `if`/`then`/`else`, `dependentSchemas`; `properties`/`patternProperties`/`additionalProperties`/`items` steps with the declaration's position. |
| `complete.rs` | Completion contexts (JSON from the tree, YAML from indentation) and items: property names (required first) with value templates and commas, values (`enum`, `const`, booleans, `null`, `default`, `examples`, `{}`/`[]`). |
| `mapping.rs` | Which schema a file uses: user mappings, `$schema` / the YAML modeline, built-in mappings, the SchemaStore catalog; glob matching. |
| `remote.rs` | (`remote` feature) `RemoteCache`: downloads into `<cache dir>/forge/json-schemas/<sha256>.json`, fresh for a day, stale copies when offline. |
| `lib.rs` | `validate`, `complete`, `hover`, `goto` on a registry and a root URI, `DocKind`, `load_bundled`. |

## Main public items

```rust
pub fn validate(reg: &Registry, root_uri: &str, kind: DocKind, text: &str) -> Vec<ProblemOut>;
pub fn complete(reg: &Registry, root_uri: &str, kind: DocKind, text: &str, offset: usize) -> Option<CompletionOut>;
pub fn hover(reg: &Registry, root_uri: &str, kind: DocKind, text: &str, offset: usize) -> Option<HoverOut>;
pub fn goto(reg: &Registry, root_uri: &str, kind: DocKind, text: &str, offset: usize) -> Vec<Target>;
pub fn load_bundled(reg: &mut Registry, uri: &str) -> bool;
pub mod mapping { pub fn select(path, text, kind, user: &[UserMapping], catalog: Option<&Catalog>) -> Option<Selection>; }
impl Registry { pub fn insert(&mut self, doc: Arc<SchemaDoc>); pub fn missing(&self) -> Vec<String>; pub fn mark_failed(&mut self, uri: &str, error: String); }
impl SchemaDoc { pub fn parse(uri: &str, location: &str, text: String) -> Result<SchemaDoc, String>; }
```

Loading is the caller's job: insert the root schema, then load what `Registry::missing()`
lists (`$ref`s to other files) until it is empty; unloadable documents are marked failed and
their refs accept anything.

## Used by

# forge-keymap

`crates/forge-keymap` — PHPStorm-compatible keymap: shortcut model, default keymaps, overrides, conflicts and the key resolver.

## Purpose

Forge's PHPStorm-compatible keymap engine.

- `shortcut`: parsing ("Ctrl+K Ctrl+C", "Shift Shift", "Cmd+,"), canonical ids, display
  strings ("Ctrl+Shift+A" / "⇧⌘A") and key names of DOM keyboard events.
- `catalog`: PHPStorm's default keymaps (Windows/Linux and macOS), the derived bundled
  keymaps (VS Code, Eclipse, Sublime Text, Emacs, `data/keymaps.json`) and action aliases.
- `engine`: bindings, conflict detection and the `Resolver` state machine that turns
  key events into actions (chords, double taps, focus contexts).
- `keymap`: the `KeymapService` combining the catalog, plugin actions, registered
  commands, user overrides and user keymaps (Duplicate / Derive / Rename / Delete) from the
  settings.
- `shortcut` also models mouse shortcuts ("Ctrl+Button1 Click", "Button2 Double Click",
  "Alt+Wheel Up"), which the resolver handles as single strokes.
- `menu`: the main menu (PHPStorm's structure, plugin contributions, resolution).

The crate is pure (no file system or async runtime): the desktop app wraps it in IPC
commands, and browser mode runs the same code as WebAssembly (`crates/forge-wasm`).

## Modules

| Module | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| `catalog.rs` | PHPStorm's default keymaps as data: "Windows/Linux" (`$default`) and "macOS". |
| `engine.rs` | Bindings, conflict detection and the resolver state machine that turns key events into action ids. |
| `keymap.rs` | The keymap as the IDE sees it: the PHPStorm catalog, actions contributed by plugins and commands, the user's overrides from the settings, and the resolver built from all of it. |
| `menu.rs` | The main menu (PHPStorm's New UI hamburger menu and the classic menu bar) as data. |
| `shortcut.rs` | Keyboard shortcut model: parsing of PHPStorm-style strings, formatting for display (Windows/Linux text or macOS symbols) and conversion from DOM keyboard events. |

## Main public items

# forge-langservers

`crates/forge-langservers` — Forge IDE: catalog, detection, configuration and installation of language servers.

## Purpose

Forge's catalog of language servers for many languages, and everything around it:

- `catalog`: the data-driven catalog (`catalog.toml`) of languages and servers with
  commands, initialization options, settings, install hints and licences,
- `detect`: finding installed servers (PATH, npm/nvm/volta, pip/pipx, cargo, go,
  dotnet, gem, Mason, Windows `.cmd` shims),
- `scan`: which languages a project uses,
- `config`: building a `forge_lsp::LspServerConfig` for a project,
- `plan`: which servers start, and the rows of the settings page,
- `install`: running an install command with streamed output,
- `managed`: installs of npm servers without prerequisites (Node.js and packages
  downloaded and verified into Forge's data directory) and their update check,
- `licence`: the Intelephense licence key in the OS keychain.

PHP servers (Intelephense, phpactor) stay in the PHP pack; the app lists them next to
these rows.

## Modules

| Module | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| `bin/forge-langservers.rs` | Pre-install npm language servers the way Forge does (`pnpm langservers` in `app/ui`): Node.js (if missing) and the packages go into Forge's data directory, so `pnpm tauri dev` and installed builds find them at once. |
| `catalog.rs` | The built-in catalog (`catalog.toml`): languages Forge detects in projects and the language servers that serve them. |
| `config.rs` | Turning a catalog entry into a `LspServerConfig` for one project: file routing, user overrides and the project specific bits some servers need (TypeScript SDK, the Vue TypeScript plugin, ESLint's workspace folder, jdtls' data directory, Lua runtime). |
| `detect.rs` | Finding installed language servers: `PATH` plus the places package managers put executables that are often missing from `PATH` in a desktop session (npm global prefix, nvm/fnm/volta, `~/.local/bin` for pip/pipx, `~/.cargo/bin`, `~/go/bin`, `~/.dotnet/tools`, gem user dirs and Neovim's Mason directory). |
| `install.rs` | Running an install command (`npm install …`, `pipx install …`) with streamed output. Commands come from the catalog only and run without a shell. |
| `licence.rs` | Intelephense licence key: kept in the OS keychain (service `forge-lsp`, account `intelephense`), never in settings files. |
| `managed/archive.rs` | Unpacking downloaded archives (`.tgz` npm tarballs, Node.js `.tar.gz` and `.zip` builds) into a directory. Entries are checked before anything is written: absolute paths, `..` components and symlinks pointing outside the destination are refused. |
| `managed/http.rs` | A small HTTP client for downloads with progress (Node.js builds, npm metadata and tarballs). The system proxy settings (`HTTPS_PROXY`, …) are honoured. |
| `managed/mod.rs` | Zero-prerequisite installs of npm language servers (Intelephense, typescript-language-server, vscode-langservers-extracted, yaml-language-server, …) on the user's machine: |
| `managed/node.rs` | A Node.js runtime for npm language servers: a suitable one on the machine (>= 18), or the official build from nodejs.org (or a mirror) downloaded into `<data dir>/forge/runtimes/node-<version>`, verified against the release's `SHASUMS256.txt`. |
| `managed/npm.rs` | npm packages without npm: registry metadata, tarball download with `dist.integrity` (sha512) verification, unpacking into `<managed dir>/node_modules/<name>` and the `node_modules/.bin` entries detection looks for. |
| `managed/stubs.rs` | PHP stubs for Go to Declaration on PHP's own symbols: a pinned JetBrains phpstorm-stubs release downloaded on first use into `<cache dir>/forge/php-stubs/<version>`, unpacked and checked against a pinned `content_digest` of its files (reproducible from `git archive <commit>`; see the ignored `print_content_digest` test), with its `LICENSE`; `intelephense_stubs` finds Intelephense's own `lib/stub`. |
| `managed/testserver.rs` | A tiny HTTP/1.1 server on localhost for tests: fixed bodies per path, request counts. |
| `managed/updates.rs` | "A newer version is available": at most one registry check a day, remembered in `<managed dir>/.forge-update-check.json`. |
| `plan.rs` | Which servers to start for a project, and the rows of the Language Servers settings page. |
| `prefs.rs` | User preferences for language servers, read from Forge settings. |
| `scan.rs` | Quick scan of a project: which catalog languages occur (by file name, honouring `.gitignore`, capped), which root files exist and which npm packages it depends on. |

## Main public items

# forge-livetemplates

`crates/forge-livetemplates` — Live templates: template sets, contexts, variables and expansion, Surround With and Unwrap/Remove (pure, WebAssembly-friendly).

## Purpose

Everything behind PHPStorm's live templates, Surround With (`Ctrl+Alt+T`) and Unwrap/Remove
(`Ctrl+Shift+Delete`). The UI only shows popups and turns an expansion into CodeMirror
snippet fields.

- `sets`: the built-in groups (`data/*.toml`: PHP, JavaScript, Lua, Twig, Laravel, Blade,
  Symfony) and `resolve`, which applies the user's settings (`editor.liveTemplates.custom`:
  new and changed templates, removed built-ins; `editor.liveTemplates.disabled`) and marks
  framework groups active only for the project's frameworks.
- `context`: the "Applicable in" tree (`PHP_STATEMENT`, `PHP_CLASS_MEMBER`, `JS_EXPRESSION`,
  `HTML`, `BLADE`, …) and `analyze`, which finds the contexts at a position from small lexers
  (PHP with inline HTML, heredocs and attributes; JavaScript with template literals and
  regular expressions; Lua with long strings) plus the class, function, namespace and the
  variables used before the caret.
- `template` and `expr`: `$NAME$` / `$END$` / `$SELECTION$` / `$$` parsing and the variable
  expressions (`className()`, `camelCase(NAME)`, `date("yyyy-MM-dd")`,
  `suggestVariableName(ARRAY)`, …). The clock, clipboard and user name come from the caller.
- `expand`: expansion by abbreviation (`expand`), the Insert Live Template list
  (`applicable`), Surround With (`surround_items`, `surround_apply`). Results are UTF-16
  offsets: the text to insert, one field per variable occurrence (same `index` = edited
  together) and the final caret. Template indentation is converted to the file's indent unit
  and a surrounded selection is re-indented.
- `surround`: the code surrounders per language (PHP, JavaScript, Lua, HTML, Blade, Twig).
- `unwrap`: the statements around the caret (`if`/`elseif`/`else`, loops, `do … while`,
  `try`/`catch`/`finally`, braces; Lua keyword blocks) and the edits that unwrap or remove
  them.

## Main public items

```rust
pub fn catalog(settings: &TemplateSettings) -> Catalog { … }
pub fn resolve(settings: &TemplateSettings) -> Vec<Group> { … }
pub fn analyze(text: &str, at: usize, language_id: Option<&str>, path: &str) -> CaretInfo { … }
pub fn expand(req: &ExpandRequest) -> Option<Expansion> { … }
pub fn applicable(req: &ApplicableRequest) -> ApplicableResult { … }
pub fn surround_items(req: &SurroundRequest) -> Vec<SurroundItem> { … }
pub fn surround_apply(req: &SurroundRequest) -> Option<Expansion> { … }
pub fn unwrap_options(req: &UnwrapRequest) -> Vec<UnwrapOption> { … }
pub fn variable_names(text: &str) -> Vec<String> { … }
```

## Used by

- IPC: `live_templates_catalog`, `live_templates_applicable`, `live_templates_expand`,
  `live_templates_surround_items`, `live_templates_surround`, `live_templates_unwrap`,
  `live_templates_variables`, `live_templates_user` (`app/src-tauri/src/commands/live_templates.rs`)
- UI: `app/ui/src/features/liveTemplates` (expand key, completion, popups, settings page).
  The expand key calls `live_templates_expand` in-process through `forge-wasm` in both modes,
  because the key handler must decide at once whether it expands.
- Browser mode: built into `forge-wasm` (`livetemplates.rs`)

# forge-localhistory

`crates/forge-localhistory` — Local History: file contents recorded on save, refactorings, VCS operations and external changes, with labels, revert and selection history.

## Purpose

The model and store behind PHPStorm's Local History ([user guide](docs/guide/user/local-history.md)).

- **Event model** (`model`): a `ChangeSet` (id, time, `ChangeKind`, name) holds `Entry`s, one
  per path, with the path's `FileState` before and after (`Unknown`, `Absent`, `Dir` or
  `File(hash)`; renames and moves carry `from`). Labels are change sets without entries;
  `Baseline` sets keep the content a file had when Forge first read it and are never listed.
  `Limits` decide what is recorded (excluded folders, size limit, no binary files).
- **Storage** (`storage`): `Storage` is implemented in memory (`MemStorage`, used by
  WebAssembly and tests) and on disk (`DiskStorage`, feature `disk`): an append-only
  `changes.jsonl` (a set written again replaces the earlier line; compacted on load) and
  `content/<2 hex>/<hash>`, zlib-compressed and deduplicated by the first 128 bits of the
  SHA-256 of the content.
- **`LocalHistory`**: `record` (unknown "before" states come from the last recorded state;
  changes of one operation share a `group` and are merged into one set), `baseline`
  (detects external changes), `put_label`, and the queries: `history` (file revisions
  following renames, or folder revisions, with labels and a name/content filter), `state_at` /
  `content` (a revision is the state *before* its change set), `folder_changes`,
  `revert_file` / `revert_folder` / `revert_change` (plans of writes, deletes and folders to
  create, in a safe order), `selection_history` (lines followed back through the revisions with
  a line diff), `recent_changes` (saves in a row grouped), `change_files`, `patch` (git-style
  unified diff) and `purge` (keep the last N working days, then drop the oldest sets until the
  contents fit the size limit, delete unreferenced contents).

The crate does no file system work on the project: callers hand it contents and apply the
revert plans through the project backend.

## Main public items

```rust
pub enum FileState { Unknown, Absent, Dir, File(String) }
pub enum ChangeKind { Save, Edit, Refactoring, External, Vcs, Create, Delete, Rename, Move, Copy, Revert, Label, Baseline }
pub struct ChangeSet { … }
pub struct NewChange { … }
pub struct Limits { … }
pub trait Storage { … }
pub struct MemStorage { … }
pub struct DiskStorage { … }
pub struct LocalHistory<S: Storage> { … }
pub struct RevertPlan { … }
pub fn content_hash(bytes: &[u8]) -> String { … }
```

## Used by

- IPC: `local_history_list`, `local_history_content`, `local_history_folder_changes`,
  `local_history_selection`, `local_history_recent`, `local_history_change_files`,
  `local_history_put_label`, `local_history_patch`, `local_history_revert`,
  `local_history_record`, `local_history_begin` / `local_history_end`,
  `local_history_snapshot` (`app/src-tauri/src/commands/local_history.rs`). A recorder thread
  per project receives messages from the file commands (`fs_write_text`, `fs_write_file`,
  `fs_create_*`, `fs_rename`, `fs_delete`, `fs_copy`, `fs_read_text`), `code_apply_edit`,
  Replace in Files, file templates and the file watcher; stored in
  `<data dir>/forge/projects/<name>-<hash>/local-history/`.
- UI: `app/ui/src/features/localHistory` (history tabs, Recent Changes popup);
  `withLocalHistory` (`app/ui/src/ipc/localHistory.ts`) brackets refactorings and VCS
  operations.
- Browser mode: built into `forge-wasm` (`local_history_call`, in-memory store).

## Dependencies

- Workspace crates: none
- External: `serde`, `serde_json`, `sha2`, `similar`, `flate2` (feature `disk`)

## Tests

5 source files; 14 unit tests (revisions before saves, exclusions, grouped operations, renames
and folder reverts with labels, selection history, baselines and external changes, Recent
Changes grouping, retention by working days and size, the disk log and compressed contents).

```sh

```

# forge-lsp

`crates/forge-lsp` — Forge IDE: generic Language Server Protocol client and server manager.

## Purpose

Forge's generic Language Server Protocol client.

- `framing`: `Content-Length` JSON-RPC framing over stdio.
- `LspClient`: one server process; request/response correlation, notifications,
  answers to server→client requests, document sync and typed feature requests.
- `LspManager`: routes files to servers by extension and starts them lazily; several
  servers may serve one file and their results are merged.
- `model`: editor-friendly result types consumed by the UI.
- `launch`: how server processes start (`LocalLauncher` here, or on a remote host).

Nothing here is language specific; language packs contribute `LspServerConfig`s.
`LspClient::update_settings` merges later changes (the code style options before Reformat
Code, `LspManager::format`'s `settings`) into a server's settings, pushes them with
`workspace/didChangeConfiguration` and answers later `workspace/configuration` requests with
them.

## Modules

| Module | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| `client.rs` | An LSP client talking to one language server process over stdio. |
| `config.rs` | Language server configuration as contributed by language packs. |
| `framing.rs` | JSON-RPC message framing used by LSP over stdio: a `Content-Length` header block, an empty line, then exactly that many bytes of UTF-8 JSON. |
| `hierarchy.rs` | Type and Call Hierarchy from the servers as `forge_codeintel::hierarchy`'s model: `LspManager::type_graph` (prepare, then supertypes and subtypes breadth-first, at most 300 types), `call_root` and `call_nodes` (incoming / outgoing calls of an item); items keep the server id and the server's own item as their `handle`. The manager's `prepare_type_hierarchy`, `type_hierarchy`, `prepare_call_hierarchy`, `incoming_calls` and `outgoing_calls` ask only servers announcing `typeHierarchyProvider` / `callHierarchyProvider` (`Feature::TypeHierarchy`, `Feature::CallHierarchy`). |
| `launch.rs` | Starting language server processes. `LocalLauncher` spawns them on this machine; other launchers start them elsewhere (on a remote development host) and hand back their stdio as streams, so `LspClient`(crate::LspClient) works the same either way. |
| `manager.rs` | Routes files to language servers: one server per registered config, started lazily the first time a matching file is used. |
| `model.rs` | Editor-friendly views of LSP results. |

## Main public items

```rust
pub use client::{path_to_uri, uri_to_path, LspClient, LspEvent, ServerState};
pub use config::{find_on_path, LspServerConfig};
pub use launch::{LocalLauncher, ServerIo, ServerLauncher, ServerProcess};
pub use lsp_types;
pub use manager::{LspManager, ServerStatus, COMPLETION_SERVER_KEY};
```

# forge-maintenance

`crates/forge-maintenance` — Repairing and resetting the IDE: Invalidate Caches, Restore Default Settings, Export / Import Settings.

## Purpose

The logic behind PHPStorm's File | Invalidate Caches… and File | Manage IDE Settings
([user guide](docs/guide/user/repair-ide.md), [settings](docs/guide/user/settings-and-themes.md#export-and-import-settings)).

- **Invalidate Caches** (`caches`): `invalidate_model` is the dialog (texts and the four
  `CacheOption`s); `cleanup_plan(dirs, options)` lists the folders that exist and would be
  deleted (always the PHP index, search index, command line tools cache, JSON schemas,
  Packagist and shell integration; per option the Local History of all projects, the PHP
  stubs, the webview cache and language server data); `run_cleanup` deletes them and reports
  failures.
- **Work for the next start** (`pending`): `schedule` merges work into
  `<data dir>/forge/pending-maintenance.json`; `run_pending` runs it once at startup (the
  app calls it before the settings load), removing the marker first.
- **Settings groups** (`groups`): PHPStorm's export components as setting key prefixes
  (the longest prefix wins, the rest is "Other settings") or whole configuration files;
  `count_groups` lists the non-empty ones for the dialogs.
- **Settings archive** (`archive`): `export_settings` writes a zip with `forge-settings.json`
  (format, version, groups), the chosen keys as `settings.toml` and the chosen files;
  `read_archive` reads one back (unknown entries ignored, size-limited); `SettingsArchive::plan`
  replaces the chosen groups of the current user settings (keys the archive does not set are
  removed).
- **Restore Default Settings** (`restore`): `backup_settings` copies `<config dir>/forge` to
  `forge-backup-<UTC timestamp>`; `reset_settings` removes `settings.toml`,
  `new-project-settings.toml` and `dialog-windows.json` at the next start.

`ForgeDirs` names the user directories, so tests run entirely in temporary folders.

## Main public items

```rust
pub enum CacheOption { FileSystemAndLocalHistory, SharedIndexes, BrowserEngine, LanguageServerData }
pub fn invalidate_model() -> InvalidateModel { … }
pub fn cleanup_plan(dirs: &ForgeDirs, options: &[CacheOption]) -> Vec<CleanupItem> { … }
pub fn run_cleanup(plan: Vec<CleanupItem>) -> CleanupReport { … }
pub fn schedule(dirs: &ForgeDirs, change: impl FnOnce(&mut PendingWork)) -> Result<(), String> { … }
pub fn run_pending(dirs: &ForgeDirs) -> Option<PendingReport> { … }
pub fn settings_groups() -> &'static [SettingsGroup] { … }
pub fn group_of_key(key: &str) -> &'static str { … }
pub fn export_settings(values, files, groups, version) -> Result<Vec<u8>, String> { … }
pub fn read_archive(bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<SettingsArchive, String> { … }
pub fn backup_settings(dirs: &ForgeDirs, now_secs: u64) -> Result<PathBuf, String> { … }
```

## Used by

- IPC: `maintenance_invalidate_model`, `maintenance_invalidate_caches`, `maintenance_restart`,
  `maintenance_rescan_indexes`, `settings_export_info`, `settings_export`,
  `settings_import_preview`, `settings_import`, `settings_restore_defaults`
  (`app/src-tauri/src/commands/maintenance.rs`).
- UI: `app/ui/src/features/maintenance` (Invalidate Caches dialog, Repair IDE balloons,

# forge-markdown

`crates/forge-markdown` — Forge Markdown: a safe AST (no raw HTML) for chat messages, documentation popups and the Markdown preview, built with pulldown-cmark (pure, also built to WebAssembly).

## Purpose

Markdown as a safe AST for the UI, which renders it with Solid components (never as
HTML). Raw HTML is never passed through: in chat messages it stays literal text, in
documentation `<br>`/`<p>` become line breaks and every other tag is dropped.

- `parse`: Markdown into `Block`s (`Flavor::Chat`, `Flavor::Docs` or `Flavor::Preview`).
- `parse_document`: a Markdown file for the preview: GitHub-flavored blocks (tables, task
  lists, strikethrough, footnotes, autolinks, alerts, heading anchors, images) with the source
  lines of every top-level block (synchronized scrolling), the front matter and the footnotes.
  Raw HTML is sanitized into the AST (`<img>`, `<a href>`, `<br>`, `<b>`, `<i>`, `<s>`); comments
  and every other tag are dropped.
- `hover`: language server hover Markdown (Intelephense & co.) split into the parts of
  a PHPStorm-style documentation popup.

## Modules

| Module | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| `ast.rs` | The Markdown AST sent to the UI (JSON tagged by `t`). |
| `doc_comment.rs` | Documentation comments for the editor's rendered view and Reader mode: `doc_comments(text, language)` finds `/** … */` (PHPDoc, JSDoc / TSDoc) and `---` (LuaDoc / LuaCATS) comments, `parse_doc_comment` turns one into a `HoverDoc`: the description as Markdown (inline `{@link url text}` / `{@see X}` as links and code), the tags as `Params:` / `Returns:` / `Throws:` / `Properties:` / `See also:` … sections, `@deprecated` as the note and `@example` as a code block. |
| `document.rs` | The Markdown preview of a file: GitHub-flavored blocks with the source lines of every top-level block, the front matter and the footnotes; `anchor_line` for links into a file. |
| `hover.rs` | Language server hovers (Markdown as Intelephense, phpactor & co. send it) split into the parts of a PHPStorm-style documentation popup: owner FQCN, signature, description and `Params:` / `Returns:` / `Throws:` sections. |
| `parse.rs` | pulldown-cmark events into the `Block` tree. |

## Main public items

```rust
pub use ast::{Block, Inline, ListItem};
pub use doc_comment::{doc_comments, doc_style, parse_doc_comment, DocComment, DocStyle};
pub use document::{anchor_line, parse_document, Document, Footnote, FrontMatter, FrontMatterEntry, LineRange};
pub use hover::{parse_hover, HoverDoc, HoverSection};
pub use parse::{parse, parse_inline, Flavor};
```

## Used by

- IPC: `markdown_parse`, `markdown_hover`, `markdown_document`, `markdown_anchor_line` (`app/src-tauri/src/commands/markdown.rs`)
- UI: `app/ui/src/features/lsp/MarkdownDoc.tsx`, `app/ui/src/features/ai-chat/Markdown.tsx`, `app/ui/src/features/markdown/MarkdownPreview.tsx`
- Browser mode: built into `forge-wasm`

## Dependencies

- Workspace crates: none
- External: `pulldown-cmark`, `regex-lite`, `serde`, `serde_json`

## Tests

5 source files; 17 unit tests.


# forge-viewers

`crates/forge-viewers` — Forge file viewers: image metadata for the image editor and CSV/TSV tables for Edit as Table (pure, also built to WebAssembly).

## Purpose

browser mode (WebAssembly) share it:

| `table.rs` | CSV/TSV for "Edit as Table". The parser remembers which cells were quoted, so writing an unchanged table gives back the same text, and edits only touch the cells they change. |

Opening files in Forge from the outside world:

| `symbols.rs` | Find the declaration of a symbol the browser only knows by name (an Angular component's constructor name, a React component without debug source) in the open project. |

# forge-output

`crates/forge-output` — Forge process output: ANSI styling, console lines, file links, TeamCity test trees and terminal OSC sequences (pure, also built to WebAssembly).

## Purpose

Process output for the Run tool window and the terminal, computed in Rust so the UI only
renders it.

- `ansi`: ANSI escape sequences (SGR colors and styles) into styled segments.
- `console`: segments into console lines with `\r` progress lines, as deltas the UI
  applies to its line list.
- `filters`: External Tools output filters (`$FILE_PATH$:$LINE$`) as file links.
- `links`: clickable file references (`app/User.php:42`, stack traces) and URLs.
- `teamcity`: TeamCity service messages (`phpunit --teamcity`, Pest, Jest) into a test
  tree that is sent to the UI as node updates.
- `junit`: JUnit XML reports (Codeception, Behat, PHPSpec) as service messages for the
  same test tree.
- `run`: everything above combined for one run.
- `osc`: terminal OSC sequences (progress, notifications, working directory) and OSC 8
  link targets.
- `stacktrace`: Analyze External Stack Trace: frames of PHP, Laravel/Symfony, Xdebug,
  JavaScript/Node and Lua traces linked to project files, with server and container paths
  mapped (`PathMapping`, `compose_mappings`, longest existing tail).

The crate is pure (no I/O) so `forge-wasm` can run it in browser mode.

## Modules

| Module | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| `ansi.rs` | ANSI escape handling: SGR colors and styles become styled segments, other control sequences (cursor movement, OSC titles) are dropped. Colors are CSS values, either a theme variable (`var(--ansi-red)`) or `rgb(…)`. |
| `console.rs` | Console lines built from styled segments, sent to the UI as deltas. |
| `filters.rs` | External Tools output filters: a regular expression with `$FILE_PATH$`, `$LINE$` and `$COLUMN$` (`$FILE_PATH$:$LINE$`); `RunOutputOptions.outputFilters` links their matches before the built-in patterns. |
| `junit.rs` | JUnit XML reports turned into TeamCity service messages: suites, a suite per class for Codeception's flat suites, failures and errors (with expected/actual from PHPUnit diffs), skipped and the `status` of Behat and PHPSpec (`pending`, `undefined`, `broken`), durations, and locations by `JUnitFlavor` (`file`/`line`; Behat features; PHPSpec spec files and example methods derived from the class). |
| `links.rs` | File references in console and terminal output (`app/User.php:42`, `/abs/path/File.php on line 7`, `File.php(12)`, `#0 /path/x.php(31): …`) and web links, so the UI can make them clickable. |
| `osc.rs` | Payloads of the OSC sequences the terminal understands beyond xterm.js: OSC 9;4 progress (normal, error, indeterminate, paused, remove), OSC 9 and OSC 777 notifications, OSC 7 and ConEmu 9;9 working directories, OSC 133 command boundaries, and which OSC 8 hyperlinks may open (web and mail links, `file://` links into the project). The terminal calls it synchronously through `forge-wasm` from xterm.js's OSC handlers. |
| `stacktrace.rs` | Analyze External Stack Trace: `analyze(text, ctx, exists)` turns a pasted trace into console lines whose frames link to project files (message in red, library frames dimmed); `resolve` maps a path with `TraceContext.mappings`, the project root or the longest trailing part that exists; `compose_mappings` reads Docker Compose bind mounts; `normalize` splits one-line logs with escaped line breaks. |
| `run.rs` | The output of one run: console lines for every stream, and for test runners the test tree built from TeamCity service messages on stdout (those lines are not shown in the console). Output while a test runs is attributed to that test. `TestReport` says where results come from: TeamCity messages, a JUnit document on stdout (collected and parsed at the exit) or JUnit files handed in as `RunInput::Report` before the exit. |
| `teamcity.rs` | TeamCity service messages (`phpunit --teamcity`, Pest, Jest reporters) turned into the test tree of the Run tool window. The tree lives here; the UI receives changed nodes. `TestTree::export` / `import` store a finished tree as `StoredNode`s for the Test History. |
| `utf16.rs` | Offsets for the UI: JavaScript strings and CodeMirror count UTF-16 code units, Rust counts bytes. |

## Main public items

```rust
pub use ansi::{AnsiParser, Segment, Style};
pub use console::{ConsoleDelta, ConsoleLine, ConsoleModel, Span};
pub use links::{…};
pub use osc::{link_target, parse_osc, LinkTarget, OscAction, Progress, ProgressState};
pub use junit::{junit_messages, JUnitFlavor};
pub use run::{OutputEvent, RunInput, RunOutput, RunOutputOptions, TestReport};
pub use teamcity::{…};
pub use utf16::{byte_to_utf16, utf16_to_byte};
```

## Used by

- IPC: `output_file_links`, the `console`/`tests` events of `run://<runId>` and
  `stacktrace_analyze` (`app/src-tauri/src/commands/stacktrace.rs`)
- UI: `app/ui/src/features/run`, `app/ui/src/features/terminal`, `app/ui/src/features/stacktrace`
- Browser mode: built into `forge-wasm`; the terminal uses `osc` through `forge-wasm` in the desktop app too

# forge-plugin-api

`crates/forge-plugin-api` — Stable plugin API for Forge language packs and feature plugins.

## Purpose

The contract between Forge and its plugins.

A plugin (a language pack like PHPForge, or a feature like Git) describes itself with a
`PluginManifest` and contributes capabilities through `Contributions`: commands,
keybindings, tool windows, typed settings, language servers, run configuration types and
AI providers/agents/generators. The `PluginRegistry` tracks installed plugins, their
enablement, and answers lookups over the contributions of enabled plugins. Packs depend
only on this crate, never on app internals.

## Modules

| Module | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| `contributions.rs` | Contribution types: everything a plugin can add to the IDE. |
| `registry.rs` | The plugin registry: which plugins are installed, which are enabled, and lookups over the contributions of the enabled ones. |
| `settings_model.rs` | The model behind the Settings dialog (Ctrl+Alt+S): the page tree built from registered pages, search over pages, settings and plugins, and highlighting of search hits. The UI sends what it shows and renders the answer; this module decides what matches. |

## Main public items

```rust

pub use registry::{PluginDescriptor, PluginInfo, PluginRegistry};

pub trait Plugin: Send + Sync { … }
```

# forge-process

`crates/forge-process` — Forge IDE processes: PTY terminal sessions, run configurations and the process runner.

## Purpose

Forge processes: everything the IDE starts on behalf of the user.

- `pty`: interactive terminal sessions on a pseudo terminal (Terminal tool window).
- `runner`: plain processes with piped output for run configurations (Run tool window),
  with exit codes and process-tree kill.
- `config`: Run/Debug configurations, their persistence in
  `<project>/.forge/runConfigurations.toml` and the registry of configuration kinds that
  turns a configuration into a command line.
- `output`: the pure output models of the `forge-output` crate (ANSI, console lines,
  file links, TeamCity test trees), re-exported for the run backend.

## Modules

| Module | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| `args` | Splitting and quoting of argument strings as typed into run configuration fields ("Arguments", "Interpreter options", "Test runner options"); re-exported from `forge-runtools`. |
| `config.rs` | Run/Debug configurations. |
| `pty.rs` | Interactive shell sessions on a pseudo terminal, used by the Terminal tool window. |
| `runner.rs` | Non-interactive processes for run configurations: piped stdout/stderr streamed as text, stdin for input typed into the Run console, the exit code, and kill of the whole process tree (so `composer run` or `npm run` children stop too). |
| `shell.rs` | Picking the user's default shell. |
| `test_history.rs` | The Test History of the Run tool window: `TestRunRecord` (configuration, start time, summary, counts and the stored tree), saved as compact JSON in `<data dir>/forge/test-history/<project key>/<id>.json`, listed newest first and pruned to the last `MAX_RUNS` (10) per project. |
| `termenv.rs` | The environment a terminal session starts with: `TERM`, `COLORTERM`, `TERM_PROGRAM=Forge`, `TERM_PROGRAM_VERSION` and `FORGE_TERMINAL=1`, a UTF-8 `LANG` when the inherited locale is not UTF-8, and removal of variables that describe another terminal or multiplexer (kitty, tmux, iTerm2, WezTerm, Ghostty, …). |
| `utf8.rs` |  |

## Main public items

# forge-project

`crates/forge-project` — Forge IDE projects: project type detection and New Project generators.

## Purpose

Forge projects: detect what a project is made of (languages, frameworks, tools) so the
matching packs activate, and create new projects from generators (File | New Project).

## Modules

| --- | --- |

| `generators.rs` | New Project generators (File \| New Project). |
| `templates.rs` | Built-in offline project templates. Files are embedded with `include_str!` and use `{{placeholder}}` variables in both contents and paths (see `TemplateVars`). |

## Main public items

```rust
pub use create::{create, find_executable, has_tool, plan_for_system, CreateEvent};
pub use detect::{detect, language_name, Framework, ProjectInfo};
pub use generators::{…};
```

## Used by

# forge-remote

`crates/forge-remote` — Forge IDE remote development: SSH connections, host keys, ~/.ssh/config and the Forge agent deployment.

## Purpose

Remote development over SSH, like JetBrains Gateway: Forge connects to a host, installs
its headless agent (`crates/forge-remote-agent`) there and opens the project through a
`forge_backend::RemoteBackend`, so indexing, Intelephense, git, terminals and runs all
happen next to the files.

Pure modules (also built for WebAssembly without the `client` feature):
- `ssh_config`: `~/.ssh/config` host blocks.
- `known_hosts`: host key verification and fingerprints.
- `deploy`: probing a host and planning the agent upload.
- `config`: saved SSH configurations.

With `client` (the default):
- `session`: SSH connections with russh (password, key file, ssh-agent; known_hosts
  check with a fingerprint confirmation).
- `agent`: installing and starting the agent.
- `connection`: a live connection to an agent with reconnects and latency.
- `store`: saved configurations on disk and their secrets in the keychain.
- `shell`: SSH terminal sessions (`SshShell::open(params, cols, rows, sink)`, a
  `forge_backend::Terminal` on a pseudo terminal of an SSH channel).

## Modules

| Module | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| `agent.rs` | Installing and starting the Forge agent over an SSH session. |
| `config.rs` | Saved SSH configurations (Settings \| Tools \| SSH Configurations), stored in `<config dir>/forge/ssh.toml`. Passwords and key passphrases never go there: they live in the OS keychain. `parse_config` ("Parse config file ~/.ssh/config", on by default) decides whether `~/.ssh/config` resolves the host. |
| `connection.rs` | A live connection to the Forge agent on a host: connects (SSH + agent start), measures latency, notices a dead connection and reconnects with backoff. |
| `deploy.rs` | Installing the Forge agent on a remote host: probe the host with one shell command, decide whether the agent must be uploaded, upload it through `cat` (no SFTP needed) and start it. |
| `known_hosts.rs` | OpenSSH `known_hosts`: which host keys are trusted. |
| `session.rs` | SSH sessions with russh: host key verification against `known_hosts` (unknown and changed keys need the user's confirmation of the fingerprint), password, key file and ssh-agent authentication, command execution and streams, jump hosts (`ProxyJump`, one session tunnelled through the previous one) and `ProxyCommand`, port forwarding (`direct-tcpip` channels and remote `tcpip-forward` listeners) and forwarded Unix sockets (the Docker API over SSH). |
| `shell.rs` | SSH terminal sessions (Tools \| Start SSH Session…): `SshSession::open_shell` (`pty-req` for `xterm-256color` + `shell`), output as UTF-8 to a `forge_process::PtySink`, input, window changes, the exit status and closing. |
| `ssh_config.rs` | OpenSSH client configuration (`~/.ssh/config`): host blocks with patterns and the keywords Forge uses to connect. Like `ssh`, the first value obtained for a keyword wins and `IdentityFile` accumulates. |
| `store.rs` | Saved SSH configurations on disk (`<config dir>/forge/ssh.toml`), their passwords and passphrases in the OS keychain (service `forge-ssh`, account = configuration id), and the user's OpenSSH files (`~/.ssh/config`, `~/.ssh/known_hosts`). |

## Main public items

```rust
pub use config::{AuthMethod, SshConfiguration, SshConfigurations};
pub use known_hosts::HostKeyStatus;
```

## Used by

- IPC: `remote_ssh_configs`, `remote_ssh_config_save`, `remote_validate_config`, `remote_ssh_config_delete`, `remote_ssh_hosts`, `remote_test_connection`, `remote_connect`, `remote_browse`, `remote_open_project`, `remote_disconnect`, `remote_status`, `remote_reconnect` (`app/src-tauri/src/commands/remote.rs`)
- IPC: `terminal_open({ options: { ssh: { configId? | serverId?, secret?, confirmed? } } })` (`app/src-tauri/src/commands/terminal.rs`)
- UI: `app/ui/src/features/remote`, `app/ui/src/features/terminal/ssh.tsx`
- Browser mode: built into `forge-wasm`

## Dependencies

- Workspace crates: [`forge-backend`](docs/guide/developer/crates/forge-backend.md), [`forge-core`](docs/guide/developer/crates/forge-core.md), [`forge-process`](docs/guide/developer/crates/forge-process.md)
- External: `base64`, `dirs`, `flate2`, `hmac`, `keyring`, `russh`, `serde`, `serde_json`, `sha1`, `sha2`, `tokio`, `toml`, `tracing`
- Features: `default` = `client`; `client` = `dep:forge-backend`, `dep:forge-core`, `dep:forge-process`, `dep:russh`, `dep:tokio`, `dep:tracing`, `dep:dirs`, `dep:keyring`, `dep:toml`, `dep:flate2`

# forge-runtools

`crates/forge-runtools` — Run Anything, compound and before-launch plans, External Tools and their macros (pure, also built to WebAssembly).

## Purpose

Pure logic behind Run Anything, compound run configurations, "Before launch" tasks and
External Tools. No I/O, so `forge-wasm` builds it for browser mode; the desktop app
(`app/src-tauri/src/commands/runtools.rs`) collects the inputs (npm and Composer scripts,
PHP files, settings) through the project backend and starts the processes with `run_start`.

## Modules

| Module | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| `args.rs` | Splitting and quoting of argument strings (shared with `forge-process`, which re-exports it). |
| `macros.rs` | PHPStorm's macros (`$FilePath$`, `$ProjectFileDir$`, `$LineNumber$`, `$SelectedText$`, `$ClipboardContent$`, `$Prompt$`, `$PhpExecutable$`, …): the list with descriptions and previews for "Insert Macro…", and expansion with an `Expander` that hands out `$Prompt$` answers in order. Unknown `$Names$` stay as they are; macros without a value expand to nothing and are reported. |
| `external.rs` | External Tools: the model, its settings object (`tools.externalTools`, string values), validation (name, program, output filters), the command of a run (arguments split first, then expanded) and grouping for menus; `action_id` is PHPStorm's `Tool_<group>_<name>`. |
| `launch.rs` | Launch plans: `plan(configurations, target)` returns the configurations to start (a compound's members, nested compounds expanded, duplicates once) and each one's ordered before-launch tasks, with "Run Another Configuration" flattened; missing configurations and cycles are errors. npm, Composer, Artisan and shell tasks come with the temporary configuration that runs them. |
| `anything.rs` | Run Anything: `suggest` groups and ranks (with `forge-fuzzy`) the history, run configurations, npm and Composer scripts, PHP files, plugin commands and the typed command; `?` returns help. `resolve` turns a command into a temporary configuration (`php file.php` → PHP Script, `php artisan …` → Artisan, `composer …`, `npm`/`pnpm`/`yarn`/`bun` → npm, else Shell Script); `push_history` keeps the newest 50 entries. |

# forge-save-actions

`crates/forge-save-actions` — Actions on Save: which actions run for a saved file,
reformatting only changed lines and running external tools (ESLint, Prettier, PHP CS Fixer,
Laravel Pint) through the project's backend.

## Purpose

The logic behind Settings | Tools | [Actions on Save](docs/guide/user/actions-on-save.md):

- `plan(path, trigger, settings)` decides which actions run for one save: Reformat code
  (whole file or changed lines, limited to file types), Optimize imports, Rearrange code and
  Run code cleanup (PHP files only) and the external tools. On autosave nothing runs unless
  "Also run on autosave" is on, and the external tools never do.
- `restrict_to_changed_lines(base, original, formatted)` keeps only the hunks of a
  reformatting that touch lines changed since `base` (the committed text; `None` = the whole
  file is new).
- `tools` (feature `backend`, on by default) finds a tool in the project (`vendor/bin`,
  `node_modules/.bin`, `.bat` / `.cmd` too) or at its custom path and runs it on the saved
  file through a `forge_backend::Backend`, so remote projects work. A failing tool's changes
  are rolled back; ESLint's exit code 1 (problems left after `--fix`) counts as success.

The PHP actions themselves are in `phpforge-lang-php` (`imports`, `rearrange`, `cleanup`).
The UI applies the combined result as one edit (one undo step).

## Modules

| Module | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| `lib.rs` | Settings keys, `ActionsOnSave` (settings), `Trigger`, `Tool`, `SavePlan`, `plan`, `file_type_choices`. |
| `changed.rs` | "Changed lines": a line diff (LCS) between the original and the reformatted text, applied hunk by hunk. |
| `tools.rs` | Locating and running ESLint, Prettier, PHP CS Fixer and Laravel Pint; `run_tools`, `detect_tools`. |

## Main public items

```rust
pub fn plan(path: &str, trigger: Trigger, settings: &ActionsOnSave) -> SavePlan;
pub fn restrict_to_changed_lines(base: Option<&str>, original: &str, formatted: &str) -> String;
pub fn file_type_choices() -> Vec<FileTypeChoice>;
pub mod tools; // run_tools, detect_tools, locate (feature "backend")
```

## Used by

- IPC: `save_actions_plan`, `save_actions_changed_lines`, `save_actions_php`,
  `save_actions_run_tools`, `save_actions_info` (`app/src-tauri/src/commands/save_actions.rs`)
- UI: `app/ui/src/features/actionsOnSave/`, `saveFile` in `app/ui/src/state/editor.ts`
- Browser mode: `plan` and `restrict_to_changed_lines` are built into `forge-wasm`
  (without the `backend` feature)

## Dependencies

- Workspace crates: `forge-filetypes`, `forge-text`; with `backend`: `forge-backend`,
  `forge-core`, `forge-process`
- External: `serde`, `serde_json`

## Tests

tools needed).

# forge-scratches

`crates/forge-scratches` — Forge scratch files (PHPStorm's Scratches and Consoles): storage, naming, languages, run commands and the HTTP request client.

## Purpose

Scratch files, PHPStorm's "Scratches and Consoles".

Scratches are global: they live in the user config dir (`<config>/forge/scratches/`), not
in a project, and are listed at the bottom of the Project tool window.

- `languages`: the language list of the "New Scratch File" popup (file types from
  `forge-filetypes`, ranked with `forge-fuzzy`) and the language → extension mapping.
- `naming`: auto-numbered names (`scratch.php`, `scratch_1.php`, `buffer1.txt`) and name
  validation.
- `store`: create, list, read, write, rename and delete scratches on disk, plus the data
  source attached to SQL scratches.
- `run`: what runs a scratch (PHP with the project's autoloader, Node, ...) and the
  gutter run markers.
- `http`: the `.http` request parser and the console rendering of responses (PHPStorm's
  HTTP Client, lite); `handler` runs response handler scripts (`> {% … %}`) as a safe
  subset without a JavaScript engine; `client` sends the requests (feature `client`).

Everything except `store` and `client` is pure, so browser mode runs it as WebAssembly.

## Modules

| Module | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| `client.rs` | Sends the requests of `.http` scratches (feature `client`). |
| `handler.rs` | Response handler scripts of `.http` requests (`> {% … %}`), PHPStorm's HTTP Client API as a small, safe subset: no JavaScript engine, no loops, no access to anything but the response and the global variables. |
| `http.rs` | `.http` request files (PHPStorm's HTTP Client, lite): parsing, `{{variable}}` substitution and the console text of a response. |
| `languages.rs` | Languages of the "New Scratch File" popup (Ctrl+Alt+Shift+Insert): every file type of `forge-filetypes` with an extension, the extension a new scratch gets, and the popup's ordering and speed search. |
| `naming.rs` | Scratch names: PHPStorm numbers new scratches `scratch.php`, `scratch_1.php`, `scratch_2.php`, … and scratch buffers `buffer1.txt` … `buffer5.txt` (the oldest buffer is reused once all five exist). |
| `run.rs` | Running scratches: which program runs a scratch (PHP with the project's Composer autoloader, Node for JavaScript/TypeScript, …), and the gutter ▶ markers of runnable scratches and of the requests in `.http` files. |
| `store.rs` | Scratch files on disk. PHPStorm keeps scratches per user, not per project; Forge stores them in `<config dir>/forge/scratches/` and per-scratch settings (the data source of a SQL scratch) in `<config dir>/forge/scratches.json`. |

## Main public items

```rust
pub use languages::{LanguageItem, LanguageRequest, ScratchLanguage};
pub use run::{Marker, MarkerKind, RunCommand, RunContext, Runner};
pub use store::{ScratchFile, ScratchStore};
pub enum Error { … }
```

- UI: `app/ui/src/features/scratches`

- Features: `default` = `client`; `client` = `dep:reqwest`

# forge-scopes

`crates/forge-scopes` — Scopes (PHPStorm's scope language, predefined and named scopes) and file colors (pure, WebAssembly-friendly).

## Purpose

Scopes and file colors, like PHPStorm's Settings | Appearance & Behavior | Scopes and File
Colors (see the [user guide](docs/guide/user/scopes-and-file-colors.md)).

- `pattern`: the scope language: `file:` / `src:` / `test:` / `lib:` path patterns (`*`, `?`,
  `//` for any folders, a pattern without `/` matches file names), `file[module]:`, `&&`,
  `||`, `!`, parentheses, with parse errors that carry an offset. `Expr::matches` for files,
  `Expr::matches_dir` for folders as a whole.
- `Predefined` scopes (All Places, Project Files, Project Production Files, Project Test
  Files, Open Files, Changed Files, Current File, Non-Project Files), `NamedScope` and
  `ScopeSet` (shared and local scopes of the settings: entries for choosers, name lookup,
  problems).
- `ScopeFilter` (a `ScopeSpec` plus its `ScopeContext`: test roots, open, changed and current
  files) is what searches carry to the backend; `Scope` is it compiled.
- `context`: test detection (`composer_test_roots` from `autoload-dev`, conventional folders
  and file names) and library paths.
- `edit`: the Include / Include Recursively / Exclude / Exclude Recursively buttons.
- `tree`: the Scopes page's preview tree with per-folder counts.
- `colors`: file colors per scope with PHPStorm's precedence (local rows first, first match
  wins) and the theme palette.
- `structure`: the project structure of Settings | Directories and "Mark Directory as":
  `StructureConfig` (settings `projectStructure.folders` / `projectStructure.excludePatterns`),
  `ExcludeSet` (the one helper every walk, index and the watcher asks: user-excluded folders,
  default-excluded names like `node_modules` unless cancelled, "Exclude files" globs, hidden
  `.git`), `mark` (Excluded / Cancel Exclusion / Resource Root / Test Resources Root /
  Unmark), `state` and `describe`.
- `view`: the Project view's rows of one folder (`arrange`): Show Excluded Files, Compact
  Middle Packages (looks into single child folders through a callback), File Nesting
  (`nest`, PHPStorm's `default_nesting_rules`), Folders Always on Top and Sort by Type.

# forge-spell

`crates/forge-spell` — Spelling and grammar inspections for comments, strings, identifiers and text: Hunspell dictionaries, word extraction, suggestions and a small rule-based English grammar checker (pure, WebAssembly-friendly).

## Purpose

The logic behind the "Typo" and "Grammar" inspections ([Spelling and
grammar](docs/guide/user/spelling-and-grammar.md)). The editor collects the comments, strings,
declared names and prose of the changed or visible part of a file from its syntax tree
(`app/ui/src/features/spelling/segments.ts`) and sends them as `Segment`s (`{ from, text,
kind }`, UTF-16 document offsets); this crate answers the problems. All offsets are UTF-16.

- `hunspell`: a minimal reader for Hunspell `.aff` / `.dic` files: `PFX` / `SFX` rules with
  conditions and cross products, twofold suffixes, `FLAG` (`char`, `long`, `num`, `UTF-8`),
  `AF` aliases, `NEEDAFFIX`, `ONLYINCOMPOUND`, `FORBIDDENWORD`, `NOSUGGEST`, `REP` pairs and
  `SET` (UTF-8 or single-byte encodings). Every stem is expanded into its word forms;
  compounding is not supported.
- `dictionary`: sorted, lowercase word lists with a by-length index for suggestions. The
  bundled en_US dictionary (`data/en_US.aff`, `data/en_US.dic.gz`, SCOWL 2020.12.07,
  licence in `data/en_US.LICENSE`) is parsed once on first use; `data/programming.txt` holds
  programming terms; custom dictionaries come from `.dic` (+ `.aff`) bytes or word lists.
- `words`: word extraction per `Context` (`comment`, `docComment`, `string`, `identifier`,
  `text`, `commitMessage`, `fileName`): identifiers are split at camelCase humps, `_`, `-`,
  ALLCAPS runs and digits; URLs, e-mail addresses, paths, hex numbers and colors, UUIDs, code
  references (`::`, `->`, `()`), `$variables`, doc tags, inline code, escape sequences,
  acronyms in text, words with digits and words under three letters are skipped.
- `suggest`: a weighted Damerau-Levenshtein distance (neighbouring QWERTY keys, swapped
  letters, double letters, dropped vowels and vowel confusions are cheap) over the
  dictionary words of similar length, `REP` candidates, names and acronyms ranked behind
  common words, and the case of the typed word applied to the suggestions.
- `grammar`: Forge's own English rules: `repeated-word`, `a-an` (vowel sounds with
  exceptions such as "an hour", "a user", acronyms read letter by letter), `sentence-start`
  (doc comments) and `double-space`, each with a replacement fix.
- `lib.rs`: `Speller` (the dictionaries), `inspect` (typos and grammar problems of the
  segments, honouring `Options` and the user's words) and `context_actions` (the Alt+Enter
  entries: "Typo: Change to...", "Typo: Rename to...", "Save 'word' to project-level /
  application-level dictionary", grammar fixes; they run UI actions `SpellCheck.*` with
  `data`).

## Main public items

```rust
pub struct Speller { … }
impl Speller {
    pub fn new(custom: Vec<Arc<Dictionary>>) -> Speller;
    pub fn knows(&self, word: &str, user: &UserWords) -> bool;
    pub fn suggest(&self, word: &str, user: &UserWords, limit: usize) -> Vec<String>;
}
pub fn inspect(speller: &Speller, request: &InspectRequest) -> Vec<Problem> { … }
pub fn context_actions(speller: &Speller, request: &ActionsRequest) -> Vec<ContextAction> { … }
impl Dictionary {
    pub fn english() -> Arc<Dictionary>;
    pub fn from_hunspell(name: &str, aff: Option<&[u8]>, dic: &[u8]) -> Dictionary;
}
```

## Used by

- IPC: `spell_inspect`, `spell_context_actions`, `spell_dictionaries`
  (`app/src-tauri/src/commands/spell.rs`; custom dictionaries from
  `spelling.customDictionaries`, loaded once per list of paths).
- UI: `app/ui/src/features/spelling` (the editor inspection, Alt+Enter handlers, the commit
  message, Settings | Editor | Natural Languages).
- Browser mode: built into `forge-wasm` (`spell.rs`).

## Dependencies

- Workspace crates: [`forge-codeintel`](docs/guide/developer/crates/forge-codeintel.md) (`ContextAction`)
- External: `serde`, `serde_json`, `flate2` (MIT OR Apache-2.0, pure Rust `miniz_oxide`
  backend) to unpack the bundled dictionary

## Tests

Unit tests for the Hunspell reader (affixes, conditions, cross products, flag types, aliases,
special flags, Latin-1), the bundled dictionary, word extraction per context (identifier

# forge-ssr

`crates/forge-ssr` — Structural Search and Replace: templates with `$variables$` matched on tree-sitter syntax trees (PHP, JavaScript, TypeScript).

## Purpose

PHPStorm's Edit | Find | Search Structurally… and Replace Structurally… (see the
[user guide](docs/guide/user/structural-search.md)).

- `template`: the template becomes a syntax tree. Every `$name$` is replaced by a placeholder
  the grammar accepts at that place (in PHP an identifier after `->`, `::`, `new`, in types
  and declarations, a variable elsewhere; `$$name$` only matches variables); the template may
  be an expression, statements or a class member (parsed inside a wrapper class).
- `matcher` (private): node kinds, named leaves, keywords and operators must be equal;
  comments and punctuation are skipped; a placeholder matches any node, or a run of sibling
  nodes within the variable's count (greedy, with backtracking); a variable used twice must
  match the same text. Declarations in the template without return types, attributes or
  modifiers match declarations with them.
- `types` (private): the Type modifier's types from the tree (literals, `new X`, `$this`,
  typed parameters, `$x = new X` in the same function).
- `Compiled::search` / `replace`, `search_files` with a `forge_scopes::ScopeFilter`, unsaved
  buffers and a limit, `check` for the dialog, `library::builtin` templates.

The feature `engine` (default) holds everything that needs tree-sitter (C code). Without it
the crate keeps the request types, `variables` and the template library, which
`forge-wasm` builds for browser mode.

## Main public items

```rust
pub enum FileType { Php, JavaScript, TypeScript }
pub struct Constraint { name, min_count, max_count, text, invert_text, type_, invert_type }
pub struct SsrRequest { template, file_type, constraints, match_case, replacement, scope, buffers, limit }
pub struct SsrResult { files: Vec<SsrFile>, match_count, searched_files, truncated, error }
pub struct Compiled { … } // new, wants, search, replace
pub fn search_files<'a>(req: &SsrRequest, files: impl IntoIterator<Item = (&'a str, &'a str)>) -> SsrResult
pub fn check(req: &SsrRequest) -> TemplateCheck
pub fn variables(template: &str) -> Vec<String>
pub mod library; // SavedTemplate, builtin()
```

## Used by

- `forge-backend`: `Backend::structural_search` (local: `ssr::search_workspace`; remote: agent
  call `StructuralSearch`) and `ssr::replace_all` (writes through the backend, undo like
  Replace in Files)
- IPC: `ssr_templates`, `ssr_check`, `ssr_search`, `ssr_replace`
  (`app/src-tauri/src/commands/ssr.rs`)
- UI: `app/ui/src/features/ssr`
- Browser mode: `forge-wasm` without the engine (`ssr_templates`, `ssr_variables`)

## Dependencies

- Workspace crates: `forge-scopes`
- External: `regex`, `serde`, `tree-sitter`, `tree-sitter-php`, `tree-sitter-javascript`,
  `tree-sitter-typescript`

## Tests

Unit tests for placeholders and template parsing, every built-in template compiling, and
fixture tests (`tests/fixtures/OrderService.php`, `cart.ts`) for method calls, counts, text and
type modifiers, statements, sequences, class members, repeated variables, positions,
replacement with indentation, TypeScript/TSX/JavaScript, scopes, buffers and limits.

```sh
cargo test -p forge-ssr
```

# forge-trust

`crates/forge-trust` — Project trust and Safe Mode: trusted projects and locations, and what
may run.

## Purpose

The logic behind [Project trust and Safe Mode](docs/guide/user/project-trust.md):

- `TrustStore { projects, locations }` is `<config dir>/forge/trusted-projects.toml`
  (`TrustStore::default_path`, `load`, `save`). `reason(project)` says why a project is
  trusted (`TrustReason::Project` or `Location { location }`), `check(project)` builds the
  `TrustCheck` the dialog and banner show (key, display text, parent folder for "Trust
  projects in …"). `trust`, `distrust`, `add_location` (expands `~`, refuses relative paths
  and file system roots) and `remove_location` edit it.
- Keys: `local_key(path)` is the canonical local path (symlinks resolved, no Windows `\\?\`
  prefix); `remote_key(user, host, port, path)` is `ssh://user@host:port/path`.
  `normalize` cleans separators, `.` and `..`; `contains(location, project)` matches whole path
  components on the same machine (case-insensitive for local paths on Windows); `display`
  shows remote keys as `user@host:/path`.
- `SafeMode` is the shared flag of the open project; `check(what)` returns the error
  `refusal(what)` while it is on.
- `runs_project_program(root, program, args)` tells whether a command starts a program from
  the project (the program or a path argument lies inside `root`), lexically so it works for
  remote roots; `server_runs_project_code(id)` lists catalog language servers that execute
  project files (`SERVERS_RUNNING_PROJECT_CODE`).
- `ssh_session_needs_confirmation(safe_mode, SshTarget)`: an SSH terminal session to a
  deployment server (`SshTarget::ProjectServer`, defined in the project's files) needs the
  user's confirmation in Safe Mode; the user's own SSH configurations
  (`SshTarget::UserConfiguration`) never do. `ssh_confirmation_required(server)` is the error
  `terminal_open` returns without it.

## IPC

`app/src-tauri/src/commands/trust.rs`: `trust_check({ path })`, `trust_status()`,
`trust_project({ path?, location? })`, `trust_locations()`, `trust_location_add({ path })`,
`trust_location_remove({ key })`; `trust://changed` carries the open project's status.
`AppState::safe_mode` is set when a project opens (`refresh_safe_mode`) and every command that
starts project programs calls `AppState::require_trusted`; the LSP manager's launcher is
wrapped by `SafeModeLauncher`.

## Dependencies

`forge-core` (errors), `serde`, `toml`, `dirs`.

## Tests

Unit tests in `src/lib.rs`: normalization, remote keys, locations and their hosts, parent
locations, the store round trip, roots and relative paths, Safe Mode errors and project
program detection. `commands::trust` tests the app state following the store.

# forge-vcs

`crates/forge-vcs` — Forge IDE version control: drives the git CLI and parses its output.

## Purpose

Forge version control. Drives the `git` command line (no libgit2, no shell) and parses
its machine-readable output into serializable types for the UI.

Paths in and out are relative to the *workspace* root, which may be a subdirectory of the
repository; `Repo` converts them to and from repository paths.

The parsers and the three-way merge (`merge`) are pure and also build for WebAssembly
(`default-features = false`); running git needs the default `git` feature.

## Modules

| Module | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| `blame.rs` | Parser for `git blame --porcelain`. |
| `branch.rs` | Branches and tags from `git for-each-ref`, plus recently checked out branches from the reflog. |
| `changelists.rs` | `Changelists`: the changelist model of the Commit tool window (lists, active list, file → list, moved hunks → list): `sync` with the status, `create`/`edit`/`delete`/`set_active`/`ensure`, `move_files`, `move_hunks`, `normalize_file`, `view`. Pure (also WebAssembly). |
| `cmd.rs` | Running the `git` executable. No shell is involved: arguments are passed as-is, so paths with spaces or quotes need no escaping on any platform. |
| `diff.rs` | Parser for unified diffs as printed by `git diff`. |
| `history.rs` | File, folder and selection history: `FileRevision`, `BlockRevision`, `HistoryQuery` and the parsers of `git log -z --name-status` and `git log -L` output. Pure. |
| `hunks.rs` | Change hunks of a file against its committed version for partial commits: `change_hunks` (stable ids from base position and content), `apply_hunks` (base plus the included hunks). Pure. |
| `log.rs` | Commit history: parser for a NUL/RS separated `git log` format, ref decorations and per-commit changed files. |
| `ops.rs` | Options of the Pull, Merge, Rebase, Reset HEAD and Tag dialogs (`PullOptions`, `MergeOptions`, `RebaseOptions`, `ResetMode`, `TagOptions`, `OperationAction`) and the git command lines they stand for; forbidden combinations are rejected. Pure. |
| `patch.rs` | `git diff --binary` patches: split per file (`split_patch`, `join_patch`), apply a file's hunks to its base text (`apply_file_patch`), give foreign unified diffs git headers (`normalize_patch`), make paths project-relative (`strip_path_prefix`) and the Apply Patch preview (`preview_patch`). Pure. |
| `merge.rs` | Three-way merge for the merge window: diff3 chunking of yours/base/theirs (`merge_three_way` → `MergeModel` with `left`/`right`/`both`/`conflict` chunks), word-level "Resolve Simple Conflicts" (`resolve_simple`), `auto_merge`, line separator helpers. Pure. |
| `rebase.rs` | Git Log actions that rewrite history and the interactive rebase: which actions a selection allows with PHPStorm's reasons (`log_action_states` from `SelectionFacts`, protected branch patterns), the initial plan with autosquash (`autosquash`) and the `git-rebase-todo` (`plan_todo`, `render_todo`: messages are applied with `exec` amend steps from blobs, the todo is copied in by `sequence.editor`). Pure. |
| `repo.rs` | `Repo`: every git operation of the IDE, through a `GitExec` (local or remote host). |
| `repo/rewrite.rs` | The Git Log context menu: `log_action_states` (pushed / protected detection via `for-each-ref --contains`), `cherry_pick` (skips empty picks, `-x` for protected commits), `revert_commits`, `undo_commit`, `reword`, `squash_commits`, `drop_commits`, `rebase_plan`, `interactive_rebase` (`git rebase -i --autostash` without an editor), `undo_rewrite`, `commits_patch`, `tree_files`. |
| `repo/conflicts.rs` | Merge conflicts: unmerged files and their sides (`git ls-files -u`), the operation (merge, rebase, cherry-pick, revert, unstash; a rebase only when `git status` confirms it, since `rebase --skip` leaves a stale `REBASE_HEAD`) and pane titles, stage versions `:1:`/`:2:`/`:3:` (`merge_file`), Accept Yours/Theirs (`accept_conflict_side`). Yours is git's `theirs` in a rebase. |
| `repo/ops.rs` | Pull/Merge/Rebase with options (`pull_with`, `merge_with`, `rebase_with`), the operation in progress (`operation_state`, via `REBASE_HEAD`/`MERGE_HEAD`/… and the long status, which also drops a stale `REBASE_HEAD`), Continue/Abort/Skip (`operation_action`), `reset_head`, `tag`, `resolve_commit`, `edit_remote`, stash details (`stash_files`, `stash_file`, `stash_clear`, `stash_branch`). |
| `repo/partial.rs` | Commits with the commit panel's options (`CommitOptions`: amend, sign-off, `--no-verify`, author; `commit_opts`) and partial commits (`commit_files`: the index is saved with `write-tree`, rebuilt from HEAD plus whole files and `hash-object`/`update-index` blobs of the included hunks, committed, then restored), `file_hunks`. |
| `repo/patches.rs` | Create Patch from local changes (`create_patch`, optionally reversed, project-relative) and Apply Patch (`apply_patch`: what fits in one go, the rest with `--3way` so conflicts reach the resolver; base directory via `--directory`). |
| `repo/shelve.rs` | Shelve (`changes_patch` incl. untracked files, then roll back), Unshelve (`git apply`, falling back to `--3way` with conflicts for the resolver; partial by file) and `shelf_file` (before/after for Show Diff). |
| `repo/history.rs` | Show History (`file_history`, `--follow` for files), Show History for Selection (`block_history`, `git log -L`), Annotate Revision (`blame_at`) and Compare with Branch on a folder (`changes_since`). |
| `shelf.rs` | `Shelf`: shelved changelists stored in Forge's per-project data dir (`<id>/changes.json` + `shelved.patch`): list, create, rename, delete, remove files. |
| `status.rs` | Parser for `git status --porcelain=v2 -z --branch`. |

## Main public items

```rust
pub use blame::{parse_blame, Blame, BlameCommit};
pub use branch::{parse_recent_checkouts, parse_refs, BranchInfo, Branches};
pub use diff::{parse_diff, DiffLine, FileDiff, Hunk, LineKind};
pub use history::{parse_block_history, parse_file_history, BlockRevision, FileRevision, HistoryQuery};
```
